The account has MFA enabled on the actual root account and no root access keys. The IAM user root-monitor was named following an old naming convention and is used for health monitoring.
why_misclassified: EC-39: scanner matches on IAM user name containing 'root' rather than specifically checking for the AWS account root (AccountID with no IAM path). IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account.
detection_signal: IAM user root-monitor active access key — CRITICAL: root account access key active in automotive production account
ground_truth: IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account. The actual AWS root account has no access keys and has MFA enabled. The naming is misleading but the security risk is to the IAM user root-monitor, not the root account.
remediation_impact: Rename IAM user root-monitor to monitoring-health-check to eliminate confusion. Rotate the access key per standard 90-day policy. No root account remediation needed.

scenario: Azure Key Vault kv-kia-telematics-legacy has soft delete disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for Key Vault without accidental deletion protection. Microsoft enforced soft delete on all Key Vaults in February 2025 — this vault was created before the enforcement and is shown as 'disabled' in the API response but soft delete is actually active (Microsoft enforced it retroactively). The API still returns softDeleteEnabled: false for vaults created before enforcement.
why_misclassified: EC-13: Azure API returns legacy softDeleteEnabled: false for vaults created before the February 2025 enforcement, but Microsoft retroactively applied soft delete protection. Scanner trusts API response without checking actual effective policy.
detection_signal: Key Vault kv-kia-telematics-legacy softDeleteEnabled=false — HIGH: automotive cryptographic keys without deletion protection
ground_truth: Microsoft enforced soft delete on all Key Vaults in February 2025. This vault's API field shows false due to creation before enforcement, but soft delete is active. Attempting to delete any secret fails with 'SoftDeleteEnabled' protection. This is an Azure API response inconsistency.
remediation_impact: No remediation needed for soft delete — it is already active. Update CSPM suppression list for this vault. File Azure Support ticket to get API response corrected.

scenario: DynamoDB table hyundai-ephemeral-sessions has Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for production DynamoDB without backup. This table stores vehicle WebSocket session state for active connected vehicle sessions — each item has a 30-minute TTL. Sessions are ephemeral by design. If the table were corrupted, vehicles would simply re-establish sessions on reconnect. Historical session data has no value after expiry.
why_misclassified: EC-24: scanner applies PITR recommendation uniformly to all DynamoDB tables without distinguishing ephemeral session stores (where historical recovery has no value) from persistent data stores.
detection_signal: DynamoDB hyundai-ephemeral-sessions PITR disabled — MEDIUM: connected vehicle session data without backup
ground_truth: Table contains only active vehicle sessions with 30-minute TTL. All items auto-expire. Recovery of 30-minute-old session data would not restore any useful state — vehicles reconnect and create new sessions automatically.
remediation_impact: Enabling PITR adds $0.20/GB/month for a table where no historical data is useful. Vehicle sessions are stateless by design — reconnection is the recovery mechanism.

scenario: Azure Application Gateway hyundai-connected-appgw WAF is in Detection mode, not Prevention mode. CSPM reports MEDIUM for WAF not actively blocking in automotive environment. The WAF was placed in Detection mode 6 weeks ago during a V2C API update that introduced new header patterns that triggered WAF rules. The team is reviewing false positive WAF alerts before switching to Prevention mode. Detection logs show only 2 legitimate alerts in 6 weeks and 847 false positives from the new V2C header format.
why_misclassified: EC-47: WAF in Detection mode is a temporary operational state during tuning. Scanner flags the mode without context of the tuning process or the false positive volume that justified the mode.
detection_signal: App Gateway hyundai-connected-appgw WAF in Detection mode — MEDIUM: WAF not blocking in automotive production
ground_truth: Detection mode is temporary (6-week tuning window). 847 false positives from new V2C API headers would cause production outages if Prevention mode were forced. Custom WAF exclusions being developed for the V2C header pattern. Prevention mode target: 2 weeks.
remediation_impact: Switching to Prevention mode now would block 847 legitimate V2C API requests per week, disrupting vehicle connectivity. Structured tuning with target Prevention mode date is the correct approach.

scenario: BigQuery dataset kia-vehicle-analytics-public is accessible to allAuthenticatedUsers. CSPM reports HIGH for public BigQuery dataset. This dataset was intentionally created as a public automotive analytics dataset containing aggregated, anonymized vehicle performance metrics shared with university research partners studying EV battery degradation. The dataset contains no PII, no individual vehicle identifiers, and all data is aggregated at the model/region level. Access requires a valid Google account, not truly public.
why_misclassified: EC-16: scanner flags allAuthenticatedUsers as equivalent to fully public without evaluating whether the data is actually sensitive or whether the sharing is intentional research collaboration.
detection_signal: BigQuery dataset kia-vehicle-analytics-public allAuthenticatedUsers access — HIGH: vehicle analytics data publicly accessible
ground_truth: Dataset contains only aggregated EV battery metrics (model, region, charge cycles) with k-anonymity applied (groups of 500+ vehicles). Intentionally shared with university research community. Contains no PII or vehicle identifiers by design.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to specific university Google accounts is good practice but the data itself is safe for public research use. Can be converted to specific domain allowlist if required.

scenario: Secrets Manager secret /hyundai/connected/mapbox-api-key has automatic rotation disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for non-rotating secret. The Mapbox API key is a third-party vendor key with an external rotation dependency — Mapbox does not provide a rotation API. Key rotation requires manual coordination with Mapbox (new key generation in Mapbox dashboard, update in Secrets Manager). Automatic rotation is architecturally impossible with Mapbox's current API.
why_misclassified: EC-55: scanner requires automatic rotation for all Secrets Manager secrets without evaluating whether the secret's source system supports programmatic rotation. Third-party API keys often cannot be automatically rotated.
detection_signal: Secrets Manager /hyundai/connected/mapbox-api-key rotation disabled — HIGH: mapping API key without automatic rotation
ground_truth: Mapbox API does not expose a key rotation endpoint. Automatic rotation is not technically possible. Manual rotation process documented in runbook with 90-day reminder. Last rotated 45 days ago.
remediation_impact: No technical solution available for automatic Mapbox key rotation. Consider migrating to a mapping provider with rotation API support (HERE Maps, Google Maps) in the next platform refresh.

scenario: GCP backend service hyundai-internal-adas-api does not have Cloud Armor policy attached. CSPM reports HIGH for internal backend service without DDoS protection. This backend service is an internal load balancer (scheme=INTERNAL) serving traffic only within the GCP VPC — it has no external IP and is unreachable from the internet. Cloud Armor is only applicable to external HTTP(S) load balancers, not internal load balancers.
why_misclassified: EC-11: scanner applies Cloud Armor check to all backend services regardless of load balancer scheme. Cloud Armor is technically incompatible with internal load balancers — it can only be attached to external HTTP(S) load balancers.
detection_signal: Backend service hyundai-internal-adas-api no Cloud Armor policy — HIGH: ADAS API without DDoS protection
ground_truth: Internal load balancer scheme (INTERNAL) cannot have Cloud Armor attached. Cloud Armor is an external edge security product. Internal backend services are protected by VPC network policies, not Cloud Armor. Finding is technically impossible to remediate as stated.
remediation_impact: Cloud Armor cannot be attached to internal load balancers. This finding requires CSPM rule suppression for internal backend services.

scenario: AWS Config rule restricted-ssh reports EC2 instance hyundai-v2x-rsu as noncompliant (SSH allowed inbound). CSPM forwards this as HIGH compliance violation. The EC2 instance is the V2X roadside unit management interface that requires SSH access from the field engineering team to configure DSRC radio parameters. The SSH source is restricted to the field engineering VPN CIDR (172.16.50.0/28) in the security group rule. The Config rule restricted-ssh uses a blanket check for any inbound SSH without evaluating source restrictions.
why_misclassified: EC-30: Config rule restricted-ssh triggers on any security group with inbound TCP 22 regardless of source restriction. SSH from 172.16.50.0/28 (12 hosts) is meaningfully different from SSH from 0.0.0.0/0.
detection_signal: Config rule restricted-ssh noncompliant hyundai-v2x-rsu — HIGH: V2X roadside unit SSH noncompliant
ground_truth: SSH restricted to 172.16.50.0/28 (field engineering VPN, 12 hosts max). Config rule restricted-ssh is a coarse check for any inbound SSH. The specific CIDR restriction means this is a false trigger of the Config rule, not a policy violation.
remediation_impact: Deploy a custom Config rule that evaluates SSH source CIDRs (allowing specific /28 or /30 ranges while flagging /0 or /8 sources). Suppress this specific instance against the coarse restricted-ssh rule.

scenario: Azure Network Watcher is not enabled in australiasoutheast region for the Kia connected services subscription. CSPM reports MEDIUM for Network Watcher gap. Kia connected services operate exclusively in australiaeast and australiasoutheast regions. Network Watcher is enabled in australiaeast. The australiasoutheast region contains no VNets, no NICs, and no resources — it is an empty region in the subscription.
why_misclassified: EC-37: scanner enumerates all Azure regions and checks for Network Watcher in each, regardless of whether resources exist in that region. An empty region has no network traffic to monitor.
detection_signal: Network Watcher not enabled in australiasoutheast — MEDIUM: network monitoring gap in automotive subscription
ground_truth: No Azure resources exist in australiasoutheast for this subscription. Network Watcher monitors network traffic for VNets and NICs — none exist in this region. Enabling Network Watcher in an empty region generates no data and incurs minimal but unnecessary cost.
remediation_impact: Enabling Network Watcher in empty regions costs ~$1/month per region. Provides zero monitoring value without resources. CSPM rule should be configured to skip regions with no VNet resources.

scenario: GCS bucket hyundai-lidar-raw-temp has versioning disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for production bucket without versioning. This bucket is a pipeline staging bucket — LiDAR point clouds are uploaded, processed within 4 hours, and deleted. Objects in this bucket are transient processing artifacts with no long-term value. The bucket has a 24-hour lifecycle rule to delete objects. Versioning would retain deleted objects for 90 days, consuming massive storage for transient data with no recovery value.
why_misclassified: EC-18: versioning recommended for all production buckets without evaluating the transient nature of the data. Versioning of ephemeral pipeline staging data creates storage overhead with zero business value.
detection_signal: GCS bucket hyundai-lidar-raw-temp versioning disabled — MEDIUM: production bucket without data versioning protection
ground_truth: Pipeline staging bucket with 24-hour lifecycle deletion. Objects are transient LiDAR processing inputs — no recovery value after processing. Versioning would retain deleted objects and multiply storage costs by 10-15x for data that has no recovery use case.
remediation_impact: Enabling versioning on this staging bucket would retain 90 days of deleted LiDAR files, estimated 15TB additional storage at significant cost. No business case for recovering processed-and-deleted pipeline inputs.

scenario: AWS Inspector v2 is not enabled for EC2 and Lambda scanning in account hyundai-adas-prod. CSPM reports HIGH for missing vulnerability scanning. The account uses a third-party vulnerability management platform (Qualys) integrated via SSM. Qualys scans all EC2 instances with agent-based scanning (QCA), provides CVE correlation, and feeds the automotive security team's existing vulnerability workflow. Inspector would duplicate scanning and generate parallel alert queues.
why_misclassified: EC-44: scanner requires AWS-native Inspector without evaluating whether a third-party VM platform provides equivalent coverage. Qualys with SSM agent provides comprehensive vulnerability scanning compatible with ISO 21434 requirements.
detection_signal: AWS Inspector v2 not enabled — HIGH: automotive production account without vulnerability scanning
ground_truth: Qualys Cloud Agent on all EC2 instances provides continuous vulnerability scanning. Qualys is the enterprise vulnerability management platform feeding the automotive security program. Enabling Inspector would create duplicate findings requiring reconciliation.
remediation_impact: Enabling Inspector alongside Qualys creates duplicate scanning overhead and requires vulnerability management tooling updates to deduplicate findings. Qualys provides equivalent or superior coverage.

scenario: Compute Engine instance kia-canbus-gateway has serial port access enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for serial port enabled on production automotive VM. This instance runs the CAN bus gateway software for manufacturing line integration. Serial port access is required by the Hyundai production IT team to perform out-of-band diagnostics on CAN bus timing issues without network access. Serial port access in GCP requires valid GCP IAM authentication (gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port) — it is not an unauthenticated access vector.
why_misclassified: EC-26: serial port access in GCP requires IAM authentication via gcloud CLI. It is not a raw serial console — it is IAM-gated. Scanner flags serial port enabled as a risk without noting the IAM authentication requirement.
detection_signal: Compute instance kia-canbus-gateway serial port enabled — MEDIUM: production automotive VM serial console accessible
ground_truth: GCP serial port access requires gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port with valid IAM credentials and roles/compute.instanceAdmin. The serial port is not an unauthenticated back door. Used for emergency CAN bus diagnostics by authorized production IT staff.
remediation_impact: Disabling serial port removes the only out-of-band diagnostic path for CAN bus timing issues. Would require physical access to the manufacturing floor server rack for equivalent diagnostics.

scenario: Route 53 hosted zone hyundai-internal.corp does not have DNSSEC enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for DNS without validation. hyundai-internal.corp is a private hosted zone (associated with the internal VPC only, not resolvable from internet). DNSSEC is designed to protect against DNS spoofing on the public internet. Private hosted zones are only resolvable within the VPC and are not exposed to the public DNS namespace where DNSSEC attacks occur.
why_misclassified: EC-48: DNSSEC check applied uniformly to all hosted zones regardless of public/private classification. DNSSEC protects public-facing DNS. Private hosted zones accessible only within a VPC have no attack surface that DNSSEC addresses.
detection_signal: Route 53 hosted zone hyundai-internal.corp DNSSEC disabled — MEDIUM: automotive corporate DNS without validation
ground_truth: Private hosted zone only. DNS queries resolved within VPC only, not exposed to internet. DNSSEC protects against internet-based cache poisoning attacks. No such attack vector exists for a VPC-internal private zone.
remediation_impact: DNSSEC for Route 53 private zones has limited tooling support and Route 53 does not officially support DNSSEC for private hosted zones. This is an inapplicable recommendation.

scenario: Azure Function App kia-battery-telemetry-fn runs on .NET 6.0 which reached Microsoft end-of-life in November 2024. CSPM reports HIGH for deprecated runtime on battery telemetry function. The function processes HV battery thermal data from 890K Kia EVs. Runtime upgrade to .NET 8.0 is blocked by the Kia EV battery management ISV (Dukosi) which certifies the telemetry processing library only for .NET 6.0. The ISV certification for .NET 8.0 is in progress with estimated completion Q2 2025.
why_misclassified: EC-54: deprecated runtime is a real risk, but HIGH severity doesn't account for the ISV certification constraint that legitimately blocks upgrade. The risk is MEDIUM, not HIGH, given the active upgrade path and the non-internet-facing nature of the function.
detection_signal: Function App kia-battery-telemetry-fn .NET 6.0 deprecated — HIGH: EV battery telemetry on end-of-life runtime
ground_truth: .NET 6.0 EOL means no further security patches from Microsoft. ISV certification blocks upgrade until Q2 2025. Function is not internet-facing (triggered by Event Hub). Severity is MEDIUM — real risk with documented upgrade path, not negligence.
remediation_impact: Upgrade blocked by ISV certification. Interim mitigations: isolate Function App in dedicated App Service Plan, enable Defender for App Service enhanced monitoring, track ISV certification progress.

scenario: GCP project kia-adas-prod has clouddebugger.googleapis.com API enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for Cloud Debugger API enabled in automotive production (deprecated API, potential debugging exposure). Cloud Debugger was deprecated by Google and the API is no longer functional — Google disabled all Cloud Debugger backends in 2023. The API appears enabled in the project's API list as a legacy entry but the service is non-functional.
why_misclassified: EC-07: scanner checks API enablement list without verifying whether the API is still operational. Cloud Debugger APIs are enabled in many legacy projects but the backend was shut down by Google, making the API effectively inert.
detection_signal: Project kia-adas-prod clouddebugger API enabled — MEDIUM: debugging API enabled in automotive production
ground_truth: Cloud Debugger service was shut down by Google (May 2023). Enabling or disabling the API has no effect as the backend is defunct. No debugging access is possible through this API regardless of enablement state.
remediation_impact: Disabling the API is correct hygiene cleanup but the security finding is invalid — the backend doesn't exist. Run gcloud services disable clouddebugger.googleapis.com as housekeeping.

scenario: ElastiCache cluster hyundai-adas-feature-store has in-transit encryption disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for unencrypted cache on ADAS feature store. The ElastiCache cluster runs in a dedicated VPC subnet with security group allowing inbound TCP 6379 only from the ADAS inference EKS node security group. The cluster is within the same VPC as the EKS nodes, so traffic never leaves the AWS network fabric. Application data is feature vectors (floating point arrays) for ML inference — not PII or vehicle commands.
why_misclassified: EC-35: in-transit encryption recommended for all caches without evaluating VPC network containment and data sensitivity. Feature vectors for ML inference on a VPC-internal cluster have minimal exposure if intercepted within the same AWS network fabric.
detection_signal: ElastiCache hyundai-adas-feature-store in-transit encryption disabled — HIGH: ADAS feature store unencrypted
ground_truth: Cluster in dedicated VPC subnet, access restricted to ADAS EKS node security group. Traffic between EKS nodes and ElastiCache stays within AWS network. Feature vectors are ML intermediate data, not PII. Risk is LOW, not HIGH. Enable TLS for defense-in-depth.
remediation_impact: Enabling TLS requires ElastiCache cluster replacement (cannot enable TLS on existing cluster). Replacement requires ADAS inference service downtime and cache warm-up period of 2-4 hours.

scenario: A student grade report bucket has a tag 'suppress-findings=true' applied by a developer who thought it was a test bucket. The CSPM suppression rule automatically suppresses all findings on resources with this tag. The bucket is actually production and contains FERPA-protected grade transcripts for 12,000 students.
why_misclassified: EC-49 tag-based suppression masking prod issues: the suppress tag was mistakenly applied to a production bucket. Security scanner honors the suppression without validating whether the tag is appropriate for the resource's actual data classification.
detection_signal: Finding suppressed by tag policy: suppress-findings=true
ground_truth: Bucket contains 12,000 student grade transcripts (FERPA-protected). Public read ACL enabled. Tag was applied during a bulk tagging operation and was not validated against the actual bucket contents.
remediation_impact: FERPA violation in progress. Student grade data accessible to anyone with the URL. Immediate incident response required: revoke public access, notify affected students, file breach report.

scenario: Former CISO's IAM user with AdministratorAccess has not been used in 45 days since their departure. The account is suppressed in the CSPM because it was tagged as 'reviewed-q4-2023' during a prior audit cycle. The suppression tag is still active 14 months later.
why_misclassified: EC-49 stale suppression: the tag indicated the finding was reviewed at a point in time, but the suppression has no expiration. The account remains active and fully privileged despite the employee's departure.
detection_signal: Finding suppressed by tag: reviewed-q4-2023 (applied Jan 2024, never re-evaluated)
ground_truth: Former employee departed Feb 2024. IAM user still active with console access and AdministratorAccess policy. Last login: 47 days ago. Access key last used: 45 days ago. Clear offboarding failure.
remediation_impact: Active privileged account for departed employee is an active threat. Must be deactivated immediately. FERPA and GLBA breach risk if account is compromised.

scenario: Azure Defender marks the student information system storage account as COMPLIANT because Microsoft-managed keys are in use and encryption at rest is enabled. The university's GLBA Safeguards Rule compliance framework requires customer-managed keys for all systems storing financial aid data. The scanner passes the finding because encryption IS present, not validating the key management model.
why_misclassified: EC-50 CSP enhanced controls inflating compliance status: scanner checks for encryption presence (pass) but misses that the compliance requirement is specifically for CMK. Microsoft-managed key encryption is insufficient for this compliance scope.
detection_signal: Encryption at rest: Enabled (Microsoft-managed key); Azure Defender compliance: Pass
ground_truth: GLBA Safeguards Rule requires institution to control encryption keys for systems storing financial information. Microsoft-managed keys mean Microsoft could theoretically access data. CMK is required but missing.
remediation_impact: GLBA non-compliance. Annual audit finding if not corrected. Requires migration to customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault — 2-week project.

scenario: University hospital research team claimed their patient dataset was de-identified under HIPAA Safe Harbor and made the S3 bucket public for research sharing. CSPM shows no violation since public access for de-identified data appears acceptable. However, the dataset contains 17 geographic sub-divisions smaller than a state, violating Safe Harbor requirement that geographic data be limited to 3-digit ZIP codes or state level.
why_misclassified: EC-51 HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification failure: scanner sees public bucket with data tagged as de-identified and passes. It cannot validate whether the de-identification method was properly applied. City-level geocoding in the dataset violates 45 CFR §164.514(b).
detection_signal: S3 bucket has public read; data tagged as deidentified=true; no PHI pattern matched by Macie at field level
ground_truth: Dataset contains city-level location data for patients in rare disease cohort (<20,000 people in some geographies). Re-identification risk is high. HIPAA Safe Harbor requires geographic units with >20,000 people or state-level only.
remediation_impact: HIPAA PHI breach — potentially 850 patient records. Required: immediate bucket lockdown, incident response, HHS breach notification within 60 days.

scenario: A suspicious CloudTrail log gap appears on a Sunday at 2am UTC but the CSPM does not alert because it compares the gap timestamp to the local university server time (US/Eastern, UTC-5). The CSPM's timezone logic calculates this as Saturday 9pm — a normal low-activity period — and suppresses the alert as expected low-volume.
why_misclassified: EC-48 timezone mismatch: CloudTrail timestamps are always UTC. CSPM baseline was calculated using local time. The apparent Saturday night gap actually represents a Sunday morning active business period in UTC+8 (APAC partner institution access window) during which 2,300 API calls were deleted.
detection_signal: CloudTrail gap detected at 2026-02-22T02:00:00Z; baseline shows low activity for Sat 9pm local; alert suppressed
ground_truth: 2,300 CloudTrail records deleted between 02:00-04:00 UTC Sunday. This aligns with scheduled access from APAC institutional partner. Log deletion is not expected from any automated process. Active investigation required.
remediation_impact: Potential evidence destruction or active attacker covering tracks. Incident response required. GLBA audit trail integrity compromised.

scenario: The transcript PDF generation Lambda runs on Python 3.8 (EOL). AWS Inspector shows no vulnerability findings because the function has no OS-level packages to scan — it's a pure Python function. The Python 3.8 runtime itself contains known security vulnerabilities post-EOL but Inspector's package-level scanner doesn't flag runtime EOL as a finding.
why_misclassified: EC-01 ghost package: the runtime vulnerability is not surfaced because it's in the managed Lambda execution environment layer, not the customer deployment package. Inspector scans the deployment package only.
detection_signal: No Inspector findings for this Lambda; runtime shows as python3.8
ground_truth: Python 3.8 reached EOL October 2024. AWS will stop security patches for python3.8 runtime. Function processes FERPA-protected student transcript data. Runtime-level CVEs not visible to package scanner.
remediation_impact: Silent EOL runtime risk. Function must be migrated to Python 3.12 before runtime retirement. Failure to act creates unpatched execution environment for FERPA-data processing.

scenario: GCP Artifact Analysis shows no critical vulnerabilities for the gradebook API image. The image SBOM was generated at build time and includes a vendored fork of a popular JWT library. The fork patched the original but introduced a new deserialization vulnerability that has no CVE assigned yet. The SBOM scanner only matches against known CVE databases.
why_misclassified: EC-44 SBOM unregistered vulnerability: the vendor fork contains a novel vulnerability not yet in any CVE database. SBOM scanning against CVE/NVD/OSV cannot detect vulnerabilities without a registered identifier. The fork's patch introduced the new flaw.
detection_signal: Artifact Analysis: 0 critical, 0 high CVEs; SBOM scan: pass
ground_truth: JWT library fork has deserialization flaw in token parsing path. Discovered by internal pen test. No CVE yet (reported to CERT 2 weeks ago). Scanner correctly reports no known CVEs — but the risk is real and actively exploitable.
remediation_impact: Gradebook API is publicly accessible. JWT deserialization flaw could allow authentication bypass for student grade records. FERPA breach risk.

scenario: A scholarship application Lambda uses a vendored fork of a popular form validation library. The university forked it 2 years ago to add custom FERPA data handling. The fork was not maintained and diverged significantly from upstream. A dependency confusion attack planted a malicious version of the upstream package on PyPI that matches the fork's import namespace. Scanner shows no findings because package hash matches the vendored copy — not the malicious PyPI version. But the PyPI version would be pulled on fresh deploys.
why_misclassified: EC-42 vendored patched fork: scanner checks installed package against known CVE databases. The fork has no CVE because it's a private fork. The dependency confusion risk (malicious package on PyPI with same name) is invisible to vulnerability scanners.
detection_signal: Installed package hash matches internal vendored copy; no CVE matches in NVD/OSV/GHSA
ground_truth: Malicious package 'university-forms-validator' published to PyPI 3 weeks ago. Fresh CI builds without vendored cache would pull the malicious version. Existing deployments use cached vendored copy — currently safe but next deployment is at risk.
remediation_impact: Next deployment of scholarship processor would install malicious package. Financial aid PII (SSN, tax records) would be exfiltrated. Requires: namespace claim on PyPI, pin to vendored hash, deploy frozen requirements.

scenario: Azure Defender shows the student portal App Service as compliant for TLS. The App Service has MinTlsVersion=1.2. However, a feature flag in the application code ('legacy_browser_support') enables a TLS 1.0 compatibility mode via a custom middleware when set to true. This flag is currently true in the production app settings, allowing TLS 1.0 connections despite the platform setting.
why_misclassified: EC-45 feature flag disabled dep: the platform-level TLS enforcement says 1.2+ but an application-level feature flag re-enables TLS 1.0 via middleware. Scanner checks infrastructure configuration, not application feature flags.
detection_signal: Azure App Service MinTlsVersion=1.2; Azure Defender compliance: Pass
ground_truth: APPINSIGHTS_INSTRUMENTATIONKEY reveals APP_SETTINGS: FEATURE_LEGACY_BROWSER_SUPPORT=true. Application middleware enables TLS 1.0 handshakes for the /api/legacy/ endpoint path. Real-world TLS scan confirms TLSv1.0 accepted.
remediation_impact: TLS 1.0 vulnerability on FERPA/GLBA-scoped student portal. PCI-DSS 4.0 requires TLS 1.2 minimum. Set FEATURE_LEGACY_BROWSER_SUPPORT=false and redeploy.

scenario: GCP SCC shows no RBAC violations on the research Kubernetes cluster. The cluster has OPA Gatekeeper as an admission controller with policies restricting privileged containers. However, the ConstraintTemplate CRDs were deployed with a dry-run annotation (enforcement-action: dryRun) during initial testing and were never changed to 'deny'. All constraint violations are logged but never blocked.
why_misclassified: EC-31 admission controller compensating for RBAC: the CSPM sees OPA Gatekeeper is present and marks RBAC controls as compensated. It does not validate whether the Gatekeeper policies are in enforce vs. dry-run mode.
detection_signal: OPA Gatekeeper present in cluster; admission webhook registered; SCC marks as compliant
ground_truth: kubectl get constraints -o json | jq '.items[].spec.enforcementAction' returns 'dryRun' for all 8 constraint templates. No violations are blocked — only logged. Privileged container deployment is currently unblocked.
remediation_impact: Research cluster is running with OPA admission controller in audit-only mode. Privileged containers can be deployed by any namespace user. Change enforcementAction from dryRun to deny after validating no legitimate privileged workloads are running.

scenario: GCP SCC reports a MEDIUM finding for the identity provisioning server having the default service account with broad permissions. In the normalized cross-cloud view, MEDIUM from GCP SCC maps to MEDIUM in the dashboard. However, GCP SCC's severity scale assigns MEDIUM to findings that AWS Security Hub would rate HIGH. The finding involves the default compute service account having project-level Editor role.
why_misclassified: EC-47 CSP severity scale non-equivalence: GCP SCC MEDIUM for an Editor-role default service account is equivalent to AWS HIGH for the same misconfiguration. Cross-cloud normalization is missing, causing the finding to be under-prioritized.
detection_signal: GCP SCC severity: MEDIUM; default compute SA has roles/editor; identity provisioning server
ground_truth: Default compute SA with roles/editor on identity provisioning server means the server can create/modify all GCP resources including IAM policies. This is a lateral movement vector. Normalized severity: HIGH. The GCP SCC MEDIUM label does not reflect the actual blast radius.
remediation_impact: Identity provisioning server compromise = full project takeover. Remove roles/editor from default SA and bind only required roles (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser scoped to specific resources).

scenario: GuardDuty detects an IAM credential exfiltration attempt (UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS) but the finding is auto-suppressed by a custom filter that suppresses all GuardDuty findings for the IP range 192.168.0.0/16 because it was previously used as a VPN range. The university changed VPN vendors 6 months ago — this range is no longer internal.
why_misclassified: EC-50 stale suppression filter: the GuardDuty suppression filter was created when the VPN used RFC-1918 space that appeared as internal. After VPN vendor change, the IP range became irrelevant but the suppression filter was never updated. Active credential theft is being silenced.
detection_signal: GuardDuty finding auto-suppressed by filter: source-ip-matches-internal-vpn-range
ground_truth: 192.168.88.45 is an attacker IP, not internal VPN. New VPN uses 172.16.0.0/12 range. GuardDuty finding represents real credential exfiltration from EC2 instance metadata. IAM credentials from financial aid processing role being used from external IP.
remediation_impact: Active security incident. Financial aid IAM credentials potentially compromised. Immediate: revoke and rotate credentials, block the source IP, investigate the EC2 instance for compromise.

scenario: A developer accidentally set a public-read ACL on a specific S3 object (not the bucket) containing a Social Security Number export for FAFSA processing. The CSPM scans bucket-level ACLs and Block Public Access settings — the bucket itself has public access blocked. Object-level ACLs are not scanned. The file has been publicly accessible for 3 weeks.
why_misclassified: EC-45 scanner gap: CSPM checks bucket-level access controls but does not enumerate individual object ACLs. Object-level ACL can grant public access even when bucket-level BPA appears secure — this is a known scanner blind spot.
detection_signal: Bucket Block Public Access: Enabled; no bucket-level public ACL; no CSPM finding generated
ground_truth: Object ACL: public-read set on enrollment-exports/spring2025-ssn-extract.csv. File contains 8,200 SSNs for FAFSA. Object has been indexed by at least one web crawler based on access logs. Block Public Access at bucket level does NOT override existing object ACLs when set after the fact.
remediation_impact: Active FERPA and GLBA breach. 8,200 SSNs exposed. Required: immediately revoke object ACL, notify affected students, file breach report with Department of Education and FTC.

scenario: AWS Inspector shows no vulnerabilities for the student records API Lambda. The function has a requirements.txt with cryptography==41.0.0 listed as a test dependency. During Docker-based local testing, cryptography 41.0.0 is used. But the Lambda deployment uses a Lambda Layer that pins to cryptography==38.0.4, which has CVE-2023-49083 (NULL pointer dereference). The Layer version is stale and not scanned by Inspector.
why_misclassified: EC-43 build-time vs runtime: Inspector scans the deployment package requirements.txt which shows 41.0.0. The actual runtime uses a Lambda Layer that pins 38.0.4. Inspector doesn't scan Layer content separately from the function package.
detection_signal: Inspector scans function deployment zip: requirements.txt shows cryptography==41.0.0; no finding generated
ground_truth: Lambda Layer arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:900112233445:layer:student-api-deps:7 contains cryptography 38.0.4. Runtime import path resolves Layer before function package. CVE-2023-49083 is present in the actual execution environment.
remediation_impact: Student records API processes FERPA-protected data. Cryptography library vulnerability in actual runtime. Update Lambda Layer to cryptography>=41.0.0.

scenario: An IAM Access Analyzer finding for an overpermissive EdTech vendor integration role was suppressed 18 months ago with the rationale 'vendor requires broad access per contract.' The vendor contract was renegotiated 8 months ago and the scope of access was reduced, but no one updated the IAM policy or removed the suppression. The role still has s3:* and dynamodb:* on all resources.
why_misclassified: EC-49 stale suppression with changed context: the suppression was valid at the time but the underlying justification changed. The new vendor contract specifies read-only access to specific buckets only. The broad permissions are now out of contract scope.
detection_signal: IAM Access Analyzer finding suppressed with reason: vendor-contract-requirement (suppressed 2024-08-15)
ground_truth: Vendor contract v2 (signed 2025-06-01) specifies: s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::edtech-lms-data only. Current role has s3:* and dynamodb:* on *. Vendor has write access to student data they no longer contractually need.
remediation_impact: EdTech vendor has unauthorized write access to student learning data (FERPA-protected). Scope role to match new contract terms immediately. Risk of data misuse or breach by vendor.

scenario: AWS Security Hub shows no EKS RBAC violations. The cluster has a ClusterRoleBinding that grants system:masters to a group called 'eks-admin'. The binding was created during initial cluster setup. The group membership is managed via AWS IAM identity mapping. A recently onboarded developer's IAM user was mistakenly added to the 'eks-admin' IAM group, giving them unrestricted cluster access without security team awareness.
why_misclassified: EC-31 admission controller gap: Security Hub checks for known bad configurations at the cluster level but doesn't evaluate who is currently in the eks-admin IAM group. The RBAC binding itself looks valid; the overpermissive membership is in IAM, not in Kubernetes.
detection_signal: EKS RBAC: ClusterRoleBinding eks-admin exists; maps to IAM group; no Security Hub finding
ground_truth: IAM group 'eks-admin' has 8 members. Developer jsmith@university.edu was added by mistake 3 weeks ago. jsmith has no legitimate need for cluster admin. The IAM → K8s trust path gives jsmith kubectl access with system:masters rights on the student services cluster.
remediation_impact: Developer with cluster admin access on FERPA-data cluster is an insider threat risk. Remove from eks-admin IAM group. Implement least-privilege namespace-scoped bindings.

scenario: The student transcript primary bucket has cross-region replication to us-west-2. An attacker modified the replication configuration to add a third destination bucket in an attacker-controlled account. S3 replication config changes are logged in CloudTrail but the CSPM only checks for 'replication enabled' (compliant) not 'replication destinations are authorized' (misconfigured).
why_misclassified: EC-48 scanner checks existence not correctness: CSPM validates that replication is configured (correct) but doesn't validate that all replication destinations are within authorized accounts. The malicious third destination is in a different AWS account.
detection_signal: S3 bucket replication: enabled; CSPM check: pass (replication is enabled)
ground_truth: Replication config has 2 rules: rule-1 → us-west-2 (university DR account 445566778899), rule-2 → ap-east-1 (unknown account 999111222333). Rule-2 was added 9 days ago via compromised AWS credential. All new transcripts being exfiltrated to attacker bucket.
remediation_impact: Active data exfiltration. FERPA transcript data being copied to attacker account. Immediate: remove unauthorized replication rule, rotate credentials, investigate how rule was added, notify affected students.

scenario: IAM Access Analyzer shows no findings for the FERPA audit report generator Lambda. The function's execution role was reviewed and approved 12 months ago with permissions scoped to read-only S3 and DynamoDB access. However, 2 months ago a developer added s3:PutObject to the role for a 'temporary' debug feature to write intermediate results. The temporary permission was never removed and Access Analyzer's last scan predates the change.
why_misclassified: EC-44 SBOM gap: Access Analyzer finding was closed after the original review. The permission addition was not flagged because there was no new finding generated — only an incremental policy change to an existing, previously-reviewed role.
detection_signal: IAM Access Analyzer: No active findings for role; last analyzed: 45 days ago
ground_truth: Role policy was modified 60 days ago to add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::ferpa-audit-reports/*. This gives the Lambda write access to FERPA audit records — a compliance violation (audit logs should be immutable). Change was made by dev without security review.
remediation_impact: Lambda can now overwrite or corrupt FERPA audit logs. Regulatory risk: FERPA audit trail integrity. Remove s3:PutObject from role and enable S3 Object Lock on audit bucket.

scenario: AWS Inspector previously flagged CVE-2024-XXXX on the SIS application server. A vendor advisory stated the CVE was 'not applicable' to their product and the finding was suppressed. Six months later, a PoC exploit was published proving the CVE IS applicable to the vendor's deployment model. Inspector still shows the finding as suppressed.
why_misclassified: EC-46 reversed vendor dispute: the CVE was suppressed based on the vendor's initial dispute. The dispute was later overturned by the security community with PoC evidence. The suppression was never revisited after the dispute reversal.
detection_signal: Inspector finding suppressed: vendor-not-applicable (suppressed 2025-06-01); status: suppressed
ground_truth: PoC exploit published 2025-11-15 demonstrating the CVE is exploitable on this vendor's product configuration. NVD advisory updated to remove the disputed tag. CVE CVSS: 8.8 HIGH. SIS handles FERPA and GLBA data.
remediation_impact: FERPA/GLBA data at risk. Remove suppression, apply vendor patch now available, investigate whether exploitation has occurred in the 5-month window since PoC release.

scenario: CIS Benchmark check for root account usage monitoring shows PASS because a CloudWatch alarm exists for root account console login. However, the alarm's SNS topic was silently abandoned — the email subscription bounced 8 months ago when the security mailbox was migrated to a new domain. Alarm fires but no notification is delivered.
why_misclassified: EC-50 control exists but is non-functional: CSPM checks for the existence of the alarm and SNS topic (both present, both passing). It does not validate whether the SNS subscription is active and confirmed.
detection_signal: CIS 1.7: CloudWatch alarm for root account usage exists; SNS topic configured; check: PASS
ground_truth: SNS subscription status: PendingConfirmation (for old address) and 1 subscription with status: deleted (migration). Last alarm fire: 3 weeks ago (legitimate security team test) — zero notifications received. Root account activity would go undetected.
remediation_impact: Active monitoring gap for the most privileged AWS credential. Re-subscribe security team DL to SNS topic. Validate end-to-end alert delivery monthly.

scenario: Azure Defender generates a CREDENTIAL_DUMPING alert on the university Active Directory domain controller. The alert is auto-suppressed because it matches a suppression rule created for 'approved pentesting activity' from 3 years ago that was never removed after the pentest concluded. An active attacker is running Mimikatz.
why_misclassified: EC-49 pentest suppression never removed: suppression rule was valid for a 2-week pentest engagement in 2022. Rule was created with no expiration date. Three years later, real attacker activity matches the same pattern and is silently suppressed.
detection_signal: Azure Defender alert: Credential Dumping; suppression rule: approved-pentest-2022; status: suppressed
ground_truth: No pentest is currently authorized. Credential dumping is active attacker activity. Domain controller compromise = full AD forest takeover = access to all 45,000 student accounts, email, FERPA records, financial aid systems.
remediation_impact: Active incident. Domain controller compromise in progress. Isolate DC, rotate krbtgt account, force password reset for all privileged accounts, activate IR playbook.

scenario: GCP Artifact Analysis shows no critical vulnerabilities for the admission portal image. The image uses a multi-stage build where the build stage installs vulnerable packages. The final stage copies only the compiled binary. Artifact Analysis scans the final stage and sees only the clean binary — not the vulnerable build tools that ran during image creation.
why_misclassified: EC-43 multi-stage build blind spot: Artifact Analysis scans the final image layer only. Vulnerable packages in the build stage are excluded from the final image (correct) but if the build stage was compromised and injected malicious code into the binary, the scanner wouldn't detect it.
detection_signal: Artifact Analysis: final image scanned; 0 critical CVEs; all clear
ground_truth: The build pipeline uses a compromised base image for the build stage (supply chain attack). The malicious build stage inserted a reverse shell into the compiled admission portal binary during the latest build. Final image appears clean because the malicious code is in the compiled binary, not in package metadata.
remediation_impact: Admission portal serves 50,000 applicants including SSN and financial aid data. Reverse shell provides attacker code execution. Rebuild from trusted base image, rotate all secrets, investigate all builds in the last 30 days.

scenario: CIS check for IAM password policy shows PASS. The policy requires 8-character minimum passwords with complexity. However, an IAM identity center (SSO) feature flag 'allow_legacy_console_access' is enabled for a set of department admin users, which bypasses SSO and allows direct IAM console login with the weaker legacy password policy instead of the SSO MFA requirement.
why_misclassified: EC-45 feature flag bypass: the password policy check passes at the account level. The feature flag creating a bypass path is in IAM Identity Center configuration — a separate service not scanned by the password policy check. The actual MFA requirement is bypassable.
detection_signal: IAM password policy: min length 8, complexity enabled; CIS check: PASS
ground_truth: IAM Identity Center setting AllowLegacyConsoleAccess=true for department admin groups. These users can authenticate directly to AWS console with IAM username/password, bypassing SSO MFA. 23 users affected. Minimum password length 8 is below NIST 800-63B recommendation of 12.
remediation_impact: Department admins can log in without MFA to FERPA/GLBA scoped AWS environment. Disable legacy console access flag in IAM Identity Center, enforce SSO for all human users.

scenario: Security Hub compliance dashboard shows a high score (94%) for the university AWS environment. However, 17 Security Hub controls were disabled 2 years ago by a now-departed administrator to reduce alert noise. The disabled controls include IAM root MFA, CloudTrail encryption, and S3 public access blocking. The compliance percentage is calculated only over enabled controls.
why_misclassified: EC-50 inflated compliance score: Security Hub compliance percentage excludes disabled controls from the denominator. Disabling controls inflates the score without improving security. The 94% appears compliant but covers only the non-controversial controls.
detection_signal: Security Hub compliance: 94% PASSED; 17 controls disabled; dashboard shows green
ground_truth: 17 disabled controls include: IAM.6 (root MFA), CT.1 (CloudTrail encryption), S3.1 (S3 block public access). These are foundational controls. Re-enabling them would reveal an estimated 200+ active findings. True compliance: approximately 71%.
remediation_impact: Re-enable all 17 controls and remediate findings. The compliance score has been misleading leadership for 2 years. True security posture is significantly below reported metrics.

scenario: CSPM flags the financial aid staging bucket with a LOW finding for S3 bucket versioning being disabled. The staging bucket was seeded with a copy of production data (unmasked SSNs, tax information) for a UI testing exercise 6 months ago. The staging environment received LOW severity treatment because of its environment tag, but it contains real production data.
why_misclassified: EC-47 CSP severity scale / environment context mismatch: the scanner correctly lowered severity for a 'staging' environment (MP-01 non-prod deflator). But this staging environment contains real, unmasked production FERPA/GLBA data — making the environment label inaccurate for risk purposes.
detection_signal: Staging bucket: S3 versioning disabled; environment=staging; severity downgraded to LOW
ground_truth: Bucket contains 8,500 real student financial aid records copied from production for manual UI testing. Contains: SSNs, AGI, tax transcript data. Bucket is internet-accessible (public read was never disabled). Environment tag 'staging' does not reflect the actual data sensitivity.
remediation_impact: Active GLBA/FERPA breach. Financial data exposed publicly. Immediate: revoke public access, delete production data from staging, notify affected students, file breach report.

scenario: The student analytics dashboard ECR repository has scan-on-push enabled and shows 0 critical findings. The application uses a Python package from a private PyPI mirror that the university hosts internally. The internal mirror was compromised 3 weeks ago and a backdoored version of a statistics library was uploaded. ECR scan checks against public vulnerability databases and has no visibility into the internal mirror's integrity.
why_misclassified: EC-44 internal supply chain not scanned: ECR image scanning checks packages against NVD/OSV/Amazon Security Advisories. The backdoored package came from an internal mirror and has no CVE in public databases. The compromise is invisible to standard vulnerability scanning.
detection_signal: ECR scan: 0 critical, 0 high; repository has scan-on-push enabled; all clear
ground_truth: Internal PyPI mirror (pypi.university.edu) was compromised via weak admin password. Backdoored version of scikit-learn fork uploaded with data exfiltration capability. 15 applications installed the backdoored version over 3 weeks. No public CVE exists for this internal package.
remediation_impact: Student analytics data (grades, engagement metrics, FERPA-protected) being exfiltrated. Investigate internal PyPI mirror compromise, rebuild all affected images from clean packages, rotate credentials, assess data breach scope.

scenario: A GCP SCC finding for an overpermissive IAM binding (allAuthenticatedUsers on a BigQuery dataset) was muted 14 months ago by a developer who thought it referred to a dev dataset. The actual resource is the financial aid BigQuery dataset containing GLBA-protected financial information. All Google-authenticated users (including any Google account holder) can query student financial data.
why_misclassified: EC-49 muted finding with incorrect justification: developer muted the finding believing it was a dev dataset. The SCC finding referenced the production financial aid dataset. Mute was applied without validating the resource path.
detection_signal: GCP SCC finding muted: allAuthenticatedUsers-iam-binding; muted by: dev-ops@university.edu; mute reason: dev-environment
ground_truth: BigQuery dataset: projects/university-finance/datasets/financial_aid_prod. IAM binding: allAuthenticatedUsers has roles/bigquery.dataViewer. Any Google account holder can query student financial aid data. Dataset contains 45,000 records with EFC, AGI, and award amounts.
remediation_impact: Active GLBA breach. Financial aid data queryable by anyone with a Google account. Immediately remove allAuthenticatedUsers binding, unmute the finding, investigate whether data was accessed.

scenario: CloudWatch anomaly detection shows no unusual patterns for the grade submission Lambda. A student grade manipulation attack is occurring via a race condition — students are submitting concurrent requests that exploit a TOCTOU vulnerability to overwrite other students' grades. The attack is subtle (each individual request looks normal) and the anomaly detection baseline was trained on exam period high-volume data, making the current attack volume appear within normal range.
why_misclassified: EC-48 baseline contamination: the anomaly detection model was trained during finals periods with legitimately high-volume grade submissions. The attack volume during non-exam periods is lower than the trained peak, so it appears as normal variation. The attack pattern (concurrent duplicate request IDs) is not a volume anomaly.
detection_signal: CloudWatch anomaly detection: API call rate within normal bounds; no alert generated
ground_truth: Grade submission API receiving duplicate requestIds with different grade values for the same submission. Race condition allows whichever request wins to persist. 47 grade changes in 3 days outside grading periods. Pattern detectable by correlation analysis but not volume-based anomaly detection.
remediation_impact: Active grade manipulation attack. FERPA integrity violation. Fix: add idempotency tokens to grade submission API, implement distributed locking, investigate and reverse fraudulent grade changes.

scenario: Azure Defender shows no findings for the university student health center's FHIR API. The API is for the student health center (teaching hospital component). A misconfigured FHIR search parameter allows querying patient records without specifying a patient ID — returning all records matching a diagnosis code. This enables bulk PHI extraction with a simple query.
why_misclassified: EC-51 HIPAA-specific business logic vulnerability: Azure Defender checks infrastructure configuration (auth, encryption, network). It cannot detect application-level FHIR query logic vulnerabilities. The API is properly authenticated and encrypted — the vulnerability is in the query parameter validation.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: API Management configured correctly; authentication enabled; TLS enforced; no finding
ground_truth: FHIR API allows GET /Patient?_has:Condition:patient:code=F32.9 without patient-level authorization. Returns all students with depression diagnosis codes. 847 student health records extractable with a single API call by any authenticated API user (includes all medical students with API access).
remediation_impact: HIPAA PHI breach risk. 847 student mental health records accessible to unauthorized parties. Implement FHIR patient compartment authorization — responses must be scoped to patient context.

scenario: AWS Inspector shows no vulnerabilities for the course catalog sync Lambda. The function depends on a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline that pulls npm packages at build time. The CI/CD workflow file has a compromised third-party action (uses: malicious-org/setup-env@v2.1.0) that was introduced via a dependency update PR that passed automated review. The action exfiltrates environment variables (including AWS credentials) during CI runs.
why_misclassified: EC-42 supply chain via CI/CD: vulnerability is in the CI/CD pipeline, not in the deployed Lambda package. AWS Inspector scans the deployed artifact — it has no visibility into the GitHub Actions workflow that produced it. The credential exfiltration happens during build, not in the deployed function.
detection_signal: Inspector: Lambda function package scanned; 0 CVEs; all clear
ground_truth: GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/deploy.yml line 12: uses: malicious-org/setup-env@v2.1.0. This action was published to GitHub Marketplace 3 weeks ago. It exfiltrates secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY to attacker's endpoint during every CI run.
remediation_impact: AWS credentials compromised in every build for 3 weeks. Rotate all AWS credentials used in CI/CD immediately. Audit all GitHub Actions dependencies. Remove malicious action. Review what was deployed with potentially compromised credentials.

scenario: GuardDuty generates a LOW severity CryptoCurrency:EC2/BitcoinTool.B finding for a GPU compute node in the HPC cluster. The finding is automatically downgraded to LOW because GuardDuty's severity model assumes HPC GPU instances have higher baseline rates of mining-like traffic patterns (high GPU utilization, external connection patterns). A student researcher has actually installed a Monero miner on the node after compromising the cluster.
why_misclassified: EC-50 CSP enhanced controls inflating/deflating severity: GuardDuty's severity calibration for HPC GPU instances assumes mining-like patterns are normal. The automatic downgrade for 'HPC workloads' masks actual cryptomining. The finding should be HIGH given an unauthorized process is running.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: CryptoCurrency:EC2/BitcoinTool.B; auto-downgraded to LOW for HPC instance type
ground_truth: Process xmrig (Monero miner) running as PID 31337 on the GPU node. Network connections to pool.minexmr.com:4444. Unauthorized process consuming $4,200/month in GPU compute costs. Student gained access via weak SSH key from their personal laptop.
remediation_impact: Terminate unauthorized process, rotate SSH keys, investigate how student gained access to cluster nodes, file incident report. Financial impact: ~$4,200/month unauthorized compute cost.

scenario: Security Hub shows no findings for the student portal Cognito User Pool. The User Pool has MFA configured as OPTIONAL. A feature flag in the application code, REQUIRE_MFA_FOR_ADMIN=true, enforces MFA for admin-role users at the application layer. Security Hub passes the Cognito MFA check because MFA is enabled. However, the application-layer MFA enforcement has a bypass: changing the role claim in the JWT before token verification allows bypassing the admin MFA check entirely.
why_misclassified: EC-45 feature flag bypass: the infrastructure check (Cognito MFA available) passes. The application-layer enforcement contains a JWT role claim validation bug that allows privilege escalation before MFA is checked. Scanner cannot see application-layer authentication logic.
detection_signal: Cognito User Pool: MFA enabled (optional); Security Hub: pass
ground_truth: Application reads role from unverified JWT claim before checking MFA requirement. Attacker can craft a JWT with role=student, authenticate without MFA, then modify the role claim to admin in subsequent requests due to improper claim validation in the middleware.
remediation_impact: Authentication bypass to admin functions in FERPA-scoped student portal. Requires fix in JWT validation middleware: verify role claims from authoritative source (Cognito groups), not from user-controllable JWT claims.

scenario: Azure Policy compliance shows 100% compliant for the storage account SKU restriction policy (requiring Standard_LRS or Premium_LRS). The policy has an exemption for the student records storage account 'universitysistore' that was created during a migration project. The exemption comment says 'temporary: remove after migration' but was set with no expiration. The policy exemption makes the resource invisible to policy compliance reports.
why_misclassified: EC-50 / EC-49 policy exemption without expiration: the compliance dashboard shows 100% because exempted resources are excluded from compliance calculations. The exemption was intended to be temporary but became permanent by default.
detection_signal: Azure Policy compliance: 100% (all resources compliant or exempt); universitysistore: exempt
ground_truth: universitysistore is exempt from the storage SKU policy and also from related security policies (encryption, network rules). The storage account uses a non-standard SKU with weaker redundancy and is exempt from all security policy evaluation. Contains FERPA student information records.
remediation_impact: Remove policy exemption, bring storage account into compliance with security policies, establish expiration dates on all future policy exemptions.

scenario: CSPM shows no sensitive data findings for the application logs archive bucket. The bucket contains application logs which normally don't contain PII. However, a recent code change to the student portal accidentally started logging full HTTP request bodies (including form submissions) to application logs. Student login forms include username, and in some error paths, partial password data is logged. Macie has not been enabled for this bucket.
why_misclassified: EC-44 SBOM gap: CSPM checks bucket policy and encryption (both correct). Macie is not enabled for log buckets by default. The sensitive data appears in logs due to a recent application-level change that wasn't caught in code review.
detection_signal: S3 bucket: no public access; encryption enabled; no Macie findings (Macie not enabled for this bucket)
ground_truth: Application logs contain: 'POST /login body={"username":"student@univ.edu","password":"P@ss..."}' (truncated but partial password visible). Change was introduced in commit a1b2c3d, 3 weeks ago. Affects 45,000 daily login attempts. Logs retained 1 year.
remediation_impact: FERPA breach — authentication credentials in logs. Fix application code to scrub sensitive fields before logging. Enable Macie on log buckets. Assess whether existing logs need to be deleted.

scenario: A faculty member with administrative AWS access went on 12-month sabbatical. An IAM inactive user finding was generated and then suppressed with the note 'approved leave — account to be reactivated on return.' The sabbatical ended 4 months ago and the faculty member returned but the suppression was never removed. The account is still active, the faculty member has not used it, and no one checked whether the deactivation occurred.
why_misclassified: EC-49 suppression with future condition never re-evaluated: the suppression was appropriate when applied (sabbatical in progress) but the condition for re-evaluation (return from sabbatical) was never checked. The account may have been reactivated without the planned access review.
detection_signal: IAM user inactive finding: suppressed with reason approved-sabbatical-leave (suppressed 2025-01-15)
ground_truth: Faculty member returned 2025-09-01 (4 months ago). Account review was supposed to happen on return. IAM user has AdministratorAccess policy, console password active, no MFA. Last login: 8 months ago (pre-sabbatical). Account was never reviewed or access was never adjusted on return.
remediation_impact: Privileged IAM account with no recent use and no access review. Revoke console access pending formal access review. Re-establish appropriate permissions aligned with current role.

scenario: No GuardDuty or Security Hub alerts for the financial aid processing account. An attacker who compromised a developer's laptop is making API calls using stolen AWS SSO credentials. The attacker is carefully mimicking the developer's normal working hours (9am-5pm EST) and API call patterns to avoid anomaly detection. The stolen credential was used from a coffee shop IP in the same city — geographic anomaly is minimal.
why_misclassified: EC-48 adversarial evasion of baseline: attacker has profiled the developer's behavior patterns and is deliberately staying within the statistical baseline for time-of-day, API call frequency, and geographic proximity. Behavioral anomaly detection cannot detect what looks statistically normal.
detection_signal: CloudTrail: normal API patterns; GuardDuty: no findings; Security Hub: no alerts
ground_truth: Attacker accessed AWS SSO from a coffee shop (same city as developer). Calls are being made 9am-4:30pm on weekdays. 95% of calls are read-only (identical to developer pattern). 5% are novel — reading financial aid S3 objects the developer never accesses. Low-and-slow exfiltration of student financial records.
remediation_impact: Active credential compromise with data exfiltration. Detection requires correlation analysis beyond baseline deviation. Implement device trust (require corporate MDM device for SSO). Investigate all S3 reads on financial aid data.

scenario: AWS Security Hub flags MIT OpenCourseWare S3 bucket as CRITICAL public read exposure. The bucket serves freely available course materials, lecture videos, and problem sets intentionally published under Creative Commons license for global access.
why_misclassified: Scanner has no context that this is an intentionally public educational content bucket with no PII. FERPA does not apply to de-identified course content.
detection_signal: S3 bucket has public read ACL and no Block Public Access enabled
ground_truth: Bucket contains only published open-access academic content. No student records, no PII. Public access is the product requirement for OpenCourseWare.
remediation_impact: Blocking public access would break the OpenCourseWare platform for millions of global learners and violate the MIT OCW mission.

scenario: Security Hub flags an EC2 instance as having a public IP with port 22 open to the world. The instance is the head node of an AWS ParallelCluster HPC environment used by Stanford computational biology faculty for NIH-funded genomics research.
why_misclassified: Research HPC clusters require SSH access from collaborating institutions worldwide. The security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 intentionally to enable federated research access per NIH data access agreements.
detection_signal: Security group ingress rule allows 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP/22; instance has public IP
ground_truth: This is a research computing head node. SSH access from arbitrary academic IPs is the expected operational model. Host-based auth uses ed25519 keys only; password auth disabled.
remediation_impact: Restricting SSH to specific CIDRs would block collaborators at partner universities and violate NIH grant terms requiring open data access infrastructure.

scenario: AWS Security Hub flags a cross-account IAM trust relationship as suspicious lateral movement risk. The role is trusted by Instructure's Canvas LMS production account to pull course roster data for LTI 1.3 grade passback.
why_misclassified: Cross-account trust to a known EdTech vendor for LTI integration is standard practice. The trust is scoped to a specific external account ID with condition on ExternalId, not a wildcard.
detection_signal: IAM role has trust policy allowing sts:AssumeRole from external AWS account 899912818238
ground_truth: Vendor account 899912818238 is Instructure (Canvas). Trust is required for LTI Advantage grade passback. ExternalId condition prevents confused deputy. FERPA BAA is in place.
remediation_impact: Removing the cross-account trust breaks Canvas grade sync for 45,000 enrolled students mid-semester.

scenario: GCP Security Command Center flags a firewall rule allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 in the UC Berkeley student cloud sandbox project. The project is a CS coursework environment where students practice Linux administration and networking as part of their curriculum.
why_misclassified: This is an intentionally permissive sandbox for educational labs. No production data, no PII, no persistent workloads. The project is recycled each semester.
detection_signal: Firewall rule 'allow-ssh-student-sandbox' allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0
ground_truth: Student lab environment rebuilt each academic quarter. Students SSH into their own assigned VMs. No sensitive data stored. This permissive config is the pedagogical point of the exercise.
remediation_impact: Restricting access would break the networking lab assignment for 200 students in CS 168 (Internet Architecture).

scenario: AWS Security Hub marks the Banner SIS read replica as CRITICAL due to publicly_accessible=true. Banner is the student information system used by 80,000 students. The flag is set to true to allow Ellucian's cloud-hosted application tier to connect, but the RDS instance sits in a private subnet with no public route.
why_misclassified: EC-37 pattern: publicly_accessible=true in RDS does not mean internet-reachable. The subnet has no IGW route and the security group only allows 3306 from the application server SG.
detection_signal: RDS parameter publicly_accessible=true; FERPA-scoped data classification
ground_truth: Instance is in private subnet (10.20.30.0/24). Route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 → igw entry. Security group allows only internal app tier. Flag is a legacy Banner deployment requirement for DNS resolution.
remediation_impact: Setting publicly_accessible=false would break Ellucian Banner's connectivity architecture and take down student registration for the entire university.

scenario: Azure Defender flags Harvard Library digital collections storage account for public blob access. The account hosts digitized manuscripts, historical photographs, and out-of-copyright texts for the Harvard Digital Collections platform, which serves researchers globally.
why_misclassified: Public blob access is intentional for a public digital library. Content is entirely historical/academic with no PII. FERPA does not govern library collections. Content is explicitly licensed for public access.
detection_signal: Storage account allows public blob access; AllowBlobPublicAccess=true
ground_truth: Harvard Digital Collections is a public-facing academic resource. All content is explicitly cleared for public distribution. No student data in scope.
remediation_impact: Disabling public access breaks the Harvard Digital Collections website used by thousands of researchers and the public daily.

scenario: AWS Security Hub flags the university IT security break-glass role as CRITICAL because it has AdministratorAccess policy. Role is used only during security incidents and access is logged to immutable CloudTrail with SNS alerting on every assume-role event.
why_misclassified: EC-28 break-glass pattern: emergency admin access with full audit trail is a standard security control, not a misconfiguration. Role is never assumed in normal operations.
detection_signal: IAM role has arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess attached; no MFA condition on trust policy
ground_truth: Break-glass role assumed 3 times in past 18 months, each time with dual approval in ServiceNow. CloudTrail alert fires within 60 seconds of assume-role. Role is not associated with any user or service in normal operation.
remediation_impact: Removing or restricting the break-glass role would eliminate the incident response capability, potentially making ransomware recovery impossible without vendor support.

scenario: Security Hub flags an NSF-funded research data archive bucket for lacking SSE-S3 encryption at rest. The bucket contains climate model output data required to be publicly accessible under NSF's open data policy (NSF 23-104). The data is intentionally unencrypted at the object level to allow direct HTTP range requests from HPC clusters.
why_misclassified: NSF grant terms explicitly require data to be available without authentication barriers. The data contains no PII — only scientific measurements. Encryption would not add security value for public data.
detection_signal: S3 bucket default encryption not enabled; public read ACL present
ground_truth: This bucket fulfills NSF open data mandate (Award #2112345). All objects are synthetic climate model outputs. No human subjects data. IRB approval not required.
remediation_impact: Encrypting and blocking public access violates NSF grant terms and could result in clawback of $2.3M grant funding.

scenario: AWS Security Hub flags a security group allowing TCP/443 from 0.0.0.0/0 as high severity for a university campus Wi-Fi captive portal. The portal authenticates students and faculty before granting internet access and must be reachable from any device on campus before authentication.
why_misclassified: A captive portal by design must be reachable before credentials are established. Restricting inbound HTTPS to known CIDRs would break authentication for any new device. No sensitive data is exposed at the public endpoint.
detection_signal: Security group ingress allows TCP/443 from 0.0.0.0/0 on production-tagged instance
ground_truth: Instance serves only the pre-auth captive portal page and 802.1X redirect. All student data is processed behind ALB with WAF. Post-auth traffic moves to isolated VLAN.
remediation_impact: Restricting the captive portal security group would prevent all new devices from authenticating to campus Wi-Fi.

scenario: Security Hub flags 47 EC2 instances in an AWS classroom account for using IMDSv1. These are ephemeral student lab instances created fresh at the start of each 3-hour lab session and destroyed automatically at session end. The account contains no persistent data.
why_misclassified: EC-10 ephemeral pattern: instances exist for less than 4 hours and are auto-terminated. No IAM roles with meaningful permissions are attached. The finding is technically valid but operationally irrelevant.
detection_signal: EC2 instances with HttpTokens=optional (IMDSv1 allowed); no IMDSv2 enforcement
ground_truth: Instances are created by AWS Academy Learner Lab automation using a fixed AMI. Average lifespan is 2.5 hours. IAM role attached allows only S3 read on course materials bucket. No student PII stored.
remediation_impact: Forcing IMDSv2 requires updating the AWS Academy AMI, which is vendor-controlled and not university-modifiable without breaking the lab automation.

scenario: AWS Inspector flags CVE-2023-44487 (HTTP/2 Rapid Reset) on the university web server running nginx 1.24.0. The nginx configuration has http2 disabled in the server block for the student portal due to compatibility issues with older Banner ERP client libraries.
why_misclassified: EC-03 disabled feature: HTTP/2 is explicitly disabled (listen 443 ssl; without http2 directive). CVE-2023-44487 requires HTTP/2 to be exploitable. With HTTP/2 off, the vulnerability is inert.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-44487 matched against nginx 1.24.0 package version
ground_truth: nginx.conf has 'listen 443 ssl;' without 'http2' parameter. HTTP/2 negotiation disabled. ALPN returns only h1.1. Confirmed via curl --http2-prior-knowledge returning 400.
remediation_impact: Patching nginx to address CVE-2023-44487 while keeping HTTP/2 disabled provides no security improvement. Unnecessary change risk during exam season.

scenario: AWS Inspector flags a HIGH severity finding for a vulnerable version of lodash in the grade export Lambda function. The lodash package is listed in devDependencies of package.json and was included in the deployment zip by mistake during bundling, but is never imported in the function code.
why_misclassified: EC-43 build-time dependency: lodash is a devDependency used only in test scripts. It was accidentally bundled but no application code requires or imports it. The runtime code path never loads lodash.
detection_signal: lodash 4.17.20 detected in Lambda deployment package; CVE-2021-23337 matched
ground_truth: grep -r 'require.*lodash\|import.*lodash' src/ returns 0 results. Package is in node_modules due to bundler misconfiguration but is dead code. No require() call reaches it.
remediation_impact: False urgency; actual fix is build pipeline cleanup to exclude devDependencies from production bundle, not a security patch.

scenario: Security Hub flags the university library catalog database as CRITICAL. The Alma library management system requires publicly_accessible=true for its SaaS integration model. The RDS instance is in a private subnet with no IGW in the route table.
why_misclassified: EC-37 pattern: publicly_accessible API flag does not equal internet-reachable. Private subnet + no IGW route + restrictive SG means no actual internet path exists.
detection_signal: aws_db_instance.publicly_accessible = true; data classification = student records
ground_truth: Route table rtb-0abc123 has no 0.0.0.0/0 entry. Security group sg-0def456 allows only port 5432 from 10.0.0.0/16. ExLuis verified: nc -zv [public-dns] 5432 times out from internet.
remediation_impact: Setting publicly_accessible=false breaks Ex Libris Alma's SaaS connectivity pattern and would require a full library system architecture change.

scenario: IAM Access Analyzer flags the HPC job submission role for having batch:* permissions across all resources. The role is used by the university's slurm-to-AWS bridge to submit computational jobs for faculty. Batch:* is required because job queue ARNs are dynamically generated per research project.
why_misclassified: EC-15 permission boundary pattern: while the policy is broad, an IAM permission boundary attached to the role restricts maximum effective permissions to batch:SubmitJob and batch:DescribeJobs only. The overpermissive policy never takes effect.
detection_signal: IAM policy allows batch:* on resource *; flagged as overly permissive
ground_truth: Role has PermissionsBoundary: arn:aws:iam::161718192021:policy/hpc-submission-boundary limiting effective actions to 2 batch actions. IAM policy evaluation: effective = policy ∩ boundary.
remediation_impact: Tightening the base policy is good hygiene but has zero security impact due to the boundary. Change carries migration risk for active research jobs.

scenario: Security Hub generates duplicate findings for S3 versioning across us-east-1, us-west-2, and eu-west-1 for a Coursera video transcoding temp bucket that uses S3 cross-region replication. The bucket intentionally has no versioning because it holds ephemeral transcoding artifacts deleted after 24 hours.
why_misclassified: EC-38 cross-region replication: scanner sees 3 identical findings across regions because replication creates copies that inherit the source configuration. Single logical issue inflated to 3 findings.
detection_signal: 3 separate findings: S3 versioning disabled on buckets in 3 regions
ground_truth: All three are replicas of the same logical bucket. Content is transient (TTL 24h lifecycle rule). No student data stored. Versioning on temp storage would increase cost 3x with no benefit.
