detection_signal: S3 bucket energy-scada-config-backups IAM policy, private access — INFO: private storage with access control
ground_truth: Field teams using shared IAM user credentials for S3 access to BCSI (relay protection configurations). Shared keys cannot be attributed to individuals. NERC CIP-006 requires individual accountability. Compromise of shared key exposes BCSI to all key holders.
remediation_impact: Replace shared IAM users with IAM Roles Anywhere or per-user IAM roles with temporary credentials. Enable S3 server access logging for accountability. Review NERC CIP-004 training records for field team members with BCSI access.

scenario: GCP organization IAM binding energy-emergency-ops@utility.com has roles/owner at the organization level. CSPM reports INFO because the account shows recent activity (last login 5 days ago). This service account is used as an emergency organization owner for break-glass scenarios. It has no MFA requirement in GCP IAM (GCP does not enforce MFA at the IAM level — MFA is an Identity Provider concern). The utility uses Google Workspace as IdP. The Google Workspace admin confirms MFA is optional for this account.
why_misclassified: EC-50: scanner treats recent account activity as a positive health signal. Org-level owner with optional MFA and break-glass designation is a critical exposure — compromise gives full GCP organization control including all NERC CIP BES Cyber Systems.
detection_signal: GCP org owner energy-emergency-ops active 5 days ago — INFO: account in active use
ground_truth: Organization owner with no enforced MFA. Full control over all GCP projects including NERC CIP BES Cyber Systems. NERC CIP-007 R5 requires authentication for all accounts accessing BES Cyber Systems. Org-level owner without MFA is a CRITICAL finding.
remediation_impact: Enforce MFA in Google Workspace for energy-emergency-ops. Reduce to organization viewer + PIM-eligible owner role. Implement Google Cloud Identity's context-aware access to require MFA for all org-level operations.

scenario: IAM role energy-vendor-access-ABBLtd has no recent usage (last used 8 months ago). CSPM reports INFO because the role has specific ARN-scoped policies (not wildcard). ABB Ltd's maintenance contract for protection relay configuration was terminated 8 months ago. The role has permissions to read from the S3 bucket containing relay configuration backups and write to the DynamoDB setpoints table. ABB's AWS account can still assume this role.
why_misclassified: EC-23: specific ARN policies score INFO. Inactivity treated as a neutral signal. The role is for a former vendor with access to relay configuration (BCSI) and setpoint write capability. Orphaned vendor access is a NERC CIP-004 compliance violation.
detection_signal: IAM role energy-vendor-access-ABBLtd no recent use — INFO: unused role with specific resource policies
ground_truth: Former vendor ABB can still assume this role and write relay setpoints to 847 substations. Contract terminated 8 months ago. NERC CIP-004 requires removal of access within 24 hours of contractor termination. This is an 8-month compliance violation.
remediation_impact: Immediate: delete IAM role, revoke trust policy. NERC CIP self-report for 8-month access control violation. Audit CloudTrail for any post-termination role assumptions.

scenario: GCP service account key for energy-substation-reporter@energy-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com is 88 days old. CSPM reports LOW (within 90-day window). The key is embedded in the configuration of 120 substation data concentrators across transmission network. Key expires in 2 days. Simultaneous loss of 120 substation data concentrators removes real-time visibility into transmission network status, triggering NERC CIP monitoring obligation.
why_misclassified: EC-14: key within window scores LOW without recognizing that 2-day expiry with 120 field devices constitutes an imminent operational and compliance crisis.
detection_signal: SA key energy-substation-reporter age 88 days — LOW: key within rotation policy window
ground_truth: Key expires in 2 days. 120 substation data concentrators will lose cloud connectivity. Loss of real-time transmission monitoring may trigger NERC CIP reliability coordinator notification requirement.
remediation_impact: Emergency rotation. Push new key to all 120 concentrators via available NERC CIP-approved remote management channel. Long-term: implement IAM Roles Anywhere for concentrators.

scenario: IAM role energy-scada-lambda-role has Action: s3:* on arn:aws:s3:::energy-relay-configs. CSPM reports INFO because the resource is a specific S3 ARN. s3:* on the relay configuration bucket grants s3:DeleteBucket and s3:PutBucketPolicy — a Lambda function could delete the bucket containing protection relay configurations for 847 substations or expose it publicly.
why_misclassified: EC-25: specific resource ARN scores INFO without checking that s3:* action wildcard includes destructive capabilities on OT configuration storage.
detection_signal: IAM role energy-scada-lambda-role s3:* on specific bucket ARN — INFO: resource-scoped policy
ground_truth: s3:* grants DeleteBucket and PutBucketPolicy on the relay configuration bucket. Compromised Lambda could destroy relay configurations for 847 substations or expose BCSI. Minimum permissions: s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject.
remediation_impact: Replace s3:* with explicit [s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:ListBucket] on the relay config bucket. Critical BCSI bucket should have bucket policy denying DeleteBucket from all principals except dedicated ops role.

scenario: Azure Key Vault certificate energy-substation-tls-cert expires in 6 days. CSPM reports LOW because the certificate is not yet expired. The certificate secures TLS connections to the substation SCADA gateway. When it expires, all 67 substation RTUs will fail TLS handshakes and lose connectivity to the SCADA cloud platform. Certificate renewal requires coordinated deployment across 67 field devices.
why_misclassified: EC-14: non-expired certificate scores LOW without considering imminent expiry (6 days) and the operational impact of simultaneous loss of 67 field device connections.
detection_signal: Key Vault certificate energy-substation-tls-cert expires in 6 days — LOW: certificate not yet expired
ground_truth: Certificate expiry in 6 days will cause TLS handshake failures across 67 substation RTUs. Loss of 67 RTU connections represents a monitoring gap requiring NERC CIP reliability coordinator notification.
remediation_impact: Emergency certificate renewal and coordinated push to 67 substation RTUs. Enable Key Vault certificate auto-renewal for future certs. NERC CIP change management required.

scenario: GCP project energy-scada-prod has an IAM binding granting roles/bigquery.dataViewer to a service account from project energy-contractor-xicel (a terminated contractor's project). CSPM reports INFO because it's a specific SA ARN (not allUsers). The contractor's project was decommissioned 6 months ago but the IAM binding in the SCADA project was never removed. The former contractor SA may still be active in the decommissioned project.
why_misclassified: EC-23: specific SA binding scores INFO. Scanner does not check if the bound SA belongs to a terminated contractor or whether the source project is still active.
detection_signal: Project energy-scada-prod IAM binding for contractor SA — INFO: specific service account binding
ground_truth: Former contractor SA from decommissioned project may still be valid and retain read access to SCADA operational data (BCSI). NERC CIP-004 requires access termination. 6-month gap is a compliance violation.
remediation_impact: Remove IAM binding immediately. Check whether contractor SA is still active in the decommissioned project. NERC CIP self-report may be required. Audit for other contractor SA bindings across NERC CIP projects.

scenario: BigQuery dataset energy-nerc-audit-logs stores NERC CIP-007 R5 audit logs but has no BigQuery dataset backup policy. CSPM reports INFO (data in BigQuery). BigQuery does not have native backup — once deleted, data is gone after 7-day time travel window. If the dataset were deleted (admin error or ransomware), NERC CIP audit trail for the past 7 years could be irretrievably lost, creating a compliance violation for all past NERC CIP reporting periods.
why_misclassified: EC-30: BigQuery default time travel window treated as sufficient. No evaluation of whether 7-day retention meets NERC CIP 7-year audit log retention requirement, or whether deletion of the dataset is possible.
detection_signal: BigQuery dataset energy-nerc-audit-logs data present — INFO: audit logs in BigQuery
ground_truth: NERC CIP-007 R5 requires 7-year audit log retention. BigQuery dataset deletion beyond 7-day time travel is irreversible. A deleted dataset creates non-recoverable NERC CIP compliance violation. Dataset needs long-term backup to GCS.
remediation_impact: Configure scheduled BigQuery dataset export to GCS WORM bucket (Object Lock). 7-year GCS archive ensures NERC CIP audit logs are recoverable even if BigQuery dataset is accidentally deleted.

scenario: GCP firewall rule allow-ssh-corp allows SSH from 10.0.0.0/8 to the SCADA configuration management VM. CSPM reports LOW (private RFC1918 source). The 10.0.0.0/8 range includes the full corporate network of a multi-utility holding company with ~20,000 employees, contracted vendors, and overseas offices. The SCADA VM stores IEC 61850 substation configuration (SCL files) for 200 transmission substations.
why_misclassified: EC-16: RFC1918 treated as uniformly safe without evaluating that a /8 range for a large utility includes contractors and vendor networks with no direct operational need for SCADA configuration access.
detection_signal: Firewall allow-ssh-corp SSH from 10.0.0.0/8 — LOW: private network SSH source
ground_truth: SSH to IEC 61850 SCL configuration storage from entire 20,000-person corporate network including contractors. NERC CIP-005 requires access restricted to personnel with specific job requirements. /8 source to BCSI storage violates NERC CIP electronic security perimeter requirements.
remediation_impact: Restrict to specific NERC CIP-qualified operator workstation IPs (< 10 hosts). Implement MFA for SSH access. Log all SSH sessions to the SCADA configuration VM.

scenario: IAM user nerc-compliance-admin has AdministratorAccess and no MFA. CSPM reports INFO — account has not been used in 270 days (dormant). The account administers the NERC CIP compliance account containing audit logs, compliance evidence, and BCSI documentation for 3 NERC CIP audits. A compromised account could delete 7 years of NERC CIP audit evidence, creating irreversible compliance violations.
why_misclassified: EC-48: inactivity interpreted as low risk rather than recognizing dormant high-privilege account without MFA as an undetectable compromise target.
detection_signal: IAM user nerc-compliance-admin AdministratorAccess, inactive 270 days — INFO: account inactive
ground_truth: Administrator access to NERC CIP compliance evidence store with no MFA. Dormant account harder to detect if compromised. Compromise + audit evidence deletion = potential NERC penalty exposure. TSA SD requires MFA for all privileged accounts.
remediation_impact: Disable account. Replace with PIM-eligible role requiring MFA activation with justification. Alert on any activation.

scenario: GCP service account energy-rtd-deploy@energy-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/cloudbuild.builds.editor at project level. CSPM reports LOW (standard CI/CD role). The SA deploys configurations to the Real-Time Dispatch system. cloudbuild.builds.editor can create, trigger, and modify build pipelines that push to the GCS bucket containing RTD operating instructions. A compromised SA could inject malicious dispatch instructions into the real-time generation dispatch pipeline.
why_misclassified: EC-02: Cloud Build editor rated as a standard CI/CD role without evaluating that the build pipeline deploys to a real-time grid dispatch system. TSA SD requires supply chain security controls for pipeline OT systems.
detection_signal: SA energy-rtd-deploy roles/cloudbuild.builds.editor — LOW: standard Cloud Build role
ground_truth: Cloud Build editor on RTD deployment pipeline can create builds that inject malicious dispatch instructions. Compromised SA could push malicious dispatch file to production RTD system, causing incorrect generation dispatch.
remediation_impact: Separate build trigger SA from deployment SA. Implement dual-approval gate for any build targeting RTD production bucket. Code signing for RTD configuration packages. TSA SD supply chain security controls required.

scenario: Security group sg-scada-gateway allows all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0). CSPM reports INFO — outbound allow-all is the AWS default. The SCADA gateway VPC contains Cloud Lambda functions interfacing with substation RTUs. Unrestricted outbound allows a compromised SCADA function to exfiltrate RTU telemetry, relay configurations (BCSI), or contact C2 infrastructure. NERC CIP-005 requires documented outbound controls for ESP boundaries.
why_misclassified: EC-41: AWS default outbound allow treated as INFO baseline. For NERC CIP Electronic Security Perimeter, unrestricted outbound from SCADA infrastructure is a compliance gap.
detection_signal: Security group sg-scada-gateway outbound 0.0.0.0/0 — INFO: standard AWS outbound rule
ground_truth: SCADA gateway should only need outbound to RTU polling IPs, NTP, DNS, and AWS service endpoints. Unrestricted outbound from NERC CIP ESP-boundary infrastructure violates CIP-005 requirements for documented and justified electronic access controls.
remediation_impact: Add deny-all-outbound SG rule and explicit allow rules for RTU polling IPs, NTP, DNS, and VPC endpoints. Document all outbound communications per NERC CIP-005 R1.5.

scenario: Azure Key Vault secret energy-pipeline-supervisory-key used for pipeline SCADA supervisory system access has not been rotated in 18 months. CSPM reports LOW because the secret is in Key Vault. TSA Security Directive requires 90-day credential rotation for pipeline OT systems. The supervisory key controls access to the pipeline SCADA for a natural gas transmission pipeline. 18 months significantly exceeds TSA SD requirements.
why_misclassified: EC-36: Key Vault storage treated as sufficient. Age and TSA SD compliance context not evaluated. Pipeline supervisory credentials with 18-month rotation gap violate TSA SD requirements.
detection_signal: Key Vault secret energy-pipeline-supervisory-key age 18 months — LOW: secret in Key Vault
ground_truth: TSA SD requires 90-day rotation for pipeline OT credentials. 18-month gap is a TSA SD violation reportable to TSA. Supervisory key controls natural gas pipeline SCADA — compromise enables unauthorized pipeline operations.
remediation_impact: Immediate rotation coordinated with SCADA system restart. TSA SD self-report. Enable Key Vault expiry policy for 90-day maximum on all pipeline supervisory credentials.

scenario: GCP organization policy has an IAM binding granting roles/owner to energy-breakglass@energy-utility.com. CSPM reports INFO because the account was last active 90 days ago and owner role is documented as break-glass. The break-glass account has no MFA enforced (GCP IAM relies on IdP MFA — IdP is Google Workspace where this account has MFA optional). The account has full GCP organization ownership including all NERC CIP BES Cyber Systems projects.
why_misclassified: EC-50: break-glass owner documented as INFO acceptable pattern. Does not check whether break-glass has MFA enforced or whether the blast radius (full GCP org owner) is justified for emergency scenarios.
detection_signal: GCP org owner energy-breakglass, inactive 90 days — INFO: break-glass account
ground_truth: Org owner with optional MFA. Full control over all NERC CIP BES Cyber Systems projects in GCP. A compromised password enables deletion of all SCADA cloud infrastructure, all audit logs, and all compliance evidence. NERC CIP CIP-007 requires MFA for all BCSI access.
remediation_impact: Enforce MFA in Google Workspace for break-glass account. Reduce to PIM-eligible owner with 1-hour time-limited activation. Implement break-glass access alerting.

scenario: GCP service account energy-vendor-shared@energy-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com has its JSON key shared with 4 external vendors (Siemens, ABB, Schneider, GE Vernova) for SCADA integration access. CSPM reports LOW because the SA has a specific IAM role (roles/bigquery.dataViewer on one dataset). The SA key is stored in vendor systems with no visibility into how each vendor protects it. NERC CIP-004 requires individual accountability for BCSI access.
why_misclassified: EC-22: specific IAM role evaluated as LOW risk without detecting that a shared SA key distributed to 4 external vendors provides no individual accountability and cannot be selectively revoked for one vendor.
detection_signal: SA energy-vendor-shared, specific IAM role — LOW: scoped service account
ground_truth: Shared SA key across 4 vendors prevents individual accountability (NERC CIP-004 violation). If one vendor is compromised, the shared key must be rotated for all vendors simultaneously. NERC CIP requires individual attribution for BCSI access.
remediation_impact: Create per-vendor service accounts with identical minimal permissions. Enable Cloud Audit Logs attributed to each vendor SA. Individual revocation possible on contract termination.

scenario: NSG energy-pipeline-ems-nsg allows RDP (TCP 3389) from 10.0.0.0/8. CSPM reports LOW (RFC1918 source). The NSG protects the Pipeline Energy Management System that controls natural gas compressor stations along a 500-mile pipeline. The 10.0.0.0/8 range includes IT helpdesk, contractor VPN, and vendor support networks. TSA SD requires strict access control to pipeline OT systems limited to authorized personnel only.
why_misclassified: EC-16: /8 RFC1918 source treated as uniformly safe. Pipeline EMS controlling compressor stations has direct physical infrastructure impact — unauthorized access could cause overpressure events.
detection_signal: NSG energy-pipeline-ems-nsg RDP from 10.0.0.0/8 — LOW: private network source
ground_truth: Pipeline EMS controls natural gas compressor stations accessible to full corporate network including IT helpdesk and contractors. TSA SD requires access limited to authorized OT operators. Unauthorized control of compressor stations could cause overpressure safety events.
remediation_impact: Restrict NSG to 5 authorized OT operator workstation IPs. Implement MFA for RDP. Use Azure Bastion with PIM. TSA SD compliance review required.

scenario: Security group permits TCP 102 (IEC 104/S7) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 on the substation SCADA gateway. Scanner flags as broadly open industrial protocol port. The security group fronts an ICS-to-cloud data historian bridge — the S7 port requires certificate-based authentication at the Siemens S7comm-plus protocol layer, and the gateway validates PLC identity certificates before accepting any commands. No unauthenticated connections proceed.
why_misclassified: EC-08: scanner evaluates network-layer port reachability only; it cannot inspect ICS protocol-layer certificate authentication at the Siemens S7comm-plus layer. The S7 port appears 'open' but requires industrial certificate authentication.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup sg-scada-gw allows inbound TCP 102 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: industrial protocol port broadly accessible
ground_truth: TCP 102 requires valid PLC identity certificates issued by the utility's industrial PKI. No unauthenticated session can establish S7comm-plus connection. This is intentional NERC CIP boundary architecture for remote substation monitoring.
remediation_impact: Restricting to a static CIDR would break SCADA polling from mobile substations and emergency restoration units with dynamic IP addresses. PLC certificates provide stronger authentication than IP allowlisting.

scenario: Azure Event Hub namespace grid-telemetry-prod does not use Customer Managed Keys. CSPM reports HIGH for unencrypted grid telemetry stream. Event Hub uses Microsoft-managed encryption keys (PMK) for at-rest data. The telemetry data consists of grid frequency, voltage, and load measurements — operational data required for NERC CIP reliability but not classified as CIP High or Medium BES Cyber System Information (BCSI).
why_misclassified: EC-31: scanner requires CMK for all Event Hub namespaces without distinguishing NERC CIP BCSI classification levels. Grid operational telemetry (frequency, voltage readings) is not BCSI under CIP-011.
detection_signal: Event Hub namespace grid-telemetry-prod PMK encryption only — HIGH: grid telemetry without customer-managed encryption
ground_truth: NERC CIP-011 requires protection for BES Cyber System Information. Grid telemetry measurements are operational data, not BCSI. PMK encryption with Azure's security baseline meets compliance requirements for this data classification.
remediation_impact: CMK migration adds key rotation overhead and vault dependency. NERC CIP-011 BCSI requirements are not triggered for grid frequency/voltage measurements under the current classification.

scenario: GCP service account scada-historian@energy-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/bigquery.dataEditor on the grid-operations dataset. CSPM flags excessive permissions. The historian service must write new telemetry records AND delete records past the 7-year NERC CIP retention window. DataEditor includes both insert and delete capabilities, which is the minimum required for the historian's write + retention-purge operations.
why_misclassified: EC-22: data retention compliance requires deletion capability alongside write. Scanner treats dataEditor as excessive without evaluating that the NERC CIP 7-year retention management requires controlled deletion after retention expiry.
detection_signal: SA scada-historian has roles/bigquery.dataEditor — HIGH: SCADA historian with data deletion capability
ground_truth: NERC CIP-007 R5 requires retention of security logs for specific periods followed by secure destruction. The historian must delete records at retention expiry. dataEditor is the minimum BigQuery role supporting both write and controlled deletion.
remediation_impact: Downgrading to dataWriter breaks the retention purge pipeline, causing non-compliance with NERC CIP-007 R5 data retention requirements. A custom BigQuery role with specific table modification permissions is the ideal fix.

scenario: CloudTrail in account energy-ops-prod does not log data events for S3. CSPM reports HIGH for missing data event logging under NERC CIP. The S3 buckets in this account store SCADA backups. Data-level S3 events (GetObject, PutObject) for the SCADA backup buckets generate 180M+ events daily at $0.10/100K events. The security team uses S3 Server Access Logs (free) for the SCADA backup buckets, which meet NERC CIP-006 R1 logging requirements for physical and electronic access.
why_misclassified: EC-45: scanner requires CloudTrail data events without evaluating that S3 Server Access Logs provide equivalent access audit capability for NERC CIP compliance at significantly lower cost.
detection_signal: CloudTrail data events for S3 disabled — HIGH: SCADA backup storage access unlogged
ground_truth: S3 Server Access Logging enabled on all SCADA backup buckets. Access logs delivered to security-archive bucket with 3-year retention per NERC CIP-007 R5. CloudTrail data events would duplicate this logging at $65K/year additional cost.
remediation_impact: Enabling CloudTrail S3 data events adds estimated $65K/year in CloudTrail costs for duplicate log coverage already provided by S3 Server Access Logs.

scenario: Azure Function App iec61968-meter-data-webhook has authorization level Anonymous. CSPM flags as unauthenticated function. The function receives ANSI C12.22 metering protocol messages from smart meters deployed at customer sites. Smart meter hardware does not support Azure AD token flows — they authenticate using DLMS/COSEM application-layer authentication with meter-specific symmetric keys. The function validates COSEM authentication on every request before processing.
why_misclassified: EC-15: application-level COSEM meter authentication not visible to platform-level auth scanner. 'Anonymous' Azure auth is required because meter hardware cannot perform OAuth flows. Custom COSEM auth enforces identity at the protocol layer.
detection_signal: Function App iec61968-meter-data-webhook authorization Anonymous — HIGH: smart meter data ingestion unauthenticated
ground_truth: Every smart meter message is validated with DLMS/COSEM application-layer authentication using meter-specific symmetric keys. Invalid signatures rejected before processing. IEC 62056 metering protocol requires application-layer auth, not OAuth.
remediation_impact: Enabling Azure AD auth would break metering data ingestion from 2.4M deployed smart meters that use hardware-embedded COSEM credentials. No firmware update path available for deployed meter hardware.

scenario: Cloud SQL instance energy-ems-db has authorized network 0.0.0.0/0. CSPM reports CRITICAL for public Energy Management System database. The EMS database is accessed exclusively through Cloud SQL Auth Proxy with IAM service account authentication. The 0.0.0.0/0 entry is a legacy Terraform misconfiguration. No application connects directly to TCP 5432 — all connections use the proxy. The authorized network entry has no practical effect given proxy-only access.
why_misclassified: EC-03: legacy misconfiguration co-exists with enforced proxy architecture. Scanner flags the authorized network setting without detecting that Cloud SQL Auth Proxy is the mandatory and enforced connection path.
detection_signal: Cloud SQL energy-ems-db authorized networks 0.0.0.0/0 — CRITICAL: energy management system database publicly accessible
ground_truth: No direct TCP connection to 5432 occurs. All connections via Cloud SQL Auth Proxy with IAM SA auth. 0.0.0.0/0 authorized network is legacy misconfiguration tracked in backlog. Proxy enforcement means no direct public access is possible.
remediation_impact: Removing 0.0.0.0/0 from authorized networks is correct remediation — tracked as technical debt. CRITICAL urgency is unwarranted given proxy-only access. Scheduled for next maintenance window.

scenario: S3 bucket energy-outage-maps-public is publicly readable. CSPM reports HIGH for public S3 in NERC CIP environment. This bucket hosts public-facing storm damage maps and estimated restoration time (ETR) data for customer-facing status pages. The data is deliberately public — it is the same information displayed on the utility's customer outage map website. The bucket contains no operational grid data, no BES topology, and no BCSI.
why_misclassified: EC-12: scanner applies uniform HIGH severity to all public S3 buckets in NERC CIP accounts without evaluating whether the data is intentionally public customer-facing information.
detection_signal: S3 bucket energy-outage-maps-public allows public access — HIGH: public storage in NERC CIP operational environment
ground_truth: Bucket contains customer-facing outage maps and ETR data — same information on the utility's public website. No BCSI, no grid topology, no operational credentials. Public access is intentional by design.
remediation_impact: Making the bucket private would break the public outage map service used by millions of utility customers during outage events.

scenario: Azure Function App grid-weather-api has environment variable OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY with a value matching an API key pattern. CSPM flags HIGH for credentials in environment variables. OpenWeatherMap provides weather forecast data used for wind/solar generation forecasting. The API key is a read-only public weather data subscription key with no write access to any system. Exposure of this key would result only in unauthorized use of the weather data subscription, not access to energy systems.
why_misclassified: EC-29: scanner matches API key patterns without distinguishing between security-sensitive credentials and third-party read-only service keys with negligible impact if exposed.
detection_signal: Function App grid-weather-api OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY detected — HIGH: API credential in environment variable
ground_truth: OpenWeatherMap key provides read-only access to public weather forecast data. No energy system access possible. Worst case: unauthorized weather API calls consuming the subscription quota.
remediation_impact: Moving to Key Vault is good practice but the risk is subscription quota abuse, not energy system compromise. The key has no access to any internal systems.

scenario: GKE cluster energy-analytics-gke has the Kubernetes API server public endpoint enabled. CSPM reports HIGH. The public endpoint access is restricted to three specific CIDRs via masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig: NOC VPN egress (203.0.113.0/28), CI/CD runner IPs (198.51.100.0/27), and the corporate perimeter (10.0.0.0/22 translated via Cloud NAT). The API server is effectively locked to three known IP ranges, not broadly public.
why_misclassified: EC-42: public endpoint enabled but masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig restricts to three specific CIDRs. Scanner flags public endpoint presence without evaluating the authorized networks restriction.
detection_signal: GKE cluster energy-analytics-gke public API endpoint enabled — HIGH: Kubernetes API server internet-accessible
ground_truth: masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig restricts to NOC VPN, CI/CD, and corporate IPs. Private endpoint handles node communication. Attack surface limited to known CIDRs.
remediation_impact: Disabling public endpoint requires private endpoint + VPN for all kubectl operations. masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig provides equivalent restriction with less operational friction.

scenario: EC2 instance modbus-dnp3-translator does not use Nitro enclave. CSPM reports MEDIUM for lack of enclave isolation on industrial protocol translator. This instance runs Modbus RTU-to-DNP3 protocol conversion for legacy field devices. Nitro enclaves are designed for sensitive data processing (cryptographic operations, credentials), not generic protocol translation. The scanner is applying a blanket enclave recommendation to all EC2 instances regardless of workload type.
why_misclassified: EC-33: Nitro enclave recommendation applied uniformly without evaluating whether the workload involves sensitive data that enclaves protect. Protocol translation between Modbus and DNP3 does not process secrets or cryptographic material.
detection_signal: EC2 modbus-dnp3-translator not using Nitro enclave — MEDIUM: industrial protocol translator without enclave isolation
ground_truth: Nitro enclaves isolate sensitive computations involving secrets/keys. This instance does serial protocol framing conversion. No sensitive data requiring enclave-level isolation is processed. Recommendation is inapplicable for this workload type.
remediation_impact: Enabling Nitro enclave requires code refactoring to use enclave-specific SDK. Provides no security benefit for protocol translation workloads that don't process secrets.

scenario: GCP firewall rule allow-dnp3-master permits UDP 20000 inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 on the SCADA network. CSPM reports HIGH for broad DNP3 port exposure. UDP 20000 is the DNP3 application layer port used by Outstation Remote Terminal Units (RTUs) to report back to the DNP3 Master. Field RTUs are installed across hundreds of geographic locations with dynamic cellular carrier IPs. Restricting to a source CIDR would block RTUs that acquire new IPs after cellular reconnection.
why_misclassified: EC-06: DNP3 RTU telemetry uses dynamic cellular IPs — source IP restriction contradicts field deployment requirements. Scanner applies standard firewall policy without ICS protocol knowledge.
detection_signal: Firewall allow-dnp3-master UDP 20000 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: DNP3 SCADA master broadly open
ground_truth: RTUs across 340 field locations use cellular data connections with dynamic IPs. DNP3 application-layer authentication (DNP3-SA per IEEE 1815-2012) provides authentication independent of source IP. IP-based restriction would break RTU reporting during cellular failover.
remediation_impact: Restricting to ISP ASN CIDRs would require constant updates as cellular carrier IP ranges change. DNP3-SA application authentication is the appropriate security control for this architecture.

scenario: ECS task definition pmu-data-concentrator runs containers with privileged: true. CSPM flags HIGH for privileged containers. This container interfaces with a hardware PCI PMU (Phasor Measurement Unit) data acquisition card installed in the host EC2 instance. Privileged mode is required to access /dev/pmu0 hardware device. The container processes synchrophasor data at 60 samples/second for grid stability analysis. The PMU interface requires direct hardware device access unavailable in unprivileged containers.
why_misclassified: EC-27: hardware PMU device access requires kernel-level device permissions. Scanner applies blanket privileged container policy without hardware device access exception for ICS data acquisition.
detection_signal: ECS container pmu-data-concentrator privileged mode — HIGH: grid measurement container with kernel access
ground_truth: PMU hardware card requires privileged access to /dev/pmu0. Alternative unprivileged patterns (device plugins) are not available for custom PCI PMU hardware. Instance is a dedicated EC2 with no co-tenanted workloads.
remediation_impact: Removing privileged mode makes PMU hardware inaccessible, halting synchrophasor data collection. Grid stability analysis loses real-time frequency deviation data from this measurement point.

scenario: Azure SQL Server energy-ami-db has auditing to storage account disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for SQL without audit trail under NERC CIP. The SQL server has Microsoft Defender for SQL enabled with audit logs streaming to Log Analytics workspace energy-security-logs. Logs are retained 7 years per NERC CIP-007 R5 requirements through a Log Analytics archive tier policy.
why_misclassified: EC-19: scanner checks only for storage account audit destination. Auditing via Defender for SQL to Log Analytics is an equivalent and NERC CIP-accepted audit mechanism.
detection_signal: Azure SQL energy-ami-db storage audit disabled — HIGH: AMI database audit trail missing under NERC CIP
ground_truth: Defender for SQL streams audit logs to energy-security-logs Log Analytics. 7-year retention via archive tier. NERC CIP-007 R5 logging requirements are met via the Log Analytics destination.
remediation_impact: Adding storage account as secondary destination is optional hygiene. Primary audit trail via Defender for SQL + Log Analytics is NERC CIP compliant.

scenario: DynamoDB table energy-ami-setpoints does not use a VPC Endpoint. CSPM reports HIGH for DynamoDB without private connectivity in NERC CIP environment. The table is accessed from Lambda functions that run in the VPC. The VPC has a DynamoDB Gateway Endpoint configured, so Lambda traffic to DynamoDB routes through the AWS network backbone without traversing the internet. Gateway Endpoints for DynamoDB are a distinct architecture from Interface Endpoints.
why_misclassified: EC-09: scanner requires Interface VPC Endpoint without recognizing that DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints provide equivalent private network routing at no additional cost. Gateway Endpoints are the recommended DynamoDB private access pattern.
detection_signal: DynamoDB energy-ami-setpoints no VPC Interface Endpoint — HIGH: setpoint database without private connectivity
ground_truth: VPC Gateway Endpoint for DynamoDB configured. Lambda traffic routes through AWS backbone network. No internet traversal. NERC CIP network segmentation requirements met via Gateway Endpoint architecture.
remediation_impact: Adding a DynamoDB Interface Endpoint ($0.01/hour) alongside the existing Gateway Endpoint provides no additional security benefit. Gateway Endpoint achieves private routing without cost.

scenario: Azure Management Group energy-operations has a cross-subscription policy assignment granting Reader access to subscription energy-regulatory-reporting from the energy-operations subscription. CSPM flags HIGH for cross-subscription access. The regulatory reporting subscription needs read access to operational data for FERC compliance report generation. Cross-subscription Reader is the approved Azure pattern for read-only regulatory audit access — it has no write capabilities.
why_misclassified: EC-41: cross-subscription access treated as uniformly high-risk without evaluating read-only scope or documented regulatory business justification. Reader role with no write capability is appropriate for regulatory reporting access.
detection_signal: Cross-subscription Reader access energy-regulatory-reporting on energy-operations — HIGH: cross-subscription access without documented justification
ground_truth: FERC Order 887 requires utilities to provide regulatory access to operational data for compliance reporting. Cross-subscription Reader is the documented access method. No write permissions granted. Assignment approved through utility's NERC CIP access change management process.
remediation_impact: Removing cross-subscription access would prevent FERC compliance report generation, creating a regulatory violation. Access is documented in NERC CIP access change management log.

scenario: Compute instance energy-ems-legacy-connector uses metadata endpoint without required Metadata-Flavor header. CSPM flags MEDIUM for SSRF-vulnerable metadata access. This instance runs a 2019-era energy management system integration connector that pre-dates the metadata header requirement. The instance is in a private subnet with no external IP, and inbound access is only from the internal EMS network CIDR 10.30.0.0/16. SSRF requires serving attacker content to the instance, which the network isolation prevents.
why_misclassified: EC-44: metadata header requirement addresses SSRF risk that requires network access to serve attacker-controlled content. Private subnet with no external IP and restricted inbound eliminates the SSRF attack path.
detection_signal: Compute instance energy-ems-legacy-connector legacy metadata access — MEDIUM: SSRF risk in energy management system
ground_truth: Instance has no external IP, private subnet, access only from 10.30.0.0/16 EMS network. SSRF attack requires prior network compromise to exploit. Scheduled for connector rebuild in H2 2025.
remediation_impact: Connector rebuild is on roadmap. Network isolation provides compensating control. This is a hygiene improvement, not an active risk given the network topology.

scenario: AKS cluster energy-analytics-aks has the kubernetes-dashboard add-on enabled. CSPM reports HIGH for exposed dashboard in IEC 62443 environment. The dashboard uses ClusterIP service (no external LoadBalancer), has no ingress, and no associated public IP. Access requires kubectl port-forward with valid kubeconfig credentials. The IEC 62443 security zone concept is satisfied by the Kubernetes RBAC controls on the dashboard namespace.
why_misclassified: EC-50: dashboard add-on enabled but no external access path exists. Scanner flags add-on presence regardless of service type. No network path from ICS zone to dashboard without authenticated kubectl.
detection_signal: AKS energy-analytics-aks kubernetes-dashboard enabled — HIGH: dashboard accessible in IEC 62443 energy environment
ground_truth: ClusterIP service, no external exposure. kubectl port-forward with kubeconfig required. Dashboard used by analytics team for internal monitoring. IEC 62443 RBAC controls applied.
remediation_impact: Disabling dashboard removes internal monitoring capability. Should be removed in next cluster upgrade as best practice, but current exposure is informational.

scenario: Artifact Registry repository energy-ot-containers has container analysis disabled. CSPM reports HIGH. The SCADA container images are built in a GitLab CI pipeline with Anchore Engine vulnerability scanning. CRITICAL and HIGH CVEs block deployment. Images are rebuilt weekly. Artifact Registry scanning would duplicate the CI-level Anchore gate.
why_misclassified: EC-04: CI pipeline vulnerability scanning (Anchore) is an equivalent control. Scanner requires platform-level registry scanning without evaluating upstream CI gates.
detection_signal: Artifact Registry energy-ot-containers vulnerability scanning disabled — HIGH: SCADA containers without vulnerability scanning
ground_truth: Anchore Engine in GitLab CI scans all images. CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs block push. Weekly rebuild ensures currency. Artifact Registry scanning duplicates existing CI controls.
remediation_impact: Enabling Artifact Registry scanning creates duplicate vulnerability reports alongside Anchore findings, requiring alert deduplication tooling.

scenario: Azure App Service energy-ems-api has Easy Auth disabled. CSPM flags HIGH for unauthenticated API in IEC 62443 environment. The EMS API uses SAML 2.0 authentication with the utility's on-premises ADFS identity provider — a common pattern for utilities with existing Active Directory infrastructure. Easy Auth is incompatible with SAML 2.0 / ADFS. Authentication is enforced via OWIN SAML middleware.
why_misclassified: EC-43: Easy Auth supports Microsoft Identity (Azure AD, MSAL). SAML 2.0 with on-prem ADFS requires application-layer SAML middleware. Scanner equates Easy Auth disabled with no authentication.
detection_signal: App Service energy-ems-api Easy Auth disabled — HIGH: EMS API unauthenticated
ground_truth: SAML 2.0 authentication with on-premises ADFS enforced via OWIN middleware. Every request requires valid SAML assertion from utility ADFS. Easy Auth is incompatible with SAML 2.0.
remediation_impact: Enabling Easy Auth breaks SAML 2.0 ADFS authentication. Migration to Azure AD (Entra ID) with SAML federation is a multi-quarter project requiring Active Directory synchronization changes.

scenario: GCS bucket energy-nerc-audit-logs uses Object Retention (Object Lock equivalent in GCS) with 7-year WORM retention per NERC CIP-007 R5. CSPM reports MEDIUM for bucket without additional deletion protection. GCS Object Retention makes objects non-deletable before retention expiry even by storage admins. The additional deletion protection recommended by the scanner is redundant when WORM retention is enforced at the object level.
why_misclassified: EC-18: scanner recommends deletion protection without checking GCS Object Retention policy. Object Retention in GCS provides immutability equivalent to or stronger than the recommended control.
detection_signal: GCS energy-nerc-audit-logs additional deletion protection not configured — MEDIUM: NERC CIP audit logs at deletion risk
ground_truth: GCS Object Retention (WORM) active with 7-year retention per NERC CIP-007 R5. Objects cannot be deleted before retention expiry. NERC CIP audit log immutability requirements are satisfied.
remediation_impact: Adding redundant deletion controls on WORM-protected objects is unnecessary and provides no additional compliance benefit.

scenario: Azure Policy assignment deny-public-storage-accounts has an exemption for storage account st-energy-public-reports. CSPM reports HIGH for policy exemption in NERC CIP account. The exemption covers the storage account that publishes FERC-required public reliability reports. FERC regulations mandate public accessibility of specific operational reports. The exemption is documented in the NERC CIP access change management system with FERC citation.
why_misclassified: EC-40: policy exemptions are flagged as high-risk violations without evaluating whether the exemption is justified by a higher-level regulatory requirement (FERC public disclosure mandate).
detection_signal: Policy deny-public-storage-accounts exemption for st-energy-public-reports — HIGH: NERC CIP storage policy exemption
ground_truth: FERC reliability reporting mandates public access to specific grid reliability reports. The policy exemption is documented with FERC regulatory citation and approved through NERC CIP change management. Exemption scope is limited to the public reports storage account.
remediation_impact: Removing the exemption would prevent FERC compliance report publication, creating a regulatory violation. Exemption is required and properly documented.

scenario: Cloud Run service energy-meter-api allows unauthenticated invocation. CSPM reports HIGH. The API receives IEC 61968/61970 Common Information Model (CIM) meter data from utility AMI head-end systems. These head-end systems are third-party vendor products that authenticate using HMAC-SHA256 application-layer signatures rather than Google Cloud identity tokens. The API validates every request signature before processing.
why_misclassified: EC-34: allUsers Cloud Run permission required for non-Google systems that cannot perform OIDC token flows. AMI head-end systems use HMAC application authentication. Cloud Run unauthenticated + HMAC validation is equivalent to authenticated + no HMAC.
detection_signal: Cloud Run energy-meter-api allUsers invoker — HIGH: AMI metering API unauthenticated
ground_truth: HMAC-SHA256 application authentication validated on every request. AMI head-end vendor hardware cannot perform Google OIDC flows. Authentication enforced at application layer.
remediation_impact: Enabling Cloud Run IAM auth would break metering data ingestion from AMI head-end systems that don't support OIDC.

scenario: Azure VM energy-pi-server does not use JIT VM access. CSPM reports MEDIUM. The OSIsoft PI historian server has no RDP/SSH ports open in the NSG — all administrative access uses Azure Bastion with NERC CIP privileged account credentials. No management ports exposed means JIT has no ports to protect.
why_misclassified: EC-21: JIT protects open management ports. With no open ports, JIT is irrelevant. Scanner applies JIT check regardless of NSG port status.
detection_signal: VM energy-pi-server JIT access not configured — MEDIUM: PI historian without just-in-time access
ground_truth: No SSH/RDP open. Azure Bastion + NERC CIP privileged account required. JIT provides no benefit when no management ports are exposed.
remediation_impact: Enabling JIT on a VM with no open ports creates an empty policy with no effect.

scenario: GCP log sink energy-nerc-audit-sink routes to a regional GCS bucket (us-central1). CSPM reports MEDIUM for single-region audit log storage. The energy utility operates exclusively in us-central1. All GCP resources are in this region. Multi-region log storage would increase costs with no additional resilience benefit for a single-region deployment.
why_misclassified: EC-32: multi-region audit storage is best practice for multi-region deployments. Single-region utility with all assets in us-central1 has no workloads to log in other regions.
detection_signal: Log sink energy-nerc-audit-sink single-region storage — MEDIUM: NERC CIP audit logs not geographically redundant
ground_truth: All GCP resources in us-central1. Multi-region bucket would store duplicates of single-region log data. NERC CIP audit log requirements are met with regional retention and backup.
remediation_impact: Multi-region GCS bucket would increase storage costs by ~$50/month for duplicate log copies from empty additional regions.

scenario: SQS queue energy-public-alerts does not use KMS CMK. CSPM reports MEDIUM. The queue carries public-facing outage alerts (same content as the utility's public outage map). All messages are non-sensitive public information. The queue uses SSE-SQS (AES-256) but not a customer-managed KMS key.
why_misclassified: EC-37: CMK requirement applied uniformly without evaluating whether queue content is sensitive. Public outage alerts are regulatory disclosure content — CMK adds no security for publicly available data.
detection_signal: SQS energy-public-alerts no KMS CMK — MEDIUM: outage alert queue without CMK
ground_truth: Queue contains public outage notifications. SSE-SQS provides at-rest encryption. CMK adds key custody overhead for data simultaneously posted on the utility's public website.
remediation_impact: CMK adds KMS API costs for encrypting publicly available data. SSE-SQS is sufficient for non-sensitive content.

scenario: Compute instance energy-weather-api-egress has an ephemeral external IP. CSPM reports HIGH for external IP in NERC CIP environment. This instance is a weather data API client that pulls forecast data for renewable generation prediction. The external IP is egress-only — no inbound firewall rules accept connections from the internet. The instance uses the external IP to connect to OpenWeatherMap and NOAA APIs. All inbound rules are explicitly deny.
why_misclassified: EC-05: scanner flags external IP presence as high-risk without distinguishing between inbound-accessible and egress-only external IPs. No inbound rules + external IP = egress-only, not exposed.
detection_signal: Compute instance energy-weather-api-egress has external IP — HIGH: SCADA-adjacent instance with internet exposure
ground_truth: External IP used for outbound-only weather API calls (OpenWeatherMap, NOAA). No inbound firewall rules. No external access path to the instance. External IP is an egress-only requirement for third-party weather API integration.
remediation_impact: Removing external IP requires Cloud NAT configuration for outbound weather API calls. Functionally equivalent but adds network complexity. Risk is effectively zero given no inbound rules.

scenario: Secrets Manager secret /energy/ot/abb-relay-api-key has rotation disabled. CSPM reports HIGH. The ABB protection relay configuration API key is issued by ABB's vendor portal. ABB does not provide an API for programmatic key rotation — rotation requires logging into the ABB portal and manually issuing a new key. Automated rotation is technically infeasible with the vendor's tooling.
why_misclassified: EC-55: automatic rotation requirement applied without accounting for vendor API constraints. Third-party ICS vendor APIs often lack rotation automation support.
detection_signal: Secrets Manager /energy/ot/abb-relay-api-key rotation disabled — HIGH: protection relay API key without rotation
ground_truth: ABB relay API does not expose a key rotation endpoint. Manual rotation documented in NERC CIP change management with 90-day calendar reminder. Last rotated 60 days ago. Vendor contacted about API rotation support — roadmap item for ABB 2025.
remediation_impact: No technical automation possible. Manual rotation process with calendar enforcement is the available control. Consider rotating more frequently (60 days) given automation gap.

scenario: Azure SQL Server energy-generation-forecast has auditing to storage disabled. CSPM flags HIGH. Auditing routes to Log Analytics workspace energy-nerc-logs via Defender for SQL, with 7-year archive retention. The NERC CIP-007 R5 audit trail requirement is satisfied by the Log Analytics destination.
why_misclassified: EC-28: scanner checks only for storage account audit destination, missing Log Analytics-based auditing as a valid NERC CIP audit trail.
detection_signal: SQL energy-generation-forecast storage audit disabled — HIGH: generation forecast database audit missing
ground_truth: Defender for SQL routes audit logs to energy-nerc-logs Log Analytics. 7-year retention compliant with NERC CIP-007 R5. Storage audit is unnecessary given Log Analytics coverage.
remediation_impact: Adding storage audit destination is optional. Log Analytics provides NERC CIP-compliant audit trail.

scenario: DynamoDB table energy-realtime-measurements has PITR disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM. The table stores grid frequency and voltage measurements with 15-second TTL — data is ephemeral by design, consumed by the real-time grid monitoring application. Historical measurement data is archived to S3 Glacier by the analytics pipeline within 60 seconds. PITR recovery of 15-second measurement windows has no operational value.
why_misclassified: EC-24: PITR recommended for all DynamoDB tables without distinguishing sub-minute ephemeral measurement stores from persistent databases.
detection_signal: DynamoDB energy-realtime-measurements PITR disabled — MEDIUM: real-time grid measurements without backup
ground_truth: 15-second TTL — all data auto-expires. Analytics pipeline archives to S3 Glacier within 60 seconds. PITR recovery of 15-second measurement data has no value; archived data is the long-term record.
remediation_impact: PITR for 15-second TTL data adds cost for snapshots of data that is immediately superseded. S3 Glacier archive is the recovery mechanism.

scenario: Key Vault kv-energy-scada-legacy shows softDeleteEnabled: false in API response. CSPM reports HIGH. The vault was created before Microsoft's February 2025 retroactive enforcement — soft delete is actually active (Microsoft applied it to all vaults) but the API field still shows legacy false status.
why_misclassified: EC-13: Azure API inconsistency for pre-enforcement vaults shows legacy false value. Soft delete protection is active regardless of the API response field.
detection_signal: Key Vault kv-energy-scada-legacy softDeleteEnabled=false — HIGH: SCADA keys without deletion protection
ground_truth: Microsoft enforced soft delete retroactively in February 2025. Actual protection is active. API response is a legacy field inconsistency for pre-enforcement vaults.
remediation_impact: No action needed for soft delete — already active. File Azure support ticket to correct API response. Add CSPM suppression for legacy pre-enforcement vaults.

scenario: EC2 instance energy-pi-connector runs with IMDSv1 enabled (http-tokens=optional). CSPM reports MEDIUM for SSRF-vulnerable metadata. The OSIsoft PI connector uses a 2019-era AWS SDK that predates IMDSv2 session tokens. The instance is in a private subnet (no external IP), security group restricts inbound to the PI historian server IP (10.40.50.20/32 only). SSRF attack surface is zero given single-source inbound restriction.
why_misclassified: EC-44: IMDSv1 retained due to SDK legacy, mitigated by single-IP inbound restriction. SSRF requires serving attacker content to the instance — impossible with single-source security group.
detection_signal: EC2 energy-pi-connector IMDSv1 enabled — MEDIUM: PI connector SSRF risk
ground_truth: Private subnet, external IP absent, inbound only from single PI historian IP. SSRF requires the PI historian (10.40.50.20) to serve attacker-controlled content — extremely unlikely. SDK upgrade scheduled for H2 2025.
remediation_impact: SDK upgrade to IMDSv2-compatible version in H2 2025. Current network isolation renders this informational.

scenario: Azure SQL Server energy-load-forecast-db has Defender for SQL disabled. CSPM reports HIGH. The database is read-only, Private Link only, Azure AD auth only. Load forecast data is ML model output — not operational data or BCSI. API layer uses parameterized queries with WAF. SQL injection surface is effectively sealed.
why_misclassified: EC-47: Defender for SQL is most valuable for internet-exposed, writeable, or multi-tenant databases. This read-only, private-only database with sealed SQL injection surface has minimal threat surface.
detection_signal: Azure SQL energy-load-forecast-db Defender for SQL disabled — HIGH: forecast database without threat detection
ground_truth: Read-only, Private Link, Azure AD auth. Parameterized queries + WAF. Threat surface is sealed. Defender for SQL would generate alerts for a database with no exploitable attack surface.
remediation_impact: Enabling Defender for SQL adds $15/month for threat detection on a database with no SQL injection surface and no external access.

scenario: Cloud Function energy-rtd-processor uses Python 3.8 which is EOL. CSPM reports HIGH. The Real-Time Dispatch processor integrates with the grid operator's EMS via proprietary Python library (GridAPI v2.1) which is certified only for Python 3.8. Vendor (GE Vernova) certification for Python 3.12 is in progress. Non-internet-facing function (triggered by Pub/Sub).
why_misclassified: EC-52: deprecated runtime flagged as HIGH without accounting for ISV certification constraint blocking upgrade. Risk is MEDIUM — real but constrained by vendor certification cycle.
detection_signal: Cloud Function energy-rtd-processor Python 3.8 EOL — HIGH: real-time dispatch on deprecated runtime
ground_truth: GE Vernova GridAPI v2.1 certified only for Python 3.8. Vendor Python 3.12 certification estimated Q3 2025. Function is not internet-facing. Risk is MEDIUM with documented upgrade path.
remediation_impact: Python 3.12 upgrade blocked by ISV certification. Interim: isolate function in dedicated Cloud Run environment with enhanced monitoring.

scenario: AKS cluster energy-ot-aks uses Azure CNI with Cilium as the network plugin. CSPM reports HIGH for network policy disabled. Azure CNI with Cilium implements eBPF-based network policies natively. The Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate is disabled because Cilium handles all enforcement at eBPF layer — the standard NetworkPolicy feature gate is not required when Cilium is the CNI.
why_misclassified: EC-10: Cilium eBPF enforces network policies independently of the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate. Scanner checks feature gate status without detecting Cilium CNI enforcement.
detection_signal: AKS energy-ot-aks network policy disabled — HIGH: no pod-level isolation in OT analytics cluster
ground_truth: Azure CNI with Cilium provides eBPF-based network policy enforcement. NetworkPolicy feature gate disabled because Cilium handles enforcement. Pod-level isolation is active.
remediation_impact: Enabling Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate on a Cilium cluster may create policy conflicts. Cilium enforcement already provides equivalent isolation.

scenario: AWS Config rule restricted-ssh reports EC2 instance energy-rtd-server as noncompliant. The instance requires SSH access for GE Vernova EMS support technicians from their support network (198.51.100.0/27 — 32 hosts). The Config rule restricted-ssh flags any inbound TCP 22 without evaluating source CIDR specificity.
why_misclassified: EC-30: coarse Config rule triggers on any inbound SSH. SSH from a /27 vendor support network (32 hosts) is meaningfully different from SSH from 0.0.0.0/0.
detection_signal: Config rule restricted-ssh noncompliant energy-rtd-server — HIGH: RTD server SSH noncompliant
ground_truth: SSH from GE Vernova support CIDR 198.51.100.0/27 (32 hosts). Config rule is overly coarse. Vendor support access is documented in NERC CIP change management.
remediation_impact: Deploy custom Config rule evaluating source CIDR specificity. Suppress coarse restricted-ssh for documented vendor support CIDRs.

scenario: Azure Managed Disk energy-ems-data-disk uses Platform Managed Keys. CSPM reports HIGH for no CMK. The disk stores load forecast model outputs — ML results, not BCSI. NERC CIP-011 BCSI encryption requirements apply to BES Cyber System Information. Load forecast model outputs are operational planning data, not BCSI under NERC CIP-011 definitions.
why_misclassified: EC-49: CMK requirement applied uniformly without evaluating NERC CIP BCSI classification. PMK is acceptable for non-BCSI data.
detection_signal: Managed Disk energy-ems-data-disk no CMK — HIGH: EMS disk without customer key control
ground_truth: Disk contains load forecast model outputs. Not BCSI under NERC CIP-011 (BCSI is topology, protection settings, access procedures — not ML outputs). PMK encryption meets requirements for this data classification.
remediation_impact: CMK migration requires disk replacement and downtime. NERC CIP assessor has accepted PMK for non-BCSI EMS data.

scenario: GKE node pool energy-scada-np has Workload Identity disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM. This node pool runs legacy SCADA integration software that uses service account JSON keys mounted as K8s secrets. The application predates Workload Identity. Key rotated every 30 days. Node pool in isolated VPC with no internet access.
why_misclassified: EC-38: Workload Identity absence is real risk but MEDIUM severity overstated given 30-day rotation and network isolation. Migration in Q2 roadmap.
detection_signal: GKE node pool energy-scada-np Workload Identity disabled — MEDIUM: SCADA pods using service account keys
ground_truth: SA key rotated every 30 days, mounted via K8s secret. Node pool in isolated VPC. Workload Identity migration scheduled for Q2. Risk is LOW-MEDIUM given compensating controls.
remediation_impact: Workload Identity migration requires code changes for metadata server credential flow. 2-sprint effort with SCADA regression testing.

scenario: Azure App Gateway energy-api-appgw WAF in Detection mode. CSPM reports MEDIUM. WAF moved to Detection mode 4 weeks ago during upgrade of the NERC CIP compliance reporting API which added new request patterns. 623 false positives from CIM XML payloads in 4 weeks. Custom WAF exclusions being developed. Prevention target: 2 weeks.
why_misclassified: EC-47: Detection mode is temporary tuning state. 623 false positives from legitimate CIM XML payloads justify tuning before Prevention. Scanner flags mode without tuning context.
detection_signal: App Gateway energy-api-appgw WAF Detection mode — MEDIUM: energy API WAF not blocking
ground_truth: Detection mode temporary during CIM XML request pattern tuning (4 weeks). 623 false positives would disrupt NERC CIP compliance reporting if Prevention mode were forced. Custom exclusions in development. Prevention target in 2 weeks.
remediation_impact: Prevention mode now would block 623 legitimate CIM XML requests/week, disrupting NERC CIP compliance report generation.

scenario: Cloud Function energy-amt-processor uses Node.js 16 which is EOL. CSPM reports HIGH. The Advanced Metering Technology processor uses a proprietary Node.js module (UtilitySDK 3.x) which is certified only for Node.js 16 by the meter vendor (Itron). Itron certification for Node.js 20 estimated Q2 2025. Function triggered via Pub/Sub — not internet-facing.
why_misclassified: EC-54: EOL runtime is a real risk but HIGH severity doesn't account for ISV certification constraint. Risk is MEDIUM with active upgrade path pending vendor certification.
detection_signal: Cloud Function energy-amt-processor Node.js 16 EOL — HIGH: AMT processing on deprecated runtime
ground_truth: Itron UtilitySDK 3.x certified for Node.js 16 only. Vendor Node.js 20 certification in Q2 2025. Not internet-facing. Risk is MEDIUM — real but vendor-constrained.
remediation_impact: Node.js 20 upgrade blocked by Itron SDK certification. Interim: isolate function, enable enhanced monitoring, track Itron certification progress.

scenario: AWS account energy-ot-prod has IAM user root-monitor with an active access key. CSPM reports CRITICAL for root account access key. Security review confirms root-monitor is an IAM user (not the AWS root account) named by a former admin following an old naming convention. Actual AWS root account has no access keys and MFA enabled. The IAM user root-monitor performs health monitoring.
why_misclassified: EC-39: scanner matches on username 'root' rather than the actual AWS root account identity (no IAM path). IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account.
detection_signal: IAM user root-monitor active access key — CRITICAL: root account key in energy OT account
ground_truth: IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account. Actual AWS root: no access keys, MFA enabled. Naming is misleading but finding is about an IAM user, not root.
remediation_impact: Rename IAM user to energy-health-monitor. Rotate access key per 90-day standard. No root account remediation needed.

scenario: Azure VM energy-rtu-manager serial console is enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for serial console access in NERC CIP environment. Azure Serial Console requires valid Azure AD authentication and roles/Virtual Machine Contributor or higher. The serial console is used by NERC CIP-approved operations staff for out-of-band RTU management during network outages. Azure RBAC controls access — it is not an unauthenticated channel.
why_misclassified: EC-26: Azure Serial Console requires IAM authentication. Not an unauthenticated access vector. Scanner flags serial console without noting Azure RBAC requirement.
detection_signal: VM energy-rtu-manager serial console enabled — MEDIUM: RTU manager serial access in NERC CIP environment
ground_truth: Azure Serial Console requires Azure AD credentials and VM Contributor role. Access controlled by NERC CIP-approved role assignments. Used for emergency RTU management during network outages.
remediation_impact: Disabling serial console removes emergency out-of-band management path. Risk is informational given Azure AD authentication requirement.

scenario: GCP Cloud DNS managed zone energy-internal.ot is a private zone with DNSSEC disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM. This is an internal DNS zone resolvable only within the energy-ot VPC. DNSSEC protects against internet-based DNS spoofing attacks. A private zone not exposed to the public DNS namespace has no attack surface that DNSSEC addresses.
why_misclassified: EC-48: DNSSEC check applied to all DNS zones regardless of public/private classification. Private zones accessible only within a VPC have no internet-facing DNSSEC attack surface.
detection_signal: Cloud DNS energy-internal.ot DNSSEC disabled — MEDIUM: OT internal DNS without DNSSEC
ground_truth: Private DNS zone, VPC-internal only. DNSSEC protects public internet DNS cache poisoning — not applicable to private zones.
remediation_impact: GCP supports DNSSEC on public zones only. DNSSEC cannot be enabled on Cloud DNS private zones. Finding is technically unremediate-able as stated.

scenario: AWS Inspector v2 not enabled for EC2 in energy-scada-prod account. CSPM reports HIGH. The account uses Qualys with SSM agent for all EC2 instances — continuous vulnerability scanning with CVE correlation feeding the utility's vulnerability management workflow. Inspector would duplicate Qualys coverage and create parallel alert queues.
why_misclassified: EC-44: third-party VM platform (Qualys) provides equivalent coverage. Scanner requires AWS-native Inspector without evaluating existing third-party scanning controls.
detection_signal: AWS Inspector v2 not enabled — HIGH: energy SCADA production without vulnerability scanning
ground_truth: Qualys Cloud Agent provides continuous scanning on all EC2 instances. Inspector would duplicate findings. Qualys is the enterprise VM platform feeding the utility NERC CIP vulnerability management process.
remediation_impact: Inspector alongside Qualys creates duplicate scanning overhead requiring finding deduplication. Qualys provides equivalent or superior NERC CIP-aligned coverage.

scenario: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Enhanced Security is disabled for the energy-ot subscription. CSPM reports HIGH for missing Defender coverage. The utility uses Claroty OT security platform integrated with Azure Sentinel for OT/ICS threat detection — purpose-built for ICS environments. Defender for Cloud standard tier is not NERC CIP-certified for OT environments. Claroty provides CIP-compliant ICS network monitoring.
why_misclassified: EC-43: scanner requires Microsoft-native security tooling without evaluating specialized OT security platforms (Claroty) that provide equivalent or superior coverage for ICS environments.
detection_signal: Defender for Cloud Enhanced not enabled — HIGH: energy OT subscription without enhanced threat detection
ground_truth: Claroty OT security platform provides ICS-specific threat detection integrated with Azure Sentinel. NERC CIP compliance validated with Claroty. Defender for Cloud is not specifically designed for OT/ICS environments.
remediation_impact: Enabling Defender for Cloud alongside Claroty creates duplicate alert queues requiring ICS-aware deduplication. Claroty provides OT-specific detection that Defender for Cloud lacks.

scenario: Security group sg-modbus-gateway allows TCP 502 (Modbus) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0. CSPM reports HIGH for Modbus port broadly accessible. The Modbus TCP gateway uses Modbus Security extension (TLS-wrapped Modbus per ENISA recommendation) and requires client certificate authentication at the TLS layer. Remote Terminal Units authenticate with device certificates before Modbus commands are processed.
why_misclassified: EC-08: scanner evaluates port reachability only, not the Modbus Security TLS layer and certificate requirement. The industrial protocol appears 'open' but enforces TLS mutual authentication.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup sg-modbus-gateway TCP 502 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: Modbus gateway broadly accessible
ground_truth: Modbus Security (TLS 1.2+ with device certificates) required. Unauthenticated connections rejected at TLS handshake. Dynamic IPs of field RTUs prevent source CIDR restriction.
remediation_impact: Source IP restriction would break Modbus telemetry from RTUs with dynamic cellular IPs. TLS mutual auth provides stronger authentication than IP allowlisting.

scenario: Azure Storage account stenergypublicota stores firmware packages for smart meter OTA updates. Uses PMK encryption. CSPM reports HIGH. Firmware packages are AES-256 encrypted and ECDSA-signed with the utility's code signing certificate. Meters validate firmware signatures before flashing. Even if packages were downloaded by an attacker, tampered packages would be rejected by the meter's secure bootloader.
why_misclassified: EC-31: CMK requirement applied without evaluating that firmware packages are cryptographically signed at the application layer. Content integrity enforced by meter secure bootloader makes storage-level key custody secondary.
detection_signal: Storage account stenergypublicota PMK encryption — HIGH: smart meter firmware without CMK
ground_truth: Firmware packages cryptographically signed (ECDSA) and validated by meter secure bootloader. PMK storage encryption is sufficient given application-layer signing chain. Tampering would be detected and rejected by meter hardware.
remediation_impact: CMK migration adds key vault dependency and operational overhead for public OTA distribution storage. Signing chain provides content integrity regardless of storage encryption key type.

scenario: Compute instance energy-sei-relay runs without Shielded VM. CSPM reports MEDIUM. This VM runs SEL (Schweitzer Engineering Labs) relay management software that requires specific Linux kernel modules for SEL serial port hardware. The SEL kernel modules are unsigned — incompatible with Shielded VM Secure Boot. SEL has not released Secure Boot-compatible kernel module versions.
why_misclassified: EC-33: specialized relay management hardware drivers incompatible with Shielded VM. Scanner applies blanket Shielded VM requirement without hardware driver signing exceptions.
detection_signal: Compute instance energy-sei-relay Shielded VM disabled — MEDIUM: protection relay management VM without boot integrity
ground_truth: SEL serial port kernel modules are unsigned and incompatible with Secure Boot. Enabling Shielded VM makes the relay management software inoperable. SEL hardware requires specific unsigned kernel modules. Compensating: CIS-hardened image, TPM attestation at OS layer.
remediation_impact: Enabling Shielded VM Secure Boot prevents SEL relay software from loading. SEL roadmap for Secure Boot-compatible modules: H2 2025.

scenario: Azure Function App energy-rtd-websocket has CPU-always-on enabled. CSPM flags cost efficiency policy violation. The Real-Time Dispatch WebSocket function maintains persistent connections to grid operator systems for real-time dispatch instructions. Cold starts would drop active dispatch connections during generation events, causing missed dispatch instructions from ISO/RTO.
why_misclassified: EC-20: cost efficiency policy applied without evaluating functional requirement (persistent WebSocket for real-time generation dispatch). Cold start latency is unacceptable for real-time grid dispatch.
detection_signal: Function App energy-rtd-websocket CPU always-on — LOW: cost policy violation
ground_truth: WebSocket connections for ISO/RTO dispatch instructions require persistent CPU. Cold starts during generation events cause missed dispatch instructions — a reliability violation. CPU-always-on is functionally required.
remediation_impact: Disabling CPU-always-on causes cold start drops of active dispatch connections during generation control events. Loss of dispatch signal has NERC reliability implications.

scenario: GCS bucket energy-scada-artifacts does not have Uniform Bucket-Level Access enabled and allows legacy ACLs. CSPM reports HIGH for non-uniform access control. The bucket is accessed exclusively via VPC Service Controls perimeter — no access is possible from outside the VPC perimeter. Legacy ACLs apply only to object-level permissions within the perimeter-controlled bucket. VPC-SC prevents all external access regardless of ACL configuration.
why_misclassified: EC-17: legacy ACLs assessed without evaluating VPC Service Controls perimeter that prevents external access entirely. ACL configuration affects intra-perimeter access control, not external exposure.
detection_signal: GCS bucket energy-scada-artifacts legacy ACLs enabled — HIGH: SCADA artifacts bucket non-uniform access control
ground_truth: VPC Service Controls perimeter prevents all external access. Legacy ACLs affect intra-perimeter object permissions only. External exposure is zero regardless of ACL configuration. Uniform bucket-level access migration is good practice.
remediation_impact: Enabling uniform bucket-level access is correct hygiene and low risk. However, active security risk is zero given VPC-SC perimeter.

scenario: AWS Organizations SCP deny-direct-internet-access has an exception for account energy-weather-ingestion. CSPM reports HIGH for SCP exception in NERC CIP organization. The exception allows the weather data ingestion account to call external weather APIs (NOAA, OpenWeatherMap) for renewable generation forecasting. The exception is scoped to a specific IAM role (WeatherAPIRole) and specific destination domains via service control condition keys.
why_misclassified: EC-40: SCP exception flagged as high-risk without evaluating scope restriction (specific role + domain conditions). Targeted exceptions for documented business requirements are a standard SCP pattern.
detection_signal: SCP deny-direct-internet-access exception for energy-weather-ingestion — HIGH: NERC CIP account with internet SCP exception
ground_truth: SCP exception scoped to WeatherAPIRole and specific weather API domains. Documented in NERC CIP change management with FERC renewable integration justification. Not a blanket internet exception.
remediation_impact: Removing the exception would block weather data ingestion required for renewable generation forecasting, affecting ISO/RTO reliability modeling.

scenario: Firestore database energy-ems-state does not use VPC Service Controls endpoint. CSPM reports HIGH for Firestore without private access in IEC 62443 environment. The Firestore database stores EMS UI state (user preferences, dashboard layouts). It is protected by VPC Service Controls perimeter and requires Firestore API credentials. No sensitive SCADA data stored in Firestore — only UI configuration.
why_misclassified: EC-09: private endpoint requirement applied without evaluating data sensitivity. EMS UI state (dashboard layouts) is not operationally sensitive. VPC-SC perimeter and API auth provide sufficient control for this data classification.
detection_signal: Firestore energy-ems-state no private endpoint — HIGH: EMS state database without private access
ground_truth: Firestore stores EMS UI preferences (not SCADA data). VPC-SC perimeter and API authentication provide access control. UI state has no IEC 62443 security zone classification requirement.
remediation_impact: Private endpoint for Firestore requires VPC peering and DNS configuration. Data sensitivity (UI preferences) does not justify the migration complexity.

scenario: S3 bucket energy-eqr-filings stores FERC Electric Quarterly Reports in a publicly readable bucket. CSPM reports HIGH for public S3 in NERC CIP account. EQR filings are mandatory public FERC submissions available on FERC's EQRS system. The bucket hosts the same data available at public FERC portals. No BCSI included — regulatory submissions are public by law.
why_misclassified: EC-12: blanket HIGH severity for public S3 in NERC CIP account without checking whether the data is publicly mandated regulatory content.
detection_signal: S3 energy-eqr-filings public read — HIGH: NERC CIP account public storage
ground_truth: FERC EQR filings are public regulatory submissions. Identical to data publicly available on FERC EQRS. No BCSI. Public access is a regulatory requirement.
remediation_impact: Making bucket private breaks FERC EQR publication workflow. Public access is legally required for regulatory filings.

scenario: Managed identity energy-data-pipeline has Storage Blob Data Contributor role on account st-energy-archive. CSPM flags excessive permissions. The archive pipeline ingests telemetry data AND must delete processed temporary files before retention window (GDPR for customer usage data). Contributor includes delete capability which is required for the pipeline's retention management function.
why_misclassified: EC-22: delete capability flagged as excessive without evaluating that retention management requires controlled deletion. Both write AND delete permissions are the minimum for the archive pipeline's dual role.
detection_signal: MI energy-data-pipeline Storage Blob Data Contributor — HIGH: archive pipeline with delete capability
ground_truth: Pipeline ingests data (requires write) and manages retention by deleting processed temporary objects (requires delete). Contributor is the minimum role for both operations. A custom role with specific blob actions is the ideal long-term solution.
remediation_impact: Downgrading to Blob Data Writer breaks retention management. Custom role with storage.blobs.write and storage.blobs.delete on specific containers is the ideal but requires 4-week change process.

scenario: Lambda function energy-solar-irradiance has environment variable SOLARGIS_API_KEY with a key pattern match. CSPM flags HIGH for credential in environment. SolarGIS provides satellite solar irradiance data for photovoltaic generation forecasting. The SolarGIS key is a read-only data subscription key with no access to energy systems. Compromise would allow unauthorized solar data queries, not energy system access.
why_misclassified: EC-29: scanner matches key patterns without distinguishing read-only third-party data subscription keys from security-sensitive credentials.
detection_signal: Lambda energy-solar-irradiance SOLARGIS_API_KEY detected — HIGH: API credential in environment
ground_truth: SolarGIS key provides read-only solar irradiance data. No energy system access. Worst case: unauthorized solar data API calls consuming the subscription quota.
remediation_impact: Moving to Secrets Manager is good practice but risk is data API quota abuse, not energy system compromise.

scenario: Azure Function App energy-meter-read-api has no network access restrictions configured. CSPM flags HIGH for broadly accessible API in NERC CIP environment.
