detection_signal: S3 bucket public access block: BlockPublicAcls=false, BlockPublicPolicy=false, IgnorePublicAcls=false, RestrictPublicBuckets=false
ground_truth: Bucket serves marketing content (HTML, images, PDFs). Content intentionally public for customer-facing promotions. No sensitive data present. Reviewed and approved by security team in campaign launch checklist.
remediation_impact: Making promotional landing pages private would break the holiday marketing campaign, impacting estimated $45M in campaign-attributed revenue.

scenario: GCP IAM binding shows service account 'marketplace-analytics@retail-marketplace.iam.gserviceaccount.com' with roles/bigquery.dataViewer on the retail-core project. Scanner flags HIGH for cross-project IAM binding.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC Service Controls + org-bounded): Both projects are within the same GCP organization and VPC Service Controls perimeter. Cross-project IAM for analytics is an approved architectural pattern for the marketplace data pipeline. The SA only reads non-PII aggregated seller metrics.
detection_signal: Cross-project IAM: marketplace SA has roles/bigquery.dataViewer on project retail-core
ground_truth: Both projects in organization retail-gcp-org. VPC Service Controls perimeter covers both. SA access scoped to BQ dataset 'seller_aggregates' with row-level security limiting to aggregated (non-PII) data only.
remediation_impact: Removing cross-project IAM breaks the marketplace seller analytics dashboard, impacting 47,000 marketplace sellers.

scenario: Azure CDN profile 'retail-cdn-eu' is configured to allow both HTTP and HTTPS traffic. Scanner flags MEDIUM for allowing plaintext HTTP connections to CDN endpoints serving EU e-commerce assets.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded): CDN rule engine is configured to redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS with 301 Moved Permanently. HTTP is technically allowed at the CDN layer for the redirect response only. End-to-end encryption is enforced via redirect rule, not by disabling HTTP.
detection_signal: Azure CDN endpoint retail-eu.azureedge.net: HTTP allowed (not HTTPS-only)
ground_truth: CDN rule: IF request-protocol=HTTP THEN redirect to https://{url} with 301. No content served over HTTP. HTTPS required for all actual content delivery. GDPR-compliant encryption in transit maintained.
remediation_impact: Disabling HTTP completely would break the redirect flow for users who type URLs without https:// prefix, degrading user experience.

scenario: GuardDuty flags HIGH for 'Unusual API call volume' from inventory-management-service. 94,000 ListObjects API calls in 10 minutes flagged as potential data exfiltration or reconnaissance.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated + known pattern): All API calls originate from the inventory sync service's known IP range (10.20.30.0/24). The call volume spike corresponds to the end-of-day inventory synchronization job that polls S3 for 94,000 SKU delta files.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: UnusualApiCallVolume — 94,000 S3:ListObjects in 10 minutes from inventory-svc
ground_truth: Nightly inventory sync job runs at 22:00 UTC, processing one S3 key per SKU for 94,000 product catalog items. Pattern repeats nightly. Source IP in known service CIDR. No data egress detected.
remediation_impact: Blocking inventory sync API access would break nightly inventory reconciliation, causing stock count inaccuracies in 3,400 stores.

scenario: DMS replication task 'retail-cdc-payments' flagged for SSL mode 'none' between source RDS (payment_db) and target Redshift (analytics_warehouse). HIGH finding for unencrypted data movement of payment records.
why_misclassified: EC-13 (app-layer encryption): Payment records are encrypted at the application layer before insertion into source DB. DMS replicates the already-encrypted ciphertext. SSL on DMS transport would double-encrypt data that is already encrypted at-rest values.
detection_signal: DMS replication task retail-cdc-payments: SslMode=none for source:payment-db-prod to target:analytics-redshift-prod
ground_truth: payment_db stores tokenized card data (Stripe payment_intent_id tokens, not PAN). Application-layer encryption of PII fields applied before write. DMS replicates encrypted tokens. Risk of unencrypted transport is low given data sensitivity of replicated fields.
remediation_impact: Enabling SSL on DMS adds CPU overhead and requires certificate rotation coordination, marginal benefit for already-tokenized data.

scenario: CSPM anomaly detection flags ElastiCache cluster 'retail-session-cache' for 400% memory utilization increase between 6 PM and 8 PM on a Sunday. Flags as potential cryptomining abuse of cache resources.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (seasonal/event context): Sunday evening 6-8 PM is the peak shopping window for online retail. Session cache stores shopping cart data for concurrent users. 400% increase corresponds to the weekly peak traffic pattern visible in every prior Sunday's CloudWatch metrics.
detection_signal: ElastiCache retail-session-cache: UsedMemory increased 400% from 18:00-20:00 UTC on Sunday
ground_truth: CloudWatch historical data shows identical 350-450% Sunday evening spike for 52 consecutive Sundays. Pattern correlates with web traffic peaks. No cryptomining indicators. Cache is session-only, no persistent compute workload.
remediation_impact: Terminating or throttling session cache during peak hours would cause shopping cart loss for active customers, directly impacting Sunday evening revenue.

scenario: API Gateway stage retail-payments-v3 has CORS enabled with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for the /checkout/validate endpoint. Scanner flags HIGH for cross-origin exposure of payment validation endpoint.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (WAF-shielded): The wildcard CORS header is intentional to support payment widget embedding in third-party marketplace sellers. AWS WAF is deployed with payment-specific rules blocking non-whitelisted origins at the request evaluation layer. CORS header alone does not grant access.
detection_signal: API Gateway CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on /checkout/validate. AllowCredentials: false.
ground_truth: WAF web ACL evaluates Origin header against seller whitelist. Requests from non-whitelisted origins blocked before reaching Lambda. AllowCredentials=false means cookies/auth headers not included in cross-origin requests.
remediation_impact: Removing wildcard CORS would break payment widget for 47,000 marketplace sellers embedding checkout on their sites.

scenario: IAM role retail-cdn-access-role allows cross-account access from Akamai AWS account (account ID 444455556666). Scanner flags HIGH for third-party account access to CDN configuration data.
why_misclassified: EC-27 (intra-org trust — vendor integration): The cross-account trust is with Akamai Intelligent Platform account for CDN cache invalidation automation. Role is limited to CloudFront:CreateInvalidation on retail distribution only. Documented in CDN integration runbook and vendor security review.
detection_signal: IAM role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/retail-cdn-access-role trust policy: aws:PrincipalAccount=444455556666
ground_truth: Akamai account 444455556666 is published in their AWS integration docs. Role allows only cloudfront:CreateInvalidation on specific distribution arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:distribution/E1A2B3C4D5. ExternalId condition present.
remediation_impact: Removing trust relationship breaks automated CDN cache invalidation on product catalog updates, causing customers to see stale pricing for up to 24 hours.

scenario: DynamoDB table retail-cart-sessions shows 850% read capacity utilization spike and throttling events. CSPM anomaly detection flags potential DDoS against cart service.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (Cyber Monday seasonal event): Throttling events are expected during peak retail events. DynamoDB on-demand mode is enabled but provisioned capacity baseline was set pre-Cyber Monday. Auto-scaling lag causes transient throttling. Pattern matches last 4 years of Cyber Monday data.
detection_signal: DynamoDB retail-cart-sessions: ConsumedReadCapacityUnits 850% above baseline, ThrottledRequests=14,320 in 1 hour
ground_truth: Cyber Monday traffic 8.5x normal baseline — expected per capacity planning. On-demand mode active. Throttling events resolved within 12 minutes as DynamoDB scales. No external attack indicators. Pattern identical to prior Cyber Monday events.
remediation_impact: False alarm distracts incident response team from legitimate Black Friday monitoring responsibilities.

scenario: Azure Purview flags Cosmos DB collection retail-abandoned-carts as containing PII — specifically email addresses in the cart_owner field from 2.8M abandoned cart records. GDPR compliance finding generated.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (empty/anonymous data): The email field contains session-scoped anonymous identifiers in email format (session_abc123@anon.invalid) generated for tracking purposes before user authentication. These are not real email addresses and are not linked to any registered user.
detection_signal: Azure Purview: email pattern detected in retail-abandoned-carts.cart_owner (2.8M documents)
ground_truth: cart_owner values are synthetic session tokens in email format for legacy system compatibility. Domain .invalid is non-routable per RFC 2606. No mapping to registered user accounts. GDPR DPA confirmed anonymous processing.
remediation_impact: Treating anonymous session tokens as PII would require unnecessary GDPR consent mechanisms for anonymous browsing, degrading user experience.

scenario: GCP DLP scan flags BigQuery table retail-analytics.payment_events as CRITICAL for PAN data — detected 14M records with card_token field matching Luhn algorithm card number pattern.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): card_token stores Stripe payment method IDs (format: pm_1234567890abcdef) which happen to pass Luhn validation as a coincidence of the token format. These are Stripe opaque tokens, not actual PAN data. DLP Luhn check incorrectly identifies them as card numbers.
detection_signal: Cloud DLP: infoType CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER detected in retail-analytics.payment_events.card_token (14M rows, likelihood: LIKELY)
ground_truth: card_token values are Stripe payment method IDs (pm_XXXX format). Luhn algorithm match is coincidental. No actual PAN stored in GCP — all payment data tokenized at Stripe before reaching analytics pipeline. Verified with Stripe support.
remediation_impact: Treating Stripe token IDs as PAN would require unnecessary PCI-DSS CDE controls on analytics infrastructure, costing K+ in architectural changes.

scenario: IAM role retail-marketplace-lambda-exec has dynamodb:* on resource * flagged as CRITICAL wildcard permission potentially allowing access to all DynamoDB tables including payment data.
why_misclassified: EC-15 (permission boundary): Role has a permission boundary limiting dynamodb:* effective scope to tables prefixed with marketplace-*. Payment and customer tables use retail-* prefix and are outside the effective permissions even though the role policy appears broad.
detection_signal: IAM role retail-marketplace-lambda-exec: dynamodb:* on Resource: arn:aws:dynamodb:us-east-1:*:table/*
ground_truth: Permission boundary arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/marketplace-only-boundary conditions all DynamoDB on StringLike arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/marketplace-*. Payment tables (retail-*) cannot be accessed regardless of role policy.
remediation_impact: Emergency IAM remediation based on surface reading of role policy without boundary evaluation would disrupt marketplace Lambda functions serving 47,000 sellers.

scenario: AWS Transfer Family SFTP server retail-supplier-sftp-prod allows public endpoint access on port 22. Scanner flags MEDIUM for exposing legacy SFTP to internet for supplier file transfers.
why_misclassified: EC-17 (NACL lockdown): Network ACL acl-sftp-inbound restricts inbound port 22 to 12 specific supplier CIDR ranges. SFTP server uses certificate-based authentication only. Public endpoint label is misleading — NACL enforcement prevents non-approved access.
detection_signal: AWS Transfer SFTP server sftp-0retailsupplier: EndpointType=PUBLIC, port 22
ground_truth: NACL restricts port 22 to 12 approved supplier CIDRs covering 85 suppliers. Password authentication disabled. Host key pinned in supplier onboarding documentation. Public endpoint required for supplier IP range diversity.
remediation_impact: Moving to VPC endpoint would require suppliers to set up VPC peering or Direct Connect, a K+ integration project per large supplier.

scenario: GCP scanner flags Backend Service retail-checkout-backend as allowing all source IPs (no IP restriction on backend). Finding classifies as HIGH network exposure for checkout service.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (Cloud Armor WAF-shielded): Backend Service is protected by Cloud Armor security policy checkout-armor-policy with OWASP rule group and geo-blocking. All traffic must pass Cloud Armor before reaching backend. Backend IP restriction is unnecessary with Cloud Armor enforcement.
detection_signal: GCP Backend Service retail-checkout-backend: no IP restriction rule configured
ground_truth: Cloud Armor policy checkout-armor-policy attached to load balancer. Pre-configured WAF rules block OWASP Top 10. Geo-restriction blocks traffic from 45 high-risk countries. Backend is not directly accessible — all requests through LB + Cloud Armor.
remediation_impact: Attempting to add IP restriction to GCP backend service (not a standard config) would create management complexity with no security benefit over Cloud Armor.

scenario: CloudFront distribution E1RETAIL2PROD uses HTTP protocol policy for origin requests to internal ALB. Scanner flags MEDIUM for unencrypted origin traffic involving product search API.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded): Origin requests use HTTP but travel over AWS internal network between CloudFront PoP and the ALB. AWS internal network traffic is not exposed to internet routing. Product search API returns only public product data — no PII or PCI data in transit.
detection_signal: CloudFront distribution E1RETAIL2PROD: OriginProtocolPolicy=http-only for origin retail-search-alb.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com
ground_truth: CloudFront-to-ALB communication is internal to AWS network, not traversing public internet. ALB has HTTPS listener for client-facing traffic. Product search returns public catalog data only. HTTP origin chosen for latency optimization.
remediation_impact: Switching to HTTPS origin adds certificate management overhead and marginal latency for internal AWS network traffic with no meaningful security improvement.

scenario: CSPM generates 5 separate HIGH findings for Cosmos DB account retail-cart-cosmos — one per configured replica region (East US, West US, North Europe, Southeast Asia, Australia East). Security team opens 5 tickets.
why_misclassified: EC-38 (cross-region replication duplicate): Single Cosmos DB account with 5 geo-replicated regions generates one finding per region for the same underlying misconfiguration (missing customer-managed encryption key). Actual issue is 1 account requiring 1 remediation.
detection_signal: 5 Azure Security Center findings for retail-cart-cosmos across 5 regions: CMK encryption not enabled
ground_truth: Single Cosmos DB account with multi-region write enabled. Enabling CMK on the primary account propagates to all replicas. Deduplication by account ID would collapse to 1 actionable finding.
remediation_impact: Team assigns 5 engineers to 5 tickets for 1 remediation action, wasting 4x engineering capacity.

scenario: EC2 instance retail-paygate-legacy-01 has ports 8443 and 9443 open from 0.0.0.0/0 for legacy payment gateway protocols. Scanner flags HIGH for PCI-DSS non-standard port exposure.
why_misclassified: EC-11 (sunset lifecycle): Instance is tagged as decommission candidate since Q2 2025. Reserved concurrency is 0 (no active connections). All traffic migrated to retail-paygate-v2. DNS removed. No active connections in last 45 days per ALB access logs.
detection_signal: EC2 i-0legacypaygate: ports 8443, 9443 open in security group from 0.0.0.0/0. PCI-scoped account.
ground_truth: Instance receives 0 connections. DNS record removed 2025-09-14. Zero bytes transferred in past 45 days per VPC Flow Logs. Awaiting decommission approval from payment processor partner (6-week process).
remediation_impact: Finding is accurate about configuration but instance has no active traffic. Emergency response distracts from real threats during decommission coordination.

scenario: Azure AD Conditional Access policy compliance check flags 3 users as MFA-exempt: retail-pos-kiosk-01@retail.com, retail-pos-kiosk-02@retail.com, retail-pos-kiosk-03@retail.com. Flagged as MFA compliance violation.
why_misclassified: EC-14 (hardware MFA compensating — kiosk accounts): These are shared kiosk accounts for in-store self-service terminals. Physical hardware MFA (Azure AD FIDO2 key embedded in kiosk) compensates for per-user MFA. Standard Azure AD MFA check does not recognize hardware-embedded FIDO2 as equivalent.
detection_signal: Azure AD: 3 user accounts excluded from MFA Conditional Access policy via named location exemption for POS kiosk network
ground_truth: Kiosk accounts authenticate via hardware FIDO2 key soldered into kiosk chassis. Physical access control to kiosk serves as possession factor. Azure AD does not report hardware-embedded FIDO2 as user-level MFA enrollment.
remediation_impact: Enforcing standard per-user MFA on kiosk accounts would require software authenticator on devices that have no user interaction mechanism.

scenario: CSPM reports HIGH for retail-apac-prod project missing audit log export sink. Scanner indicates audit logs are not being exported for compliance archival.
why_misclassified: EC-19 (org-level logging): An organization-level log sink exports all audit logs from all projects including retail-apac-prod to a centralized Cloud Storage bucket. Scanner checks project-level sinks only, missing the org-level export.
detection_signal: GCP project retail-apac-prod: no project-level logging sink configured
ground_truth: Org-level log sink retail-org-audit-sink exports _Required and _Default log buckets for all projects in the organization. Destination: gs://retail-gcp-audit-archive. PCI-DSS audit trail maintained at org level.
remediation_impact: Creating duplicate project-level sinks doubles logging storage costs (K/month) with no additional compliance benefit.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags Azure App Service retail-checkout-web for 8 HIGH vulnerabilities in the staging deployment slot. Finding requests immediate patching of retail checkout service.
why_misclassified: EC-12 (blue-green inactive slot): The staging slot is the inactive slot in a blue-green swap pattern. App Service is routing 0% traffic to staging slot. Slot contains a previous version awaiting swap-back capability. Will be overwritten on next deployment.
detection_signal: Azure App Service retail-checkout-web staging slot: 8 HIGH vulnerabilities in .NET runtime 8.0.4
ground_truth: Production slot (100% traffic) runs .NET 8.0.8 (fully patched). Staging slot has old version from pre-swap state. 0% traffic routed to staging. Will be replaced at next deployment cycle in 3 days.
remediation_impact: Patching a 0%-traffic staging slot scheduled for replacement in 3 days consumes engineer time with no security benefit.

scenario: Security group for IoT POS device management allows inbound TCP 8883 (MQTT/TLS) from 0.0.0.0/0 on the AWS IoT Core private endpoint. Scanner flags CRITICAL for PCI-scoped network with open IoT management port.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated at NLB level): AWS IoT Core private endpoint is fronted by a Network Load Balancer with IP-based target group. NACL restricts port 8883 to 14 known store network CIDR ranges. SG appears open but NACL enforcement prevents non-store traffic.
detection_signal: Security group sg-iot-pos-mgmt allows TCP 8883 from 0.0.0.0/0 on NLB for IoT Core private endpoint
ground_truth: NACL acl-pos-iot restricts inbound 8883 to 14 store network CIDRs (ISP-assigned static ranges). IoT device certificates required for MQTT authentication. No internet devices can reach the endpoint.
remediation_impact: CRITICAL SLA (7 days) would disrupt IoT security team from real POS firmware update work. Actual risk is MEDIUM given NACL gating.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags Key Vault retail-payments-kv for secret rotation policy violation — 3 secrets show expiry dates more than 90 days in the past. Requires immediate secret rotation.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (immutable rotation pattern — rotation lag): Azure Policy rotation check evaluates expiry dates but the secrets have already been rotated. New secrets created 2 days ago. Old secrets are in a 7-day grace period before deletion (rollback window). Expiry date on old version misread as active.
detection_signal: Azure Key Vault retail-payments-kv: 3 secrets with ExpiryTime < today. Rotation policy non-compliant.
ground_truth: New secret versions created 2026-01-26. Old versions (expiry 2025-11-01) in disabled state, retained for 7-day rollback window. Active version is the new rotation. Scanner evaluates all versions including disabled ones.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated secrets disrupts dependent services mid-rotation window and creates unnecessary key version proliferation.

scenario: Macie scan flags Redshift cluster retail-analytics-dev for containing customer names, addresses, and order history in the dev_customer_360 schema — 8.4M records of apparent customer PII.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (synthetic data): Data generated by Faker-based synthetic data pipeline that produces realistic-looking customer profiles. Names follow census frequency distributions, addresses are real street names but fictitious combinations, orders have statistically plausible patterns.
detection_signal: Macie: customer_name, street_address, order_history columns in Redshift dev_customer_360 schema match PII patterns (8.4M rows)
ground_truth: Synthetic data pipeline documented in data-platform/synthetic-generator. All records generated with customer_id range 9000000+ (real prod IDs are 1-5M range). Data used for ML model training only. Privacy engineering confirmed no real customer data.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to synthetic dev data halts ML personalization model development, impacting product recommendation accuracy improvements.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags 5 public IP addresses as unattached, recommending deletion to reduce attack surface and cost.
why_misclassified: EC-07 (intentionally reserved orphaned IPs): IPs are pre-registered with payment processors and loyalty program partners as approved egress addresses. Releasing them requires 8-12 week re-approval process with each financial partner.
detection_signal: Azure Public IPs: pip-retail-egress-1 through pip-retail-egress-5 have no associated resource
ground_truth: IPs documented in payment-partner-allowlists.md. Registered with Visa, MC, Amex, and 3 loyalty partners for payment API egress whitelist. Reserved for use during disaster recovery when primary compute is replaced.
remediation_impact: Deleting reserved IPs would require 8-12 week re-whitelisting with each payment partner, breaking DR capability.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags 8 Azure Function Apps for not using customer-managed keys for encryption. Functions are part of the retail event processing pipeline.
why_misclassified: EC-39 (serverless encryption nuance — CMK vs platform key): Azure Functions are encrypted by platform-managed keys by default (AES-256). The finding is specifically about CMK absence, not absence of encryption. Non-CDE Functions are not required to use CMK per PCI-DSS guidance.
detection_signal: Azure Function Apps retail-event-processor-1 through -8: no customer-managed encryption key configured
ground_truth: All Functions encrypted with Azure platform-managed keys (AES-256). PCI-DSS requires encryption at rest — satisfied. CMK required only for CDE Functions. These 8 functions process anonymized event data only (no card data).
remediation_impact: Adding Azure Key Vault CMK to 8 non-CDE functions adds K/month in Key Vault costs and operational complexity.

scenario: Payment gateway API has broad CORS policy allowing third-party merchant domains. Scanner flags HIGH for cross-origin payment API exposure. Gateway processes Apple Pay and Google Pay tokenized payments.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (WAF-shielded): WAF with PCI-DSS managed rules validates origin headers. Payment tokens are single-use and cryptographically bound to the merchant domain. CORS permissiveness does not expose cardholder data since tokens expire immediately after use.
detection_signal: API Gateway payment-gateway-prod CORS: AllowOrigins=[*.merchant.com, *.partner-pay.com]
ground_truth: WAF blocks non-whitelisted origins. Apple Pay/Google Pay tokens are DPAN (device PAN) with transaction-scoped validity. Even intercepted tokens cannot be reused or decoded to extract card numbers.
remediation_impact: Restricting CORS would break embedded payment widgets on 12,000 merchant partner sites.

scenario: GuardDuty flags unusual EC2 instance launch pattern — 180 spot instances of c5.4xlarge type launched in 3 minutes. Finding suggests potential cryptomining account compromise.
why_misclassified: EC-10 (ephemeral product rendering): Spot fleet is for the 3D product rendering pipeline that generates augmented reality product views. Fleet launches during nightly batch render job for new product catalog additions, all with TTL tag of 2 hours.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: EC2/UnauthorizedAccess — 180 c5.4xlarge spot instances launched in 3 minutes in us-east-1
ground_truth: Nightly product rendering job launched at 02:00 UTC. All instances tagged with ProductionBatch=true, TTL=2h, and use approved AMI ami-0render-pipeline. Spot fleet auto-terminates after render completion. Pattern repeats nightly.
remediation_impact: Terminating rendering fleet would halt product image generation, delaying new product launches by 24 hours.

scenario: GCP DLP detects PAN-format data in BigQuery table retail-payments.transaction_tokens. 22M records flagged as containing 16-digit sequences passing Luhn validation.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): Fields contain network tokens (Visa Token Service / Mastercard MDES tokens) which are valid 16-digit numbers satisfying Luhn but are cryptographic tokens bound to specific merchant and device context. Not actual PANs.
detection_signal: DLP scan: infoType CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER in retail-payments.transaction_tokens — 22M rows, 16-digit Luhn-valid sequences
ground_truth: All values are Visa Token Service and Mastercard MDES network tokens. These are scheme-managed tokens that look like card numbers but are bound to specific merchant contexts and cannot be used at other merchants.
remediation_impact: Applying CDE controls to token storage adds significant architecture complexity to analytics infrastructure.

scenario: IAM policy MarketplaceSellerPolicy allows DynamoDB GetItem on all tables matching arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/marketplace-*. Scanner flags HIGH for overly permissive DynamoDB access allowing cross-seller data access.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC-bounded tenant isolation): All DynamoDB table access is within a dedicated marketplace VPC with VPC endpoints. DynamoDB tables use partition key design where seller_id is the hash key, and all application-layer queries enforce seller_id = caller_seller_id. Scanner evaluates IAM policy in isolation without application-layer context.
detection_signal: IAM policy: dynamodb:GetItem,PutItem,Query on arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/marketplace-*
ground_truth: Application enforces seller_id partition key isolation at query layer. No DynamoDB query can return another seller's data. VPC endpoint prevents cross-account access. Partition design confirmed by database architect.
remediation_impact: Per-seller DynamoDB table isolation would require 47,000 separate table namespaces, infeasible at scale.

scenario: Azure VMSS retail-storefront-vmss scaled from 15 to 85 VMs in 20 minutes. Defender for Cloud flags anomalous scale-out event as potential account compromise for unauthorized compute provisioning.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (seasonal event): Back-to-school shopping season triggers documented scale-out. Azure Monitor scheduled alert fired the scale-out at the pre-defined threshold. Pattern matches same week in prior 3 years.
detection_signal: Azure VMSS scale-out: 70 instances added in 20 minutes. Defender: anomalous compute provisioning pattern
ground_truth: AutoScale rule with custom metric 'cart_add_rate > 500/min' triggered. Documented seasonal event. All instances launched from approved image. Scale-out acknowledged in Azure DevOps release notes.
remediation_impact: Terminating back-to-school scale-out would cause checkout timeouts during peak student shopping period.

scenario: GCP Dataflow pipeline retail-etl-pipeline for order processing does not enable worker disk encryption with CMEK. Scanner flags HIGH for potential unencrypted data on temporary worker disks.
why_misclassified: EC-13 (app-layer encryption): Pipeline processes already-encrypted order records. Order data is encrypted with AES-256 at the application layer before entering the Dataflow pipeline. Even if worker disk were readable, only ciphertext is present.
detection_signal: Dataflow job retail-etl-pipeline: workerDiskEncryptionKey=null (no CMEK on worker disks)
ground_truth: Orders encrypted with application-level key before Dataflow ingestion. Worker disk contains only application-level ciphertext. GCP default encryption still applies to worker disks. CMEK would add encryption-of-encryption overhead.
remediation_impact: Adding CMEK to Dataflow adds KMS costs and Key Management operational complexity for already double-encrypted data.

scenario: Lambda function retail-old-reports uses python3.8 runtime which reached end-of-life in October 2024. Scanner flags HIGH for EOL runtime in production.
why_misclassified: EC-11 (sunset lifecycle): Function is tagged as sunset=Q1-2026 with reserved concurrency set to 0. All functionality migrated to retail-reports-v2 using python3.12. Old function retained for rollback capability, never invoked in production.
detection_signal: Lambda retail-old-reports: runtime=python3.8 (EOL 2024-10-14). No invocations in 180 days.
ground_truth: Reserved concurrency=0. Zero invocations since 2025-08-12. Trigger disabled. Decommission scheduled for Q1 2026 after migration validation period. EOL runtime poses no runtime risk if function never executes.
remediation_impact: Emergency runtime migration of a never-invoked function scheduled for decommission is unnecessary busywork.

scenario: IAM role retail-delivery-ops-role has ec2:* and ecs:* permissions flagged as HIGH overpermission. Role used by last-mile delivery operations team to manage their fleet of delivery tracking EC2/ECS resources.
why_misclassified: EC-15 (permission boundary): Role has permission boundary restricting ec2:* and ecs:* to resources tagged with Team=delivery. Payment and core retail resources tagged Team=retail cannot be accessed even though the role policy appears broad.
detection_signal: IAM role retail-delivery-ops-role: ec2:*, ecs:* with Resource: *
ground_truth: Permission boundary policy 'delivery-team-boundary' adds Condition: StringEquals aws:ResourceTag/Team delivery for all EC2 and ECS actions. No access to non-delivery-tagged resources effective.
remediation_impact: Tightening role without understanding permission boundary would disrupt last-mile delivery operations for 3,400 store delivery routes.

scenario: SAST scan of CodeBuild project retail-security-scanner reports CVE-2024-32002 (git arbitrary code execution, CRITICAL) in the git binary used for SCM checkout. Finding escalated as CRITICAL supply chain risk.
why_misclassified: EC-02 (build layer CVE): git is present in the CodeBuild environment for source checkout only. The vulnerability requires a malicious submodule URL to be cloned. CodeBuild checks out from a trusted private CodeCommit repository with no external submodules.
detection_signal: CodeBuild environment: git 2.44.0 with CVE-2024-32002 (CVSS 9.0) detected
ground_truth: git used exclusively for CodeCommit checkout in a controlled build environment. No external repository URLs or submodules configured. CodeCommit repository is private and write-protected. CVE exploit requires cloning a malicious repo with crafted submodule paths.
remediation_impact: Updating git in build environment image is good practice but CRITICAL escalation overstates urgency given controlled source.

scenario: Macie scans Redshift cluster retail-dw-prod and flags customer_lifetime_value table as containing PII. Table has 18M records with columns: cust_key, age_group, region, ltv_tier, preferred_category.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (empty/non-PII data): cust_key is a surrogate integer key with no mapping to PII data in the data warehouse. age_group is a 10-year bracket. region is a 3-digit postal prefix (not full zip code). LTV and category are computed behavioral metrics — no direct identifiers.
detection_signal: Macie: 18M records with fields matching demographic PII patterns in retail-dw-prod customer_lifetime_value
ground_truth: All direct identifiers stripped in ETL transformation. cust_key has no cross-reference table in DW. age_group and region are coarsened to exceed GDPR k-anonymity threshold (k>5). Reviewed by privacy counsel for GDPR compliance.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to anonymized behavioral metrics halts retail analytics and personalization model development.

scenario: ECS Fargate task definition retail-checkout-task flagged for CVE-2024-24783 (HIGH, Go TLS) in the Fargate platform runtime. Finding requests immediate remediation.
why_misclassified: EC-36 (managed runtime shared responsibility): Fargate platform runtime (including underlying Go TLS libraries used by the Fargate agent) is managed by AWS. Customer code runs in an isolated container above the Fargate platform layer. CVE in Fargate platform runtime is AWS's remediation responsibility.
detection_signal: ECS Fargate task: CVE-2024-24783 in Go TLS runtime component of Fargate platform 1.4.0
ground_truth: CVE is in the Fargate platform agent, not in customer container code. AWS patches Fargate platform transparently. Customer cannot and should not patch Fargate platform components. Shared responsibility: AWS owns platform, customer owns container.
remediation_impact: Customer cannot patch Fargate platform. Ticket generates false urgency for an unremedial finding from the customer perspective.

scenario: GKE node pool retail-prod-nodes shows 4 new nodes with 0% CIS benchmark compliance score. Security team escalates for immediate remediation of new non-compliant nodes.
why_misclassified: EC-23 (warm-up window): Nodes launched 25 minutes ago via cluster autoscaler. GKE Security Posture assessment evaluates nodes on a 30-minute cycle. Nodes not yet assessed — 0% reflects absence of scan data, not actual non-compliance. Nodes provisioned from hardened node image.
detection_signal: GKE node pool: 4 nodes with SecurityPostureScore=0 (not yet evaluated)
ground_truth: Nodes use custom node image with CIS Level 2 baseline pre-applied. GKE Security Posture assessment pending (runs every 30 minutes). Score will populate to 94%+ after first assessment based on prior identical node images.
remediation_impact: Emergency patching newly launched nodes pre-assessment wastes SRE time and may cause service disruption before nodes have processed any traffic.

scenario: EKS pod retail-inventory-sidecar running distroless/static:latest flagged for CVE-2024-7006 (NULL ptr deref in libtiff, AV:L/AC:L). Scanner reports HIGH based on CVSS base score.
why_misclassified: EC-29 (distroless image, AV:L unexploitable): CVE-2024-7006 requires local access to trigger via crafted TIFF file. Distroless image has no shell, no package manager, no local file system write capability. The inventory sidecar processes JSON messages — no TIFF handling.
detection_signal: EKS pod: libtiff in distroless image with CVE-2024-7006 CVSS 6.5 HIGH. AV:L attack vector.
ground_truth: AV:L (local access) requires shell access — impossible in distroless. Container processes only JSON inventory data — no TIFF parsing code paths. Vulnerability is architecturally unexploitable.
remediation_impact: Patching libtiff in distroless requires base image rebuild for a library with zero code path reachability in this application.

scenario: SQS queue retail-order-events allows sqs:SendMessage from Principal: * (all principals). Scanner flags HIGH for public SQS queue that could receive unauthorized messages.
why_misclassified: EC-18 (VPC endpoint deny compensates): SQS resource policy appears to allow all, but has aws:sourceVpce condition requiring messages originate from specific VPC endpoint vpce-0sqs-retail. Internet traffic cannot send messages despite the broad Principal.
detection_signal: SQS queue retail-order-events resource policy: Principal=* Action=sqs:SendMessage (no explicit condition shown in summary)
ground_truth: Full policy includes Condition: StringEquals aws:sourceVpce vpce-0sqs-retail. Only resources in the retail VPC with access to the endpoint can send messages. Internet principals blocked by VPC endpoint condition.
remediation_impact: Restricting Principal would require enumeration of all Lambda and EC2 principals that send to queue, creating maintenance burden for auto-scaling workloads.

scenario: Azure Function App retail-reports-legacy has CVE-2024-38094 (HIGH, Microsoft SharePoint) in a .NET dependency. Finding requires emergency patching.
why_misclassified: EC-04 (dead code path): Microsoft.SharePoint.Client library is referenced in the function codebase from a previous integration attempt but the code path is never reached — the SharePoint integration was replaced with direct SharePoint REST API calls 18 months ago. The dead code path loads the library but never calls any SharePoint methods.
detection_signal: Azure Function retail-reports-legacy: CVE-2024-38094 in Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.dll (referenced in project)
ground_truth: SharePoint client library loaded but code path disabled by feature flag SharepointClientEnabled=false in app config. No SharePoint client methods called in function execution. Library effectively dead code.
remediation_impact: Removing dead library reference requires code cleanup but CRITICAL/HIGH urgency overstated for unreachable code.

scenario: GCP IAM key rotation policy flags SA key for retail-inventory-sa as overdue. Key shows creation_time 95 days ago, exceeding 90-day rotation policy.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (immutable rotation): Key was rotated 4 days ago. New key created and deployed. Old key (95 days old) is in a disabled state awaiting deletion after 7-day rollback validation. Scanner sees old disabled key and reports the creation_time without checking key state.
detection_signal: SA key for retail-inventory-sa: key_id=abc123, created 95 days ago. Policy: rotate every 90 days.
ground_truth: Key abc123 is DISABLED (disabled_time: 4 days ago). Active key def456 created 4 days ago. Rotation completed on schedule. Disabled key retained for rollback window per key management policy.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated SA disrupts inventory sync service and creates unnecessary key proliferation.

scenario: Security group saas-internal-api-sg allows inbound port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. No finding because group is tagged team=platform and platform team findings are suppressed during a feature freeze (automated suppression to reduce noise).
why_misclassified: EC-49 (tag suppression masking real issue): Feature freeze suppression was intended for low-severity config drift. The security group was modified by IaC accident during the freeze to expose an internal API endpoint to the internet. Suppression hides a real CRITICAL exposure.
detection_signal: Security group saas-internal-api-sg in suppressed state (tag team=platform, freeze_mode=true)
ground_truth: SG modified 3 days ago via Terraform apply error. Internal API (saas-internal-control-plane) now reachable from internet on port 443. Control plane has no external authentication — relies on VPC network isolation. Feature freeze suppression applied at wrong granularity.
remediation_impact: Internal control plane API exposed to internet without authentication. Real CRITICAL with potential for full tenant data access.

scenario: EKS cluster saas-prod RBAC configuration shows compliant per CSPM (last scan 12 days ago). Engineer manually added a ClusterRoleBinding for debugging 8 days ago giving their personal service account cluster-admin.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan drift): Manual RBAC change occurred between 14-day scan cycles. Real-time change detection for EKS RBAC not configured. cluster-admin binding persists unreported.
detection_signal: Last CSPM RBAC scan: 12 days ago (clean). Manual ClusterRoleBinding created 8 days ago not reflected.
ground_truth: ClusterRoleBinding debug-sa-admin grants cluster-admin to engineer service account. Created for incident debugging. Never removed post-incident. Full cluster access persists for non-operator service account.
remediation_impact: Engineer service account with cluster-admin on production cluster. Multi-tenant data accessible via kubectl exec or API server.

scenario: Lambda function saas-billing-engine uses vendored Stripe SDK fork. SBOM marks as vendor-managed, skipping CVE analysis. Vendored copy is 11 months old.
why_misclassified: EC-42 (vendored fork not patched): CVE-2024-32002 disclosed 4 months ago in stripe-node upstream. The internal fork was taken before the CVE and was never updated. Scanner assumes vendored = patched without verification.
detection_signal: vendor/stripe-node/ in saas-billing-engine Lambda. SBOM: vendor-managed, CVE scan skipped.
ground_truth: vendor/stripe-node/lib/http-client.js uses node-fetch 2.6.7 with CVE-2024-28849 (SSRF, HIGH). Vendored copy predates the CVE. Billing engine makes HTTP calls to Stripe API — SSRF exploitable to redirect payment API calls.
remediation_impact: SSRF in billing HTTP client potentially exploitable to redirect Stripe API calls during payment processing.

scenario: GCP emergency SA saas-emergency@saas-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com created a user-managed key via the GCP Console. CSPM does not flag because SA is in break-glass exemption. Key has Owner role.
why_misclassified: EC-28 (break-glass abuse): Break-glass exemption covers IAM role findings but accidentally also suppresses SA key creation alerts. Emergency procedure requires Workload Identity Federation, not key files. Key creation is out-of-policy.
detection_signal: Break-glass SA in exemption list. Key creation event logged to Cloud Audit Logs but not surfaced as CSPM finding.
ground_truth: SA key created outside documented break-glass procedure. Key persists after incident window. Owner-level SA key could be exfiltrated or misused. No expiration set.
remediation_impact: Persistent Owner SA key with no expiry. If exfiltrated, grants full project control including all customer data in GCP project.

scenario: ECR image saas-integrations:v3.5.0 passes all CVE checks. However, the SBOM was generated from the source package.json not the actual installed node_modules tree, missing a npm hoisting resolution difference.
why_misclassified: EC-44 (SBOM manifest vs installed tree mismatch): package.json declares axios@1.6.0 (no known CVEs at scan time). npm install resolves axios@0.27.2 for a nested dependency due to peer dependency conflict. axios@0.27.2 has CVE-2023-45857 (CSRF, HIGH). Scanner reads manifest, not resolved lockfile.
detection_signal: SBOM from package.json: axios@1.6.0 — no CVEs. ECR scan: passed.
ground_truth: package-lock.json shows axios@0.27.2 in nested node_modules/sdk-lib/node_modules/axios. This version has CVE-2023-45857. SBOM generated from top-level package.json misses nested resolution.
remediation_impact: CSRF vulnerability in HTTP client used by integration webhooks allows request forgery attacks against integrated SaaS APIs.

scenario: Cloud Run service saas-data-pipeline has CVE-2024-41110 in Docker engine used for build-time containers. Feature flag 'new-pipeline-engine=true' shows 15% rollout in LaunchDarkly. CSPM suppresses finding as flag below 20% threshold.
why_misclassified: EC-45 (partial rollout active in prod): 15% of the production data pipeline uses the vulnerable engine. 15% of customer data processing workflows touch the CVE. Threshold-based suppression is appropriate for unreleased features but not production traffic segments.
detection_signal: Feature flag new-pipeline-engine: 15% rollout. CSPM threshold: suppress below 20%. No finding.
ground_truth: 15% production rollout = ~4,500 customer pipeline runs/day on vulnerable Docker engine version. CVE-2024-41110 (container escape, CVSS 9.9) actively exploitable in the deployed configuration.
remediation_impact: Container escape vulnerability in production pipeline for 15% of customers goes undetected due to percentage threshold suppression.

scenario: Azure AD service principal saas-reporting-sp shows last sign-in 88 days ago per CSPM (PST timezone). Policy: revoke after 90 days. CSPM marks as active. SP has Contributor role on 8 Azure subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-48 (timezone mismatch): Azure sign-in logs are in UTC. CSPM converts to PST without DST correction. Actual UTC age: 91 days — past 90-day threshold. DST conversion error prevents flag from triggering.
detection_signal: SP last_sign_in: 2025-11-02T08:00:00Z UTC. CSPM evaluation: 88 days ago (PST calculation). Policy: 90 days. Result: active.
ground_truth: UTC calculation: 91 days since last sign-in. SP has Contributor on 8 Azure subscriptions with SaaS infrastructure. Genuinely stale but DST math keeps it 2 days under threshold.
remediation_impact: Stale Contributor SP on 8 Azure subscriptions. If credentials leaked, full infrastructure modification access.

scenario: AWS Security Hub reports LOW for 'EC2 security group allows ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22' on saas-admin-bastion. Analyst deprioritizes as LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): AWS Security Hub rates SSH exposure as LOW assuming key-based auth. The SaaS admin bastion uses password authentication (keys were reset during an access issue). The actual risk is HIGH for an exposed bastion with password auth.
detection_signal: Security Hub: SSH-open-0.0.0.0/0 LOW on sg-0saas-bastion. Default severity applied.
ground_truth: Bastion sshd_config: PasswordAuthentication yes. Exposed to 0.0.0.0/0. Password auth allows brute force. Security Hub LOW assumes key-only auth which is the default assumption but not this configuration.
remediation_impact: Brute-forceable bastion with admin access to all SaaS production infrastructure. LOW SLA (90 days) allows prolonged exposure.

scenario: EC2 instance saas-windows-rdgateway (Windows Server 2022) has no CVE findings. Scanner applied Linux CVE feed during a feed migration that incorrectly profiled the instance OS.
why_misclassified: EC-34 inverse (Windows CVEs missed on Windows instance): Feed migration tagged the instance as linux/x86_64 based on an AWS API response parsing error. Windows-specific CVEs including CVE-2024-38063 (TCP/IP RCE, CVSS 9.8) not applied.
detection_signal: Scanner: instance i-0saas-rdgateway OS detected as linux/x86_64. No Windows CVE feed applied.
ground_truth: Instance runs Windows Server 2022. GetConsoleOutput shows Windows boot sequence. CVE-2024-38063 (IPv6 TCP/IP stack RCE) applies to Windows Server 2022. Feed OS detection error caused miss.
remediation_impact: Critical RCE on Remote Desktop Gateway — internet-facing service — goes unpatched due to OS detection error in CVE feed.

scenario: EKS cluster saas-prod has Kyverno image signing policy. CSPM shows policy enabled. However, an engineer deployed a hotfix directly via kubectl bypassing the CI/CD pipeline and Kyverno was not enforcing during a node restart.
why_misclassified: EC-35 (admission enforcement gap): Kyverno webhook had a 4-minute unavailability window during node restart. During this window, Kyverno failurePolicy was set to Ignore (not Fail) meaning requests proceed without admission check if webhook unavailable. Unsigned image deployed.
detection_signal: Kyverno policy: enabled. CSPM: compliant. Webhook unavailability and failurePolicy not monitored.
ground_truth: Webhook failurePolicy=Ignore allowed deployment during 4-minute window. Unsigned image saas-api-hotfix:untagged-abc123 deployed. Image provenance unverifiable. FailurePolicy should be Fail for production image signing enforcement.
remediation_impact: Unsigned hotfix image in production. Supply chain integrity cannot be verified. Could be tampered or from unofficial build.

scenario: GuardDuty reports LOW for EC2 instance saas-api-worker-03 communicating with a known threat actor IP. GuardDuty Malware Protection tier active — malware scan clean. Severity auto-downgraded to LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-50 (enhanced tier severity discount): GuardDuty Malware Protection tier downgrades threat findings when malware scan is clean, assuming threat intelligence is a false positive. However, the instance is communicating with a C2 IP using HTTP over port 443 — C2 beacon patterns visible in CloudWatch traffic logs.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: Recon:EC2/PortProbeUnprotectedPort LOW — malware scan clean. Severity auto-reduced.
ground_truth: Traffic analysis shows 30-second interval HTTP beacons to known C2 infrastructure 185.220.101.x. Malware scan missed the beacon implant (fileless execution). GuardDuty Malware Protection's clean scan incorrectly absolves the finding.
remediation_impact: Potential C2 beacon from production API worker goes uninvestigated at LOW priority. Real threat actor potentially present in SaaS infrastructure.

scenario: IAM user saas-legacy-integration-user has access key AKIASAAS0000000001 with last_used=null. CSPM classifies as inactive/headless SA — low risk exemption applied.
why_misclassified: EC-26 (never-used key not inactive): Key created 14 months ago during vendor integration setup. Integration was abandoned but key never revoked. Key has s3:PutObject on saas-customer-data-exports bucket — never used but valid credential.
detection_signal: IAM user saas-legacy-integration-user: access key last_used=null (14 months old). CSPM: inactive, low risk.
ground_truth: Valid, never-rotated key exists with write access to customer data export bucket. Vendor integration abandoned. Key represents orphaned credential with data write access.
remediation_impact: Orphaned key with customer data write access. Credential theft or abuse could allow unauthorized data manipulation in customer export pipeline.

scenario: GCP org policy compute.requireOsLogin is enforced at org level. CSPM: compliant. However, saas-dev-tools project has project-level override disabling OS Login for a legacy automation tool.
why_misclassified: EC-40 (project override not checked): OS Login provides centralized SSH access control via GCP IAM. The project override re-enables metadata-based SSH keys for saas-dev-tools VMs. CSPM evaluates org policy but not project overrides.
detection_signal: Org policy compute.requireOsLogin: enforced. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Project saas-dev-tools has constraint override disabling OS Login. VMs in this project accept metadata SSH keys bypassing GCP IAM SSH access control. Keys could be injected by anyone with compute.instances.setMetadata permission.
remediation_impact: SSH access to dev-tools VMs bypasses OS Login, allowing unauthorized SSH if metadata injection is achieved. Dev-tools VMs have service account access to production artifact buckets.

scenario: ECR image saas-platform:v12.3.1 CVE scan passes. Scanner correctly identifies webpack, eslint, and typescript as devDependencies and suppresses their CVEs. However, the production bundle accidentally includes webpack's runtime.
why_misclassified: EC-43 inverse (devDep actually bundled): Webpack config added --mode development accidentally in a build config PR. Development mode embeds webpack-dev-server runtime in the bundle. CVE-2024-45590 (webpack-dev-server middleware prototype pollution) is present in production.
detection_signal: Scanner: webpack in devDependencies — CVE-2024-45590 suppressed. Production bundle not inspected.
ground_truth: Production Docker image contains webpack-dev-server runtime due to --mode development build flag. CVE-2024-45590 (prototype pollution) exploitable via crafted HMR requests. Scanner correctly suppressed the devDep CVE but did not inspect actual bundle.
remediation_impact: Prototype pollution in production API server allows request manipulation for affected tenants.

scenario: GCP Artifact Registry scan: CVE-2024-6387 marked as MODIFIED (OpenSSH) — scanner marks as addressed and clears the finding. A related unfixed variant CVE-2024-6409 (same component, different race condition) was published 5 days after the last scan.
why_misclassified: EC-46 (related CVE outside scan window): Scanner cleared CVE-2024-6387 finding and did not re-check the component for new CVEs within the 7-day scan window. CVE-2024-6409 missed due to feed staleness.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-6387: MODIFIED — no longer critical, cleared. No finding for CVE-2024-6409.
ground_truth: CVE-2024-6409 published after last scan — same OpenSSH signal handling race condition, CVSS 7.0 HIGH. Scanner clearing CVE-6387 did not trigger re-scan of the affected component for new CVEs.
remediation_impact: HIGH OpenSSH vulnerability in internet-facing SaaS infrastructure goes undetected due to related-CVE scan gap.

scenario: GCP SCC reports LOW for 'Service account has owner role' on SA saas-data-migration@saas-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Analyst ignores as LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): GCP SCC rates Owner role on SA as LOW because it assumes the SA is intentionally privileged (common in migration contexts). AWS Security Hub and Azure Security Center would rate Owner/AdministratorAccess on a service account as CRITICAL. The SA is actively used in production pipelines.
detection_signal: GCP SCC: SA has Owner role — LOW severity (migration SA context assumed)
ground_truth: SA with Owner role actively used by data migration pipelines processing customer data. Owner role grants full project control. GCP LOW rating inappropriate for production SA with Owner. Actual risk is CRITICAL — Owner SA compromise = full tenant data access.
remediation_impact: LOW SLA (90+ days) for an active Owner-role SA. Real risk is immediate — SA should be downscoped to minimum required permissions.

scenario: GCS bucket saas-customer-backups tagged security-reviewed=2025-01 suppresses CSPM findings per quarterly review policy. A new allUsers IAM binding was added by an automated migration script 3 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49 (suppression tag masking real issue): Quarterly review tag suppresses all findings for 90 days post-review. The allUsers binding occurred 3 weeks after the review — real exposure hidden behind review suppression.
detection_signal: Bucket saas-customer-backups: security-reviewed=2025-01 tag. CSPM suppression active.
ground_truth: allUsers storage.objects.viewer binding added 2026-01-05 by auto-migration-sa. Bucket contains customer data exports. 90-day suppression period masks the new exposure for 2 more months.
remediation_impact: Customer backup data publicly accessible for an extended period, violating GDPR data minimization and SOC 2 CC6.1.

scenario: New AWS account saas-tenant-enterprise-12345 created 3 hours ago via Control Tower. CSPM shows no findings — SecurityHub findings still generating (warm-up window).
why_misclassified: EC-23 (warm-up window): Account provisioned without root MFA and default VPC present. Security Hub enrolled but has not yet run CIS benchmark. Warm-up gap means real baseline misconfigurations are invisible for up to 24 hours.
detection_signal: Account saas-tenant-enterprise-12345: SecurityHub enrolled 3h ago. No findings yet. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Root account has no MFA (Control Tower account vending does not enforce root MFA by default). Default VPC present with open security groups. 3-hour window of unmonitored tenant account with root access.
remediation_impact: Enterprise customer tenant account with root-level access and open network during onboarding period. Real security baseline gap.

scenario: CloudTrail log retention policy shows 365 days. CSPM marks compliant. However, the retention policy was changed from 365 to 30 days in a Terraform apply 89 days ago — the Terraform state file uses PST timestamps while the CSPM policy check uses UTC.
why_misclassified: EC-48 (timezone mismatch on policy evaluation): The 90-day lookback window for policy change detection uses PST timezone. The Terraform apply occurred at 2025-10-28T01:30:00-07:00 (PST) = 2025-10-28T08:30:00Z (UTC). UTC calculation shows 93 days since change, PST shows 92 days — both indicate recent change but CSPM only flags changes within 90 days.
detection_signal: CloudTrail retention: current_value=30 days. Change timestamp evaluated as 92 days ago (PST). Policy: flag changes within 90 days. Result: no flag.
ground_truth: UTC evaluation: 93 days since retention reduction. SOC 2 requires 1-year audit trail retention. Retention currently at 30 days — compliance gap. DST evaluation keeps it 2 days outside the detection window.
remediation_impact: 30-day log retention violates SOC 2 CC7.2 audit trail requirements. Real compliance gap active for 93 days without detection.

scenario: GCP Artifact Registry SBOM for saas-tenant-api:v7.2.0 shows no CVEs. SBOM was generated from requirements.txt (Python). Actual installed packages differ due to pip's dependency resolver finding compatible sub-versions.
why_misclassified: EC-44 (SBOM from manifest vs installed env): requirements.txt specifies Pillow>=9.0.0. pip resolves to Pillow 9.0.0 (not the latest 10.x). CVE-2023-44271 (uncontrolled resource consumption in Pillow 9.0.x) present in resolved version but not detectable from requirements.txt manifest-based SBOM.
detection_signal: SBOM from requirements.txt: Pillow>=9.0.0 (no specific version). No CVE flagged.
ground_truth: pip install resolves Pillow==9.0.0 in production container. CVE-2023-44271 affects Pillow < 9.2.0. SBOM from requirements.txt cannot detect specific resolved version CVEs when version ranges specified.
remediation_impact: Image processing vulnerability in tenant API service allows resource exhaustion via crafted image uploads — potential DoS against multi-tenant platform.

scenario: Lambda function saas-export-service has CVE-2024-45337 in a SFTP library. Feature flag 'sftp-export-enabled=true' shows 8% rollout. CSPM suppresses at below-10% threshold.
why_misclassified: EC-45 (enterprise tier partial rollout): 8% is the aggregate rollout — the flag is enabled for 100% of enterprise tier customers (which are 8% of total customer count). Enterprise customers have larger data volumes and the SFTP export processes the most sensitive data.
detection_signal: Feature flag sftp-export-enabled: 8% rollout. CSPM suppressed: below 10% threshold.
ground_truth: 100% of enterprise customers (8% of total = 27 enterprises) using SFTP export. These are the highest-value, most data-sensitive accounts. CVE-2024-45337 (SSH auth bypass) active for all enterprise SFTP exports.
remediation_impact: SSH auth bypass vulnerability active for all enterprise customers' SFTP exports — the most sensitive use case in the platform.

scenario: Azure AD SP saas-legacy-partner-integration has last_sign_in=null (never signed in). CSPM classifies as inactive/headless, low risk. SP has Contributor role on 6 Azure subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-26 (never-used SP not inactive): SP created during partner onboarding 18 months ago. Integration never completed. SP has valid credentials (client secret expiry: 2027). Never-used does not mean safe — valid credential with Contributor access across 6 subscriptions exists.
detection_signal: SP saas-legacy-partner-integration: last_sign_in=null, created 18 months ago. CSPM: inactive, exempt.
ground_truth: Client secret valid until 2027. Contributor role on saas-prod, saas-staging, and 4 other subscriptions. Partner integration project was abandoned but SP was never decommissioned. Real lateral movement risk if credentials leaked.
remediation_impact: Valid Contributor-level SP credentials across 6 subscriptions with no monitoring. Compromise allows full infrastructure modification.

scenario: Cloud Run service saas-api passes CVE checks. Jest is in devDependencies with CVE-2024-21538. Scanner suppresses jest CVE as devDependency. However, jest-worker is present in the production bundle.
why_misclassified: EC-43 inverse (devDep accidentally in production): Jest's jest-worker module was inadvertently included in webpack build due to a misconfigured external configuration. CVE-2024-21538 (ReDoS in jest-worker) present in production Cloud Run image despite being a devDependency in package.json.
detection_signal: jest in devDependencies — CVE-2024-21538 suppressed. Production image not analyzed for actual bundle contents.
ground_truth: webpack.config.js externals configuration accidentally removed jest-worker from externals list. jest-worker present in production bundle. SBOM from package.json misses the actual inclusion.
remediation_impact: ReDoS vulnerability in production service. Crafted request patterns could cause worker thread hang, impacting service availability.

scenario: GCP SCC reports LOW for API server VM saas-api-prod-01 communicating with suspicious external IPs. Security Command Center Premium tier's threat intelligence integration applied LOW based on TI confidence score.
why_misclassified: EC-50 (enhanced controls severity inflation — inverse): SCC Premium TI integration applied LOW because the external IPs are in a 'gray' TI category (not definitively malicious). However, the communication pattern (30-second beacons to 3 IPs in 3 different countries) is anomalous for an API server that should only communicate with GCP services and customer IPs.
detection_signal: GCP SCC Premium: suspicious network activity to gray-zone TI IPs — LOW (TI confidence: 0.3)
ground_truth: API server communicating to IPs not in customer allowlist, GCP service ranges, or known CDN/DNS ranges. Beacon pattern: 30-second intervals. Production API server should have no outbound traffic to these IPs. Potential C2 despite non-definitive TI classification.
remediation_impact: Potential C2 beacon from production SaaS infrastructure goes uninvestigated due to low TI confidence score override.

scenario: Azure VM saas-windows-report-server (Windows Server 2019) shows no CVE findings. Defender for Cloud applied the Linux patch assessment profile during a platform migration, skipping Windows-specific CVEs.
why_misclassified: EC-34 inverse (Windows CVEs missed on Windows VM): Azure Defender patch assessment profile migration accidentally assigned Linux profile to Windows VMs in the saas-reports resource group. CVE-2024-38063 and CVE-2024-43491 (both Windows-specific, CRITICAL) not evaluated.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: saas-windows-report-server — patch assessment profile: linux-cis. No Windows CVEs.
ground_truth: VM runs Windows Server 2019. CVE-2024-38063 (TCP/IP RCE, CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2024-43491 (Servicing Stack update, CVSS 9.8) applicable. Linux patch profile misassigned during Azure VM fleet migration.
remediation_impact: Two CRITICAL Windows CVEs on production reporting server go unpatched due to profile misassignment.

scenario: Lambda function saas-sso-handler uses vendored fork of passport.js authentication library. SBOM marks as vendor-managed, CVE analysis skipped. Fork is 16 months old.
why_misclassified: EC-42 (vendored fork not patched): CVE-2024-37897 (authentication bypass in passport.js session handling) disclosed 5 months ago. The internal fork predates this CVE. Vendor directory skipped in SBOM analysis.
detection_signal: vendor/passport/ in saas-sso-handler. SBOM: vendor-managed, skip.
ground_truth: vendor/passport/lib/session.js contains the vulnerable session handling code. CVE-2024-37897 allows authentication bypass via crafted session cookie. SSO handler is critical path for all 340 tenant logins.
remediation_impact: Authentication bypass in SSO handler — CRITICAL for all tenant logins. Attacker could bypass authentication for any tenant.

scenario: GCP org policy run.allowedIngress restricts Cloud Run to internal-only traffic at org level. CSPM: compliant. However, project saas-integrations has override enabling all traffic.
why_misclassified: EC-40 (project override not traversed): CSPM evaluates org policy at org level — compliant. Integration project override allows allUsers ingress for a Cloud Run service that handles customer webhook deliveries, but also inadvertently exposes an internal admin Cloud Run service.
detection_signal: Org policy run.allowedIngress=internal. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Project override: run.allowedIngress=all in saas-integrations. Two Cloud Run services exposed: saas-webhook-delivery (intentional) AND saas-admin-panel (inadvertent). Admin panel has no authentication — assumed internal-only via org policy.
remediation_impact: Internal admin panel for managing tenant configurations exposed to internet without authentication.

scenario: Azure Security Center reports MEDIUM for 'AKS cluster has Kubernetes dashboard enabled' on saas-aks-prod. Same finding on GCP GKE would be HIGH, and on Amazon EKS would be HIGH.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): Azure rates Kubernetes dashboard exposure as MEDIUM because Azure Dashboard has RBAC in newer versions. However, the specific AKS version deployed (1.27) still uses the legacy dashboard without sufficient RBAC enforcement.
detection_signal: Azure Security Center: AKS saas-aks-prod — Kubernetes dashboard enabled — MEDIUM
ground_truth: AKS 1.27 Kubernetes dashboard uses legacy auth that can be bypassed. GCP and AWS rate similar findings HIGH. The dashboard exposes cluster admin UI on an internal port reachable from the cluster network. Multi-tenant risk.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM SLA (30 days) for a dashboard with legacy auth on a multi-tenant production cluster. Azure's lower baseline rating understates risk.

scenario: Azure AD application saas-enterprise-connector has compliance-reviewed=2025-Q3 tag. CSPM suppresses findings. A new Graph API permission (Sites.ReadWrite.All) was added 3 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49 (suppression tag masking real issue): Q3 2025 compliance review approved Sites.Read.All. New Sites.ReadWrite.All permission added via Azure Portal by a developer 3 weeks after the review. Suppression still active for full Q4 2025 review cycle.
detection_signal: App saas-enterprise-connector: tag compliance-reviewed=2025-Q3. CSPM suppression active.
ground_truth: Application now has Sites.ReadWrite.All (full SharePoint read/write for all site collections). Q3 review approved read-only Sites.Read.All. Write permission added post-review without additional review. Suppression hides the upgrade.
remediation_impact: SaaS connector with full SharePoint write access to enterprise customer tenants. Potential for unauthorized document modification across all enterprise customers.

scenario: GCP firewall rules for saas-prod VPC appear compliant per CSPM (last scan 11 days ago). An engineer added a temporary debug rule 8 days ago opening port 8080 to 0.0.0.0/0 for troubleshooting.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan): Debug firewall rule added between 14-day scan cycles. Rule never removed after troubleshooting concluded. Admin API port 8080 exposed to internet for 8 days.
detection_signal: CSPM last scan: 11 days ago (clean). Firewall rule added 8 days ago: allow-debug-8080, allow-all, port 8080 — not in CSPM cache.
ground_truth: Firewall rule allow-debug-8080 added by engineer for debugging. Port 8080 is the microservice admin API with internal management endpoints. Exposed to internet for 8 days without detection.
remediation_impact: Admin API endpoints accessible from internet for 8+ days. Admin API includes tenant management operations.

scenario: ECR image scan: CVE-2024-23827 marked as DISPUTED/WITHDRAWN — scanner clears the finding and removes the component from watch list. Three days later CVE-2024-28849 for the same follow-redirects version is published.
why_misclassified: EC-46 (related CVE outside watch window): When CVE withdrawn, scanner removes follow-redirects 1.15.4 from active watch. New CVE-2024-28849 (HIGH, SSRF in follow-redirects 1.x) published after the scan — caught in the 3-day gap between CVE publication and next scan cycle.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-23827: WITHDRAWN — cleared. follow-redirects 1.15.4 removed from watchlist. CVE-2024-28849: not yet in scanner feed.
ground_truth: follow-redirects 1.15.4 has CVE-2024-28849 (SSRF, HIGH, published 3 days after scan). Component cleared from watchlist due to prior CVE withdrawal. 3-day feed lag means new CVE missed.
remediation_impact: SSRF in HTTP redirect library used by Lambda integration functions. New vulnerability missed due to CVE withdrawal clearing component from active monitoring.

scenario: EKS pod saas-parser-svc uses distroless/python3.11. Scanner detects CVE-2023-44271 in Pillow (AV:N, uncontrolled resource consumption) and applies EC-29 distroless downgrade pattern, reducing to LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-29 (distroless pattern over-applied): CVE-2023-44271 is AV:N with no shell requirement — it's a resource exhaustion attack via crafted PNG uploads to the web API. Distroless provides no protection for application-layer CVEs that execute through the application code path.
detection_signal: Pillow CVE-2023-44271 downgraded LOW — distroless image detected. AV:N exploitability assumed reduced.
ground_truth: saas-parser-svc accepts image uploads from customers. CVE-2023-44271 exploitable by uploading a crafted PNG that causes Pillow to consume excessive memory. No shell needed. Application-layer vulnerability unaffected by distroless.
remediation_impact: DoS vulnerability in customer-facing image parsing service. Crafted PNG upload can cause OOM, crashing the parser pod and impacting all tenants sharing the node.

scenario: Azure PIM eligible role 'Owner on saas-prod' activated 31 times in 45 days. CSPM does not flag because PIM eligible roles are in the approved break-glass list. Historical rate: 2 activations per quarter.
why_misclassified: EC-28 (break-glass frequency anomaly): Break-glass exemption correctly applies to PIM eligible roles. However, 31 activations in 45 days (vs. 2/quarter baseline) is 31x above normal. No anomaly detection on exempted PIM activation frequency.
detection_signal: PIM Owner activation: 31 times in 45 days. Role in break-glass exemption list — no finding.
ground_truth: Normal rate: ~8/year. Current: 31/45 days = 250/year equivalent. 28 of 31 activations by same AAD user correlating with large S3-equivalent Azure Blob operations during off-hours. Insider threat or compromised admin account pattern.
remediation_impact: Potential insider threat using break-glass elevation to exfiltrate customer data. PIM activation frequency anomaly detection required.

scenario: GKE cluster saas-prod has Binary Authorization enabled (CSPM compliant). However, the policy evaluationMode was switched to DRYRUN_AUDIT_LOG_ONLY during an upgrade 2 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-35 (admission enforcement gap): CSPM checks binaryAuthorization.enabled=true but not the evaluationMode. Dry-run mode logs violations without blocking. Three unsigned SaaS microservice images deployed in the past week.
detection_signal: GKE: binaryAuthorization.enabled=true. CSPM: compliant. evaluationMode not inspected.
ground_truth: evaluationMode=DRYRUN_AUDIT_LOG_ONLY. Policy violations logged in Cloud Audit Logs but deployments not blocked. 3 unsigned images deployed without policy enforcement.
remediation_impact: Supply chain integrity enforcement disabled. Unsigned images in production with no blocking enforcement.

scenario: AWS Security Hub reports MEDIUM for 'RDS instance uses default parameter group' on saas-customer-db. Same finding on Azure would be HIGH, on GCP would be HIGH.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): Security Hub rates default parameter group as MEDIUM, assuming it's a best-practice gap. For a multi-tenant SaaS production database, default PostgreSQL parameter group means query logging, slow query logging, and connection logging are all disabled — a real SOC 2 audit logging gap.
detection_signal: Security Hub: RDS saas-customer-db uses default parameter group — MEDIUM
ground_truth: Default parameter group disables log_statement, log_min_duration_statement, and log_connections. Without these, SQL injection attempts and unauthorized data access queries go unlogged. SOC 2 CC7.2 audit logging not satisfied. Real HIGH for multi-tenant production DB.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM SLA (30 days) for an active audit logging gap on a multi-tenant production database. Unauthorized queries could go undetected for 30 days.

scenario: API Gateway auth-api-prod shows 34,000 failed authentication attempts in 30 minutes. GuardDuty flags as brute force attack against customer-facing authentication endpoint. Security team escalates for incident response.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated + normal OAuth pattern): High auth failure rates are expected in multi-tenant SaaS OAuth flows. Failed attempts originate from known OAuth client IPs during token refresh storms when access tokens expire simultaneously after a deployment. Not brute force.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/MaliciousIPCaller — 34,000 HTTP 401s in 30 min on auth-api-prod
ground_truth: Token expiry storm: deployment at 14:00 UTC caused simultaneous token expiration for 8,400 clients. Each client retries with expired token before discovering new token required. Pattern matches post-deployment spikes in past 12 deployments.
remediation_impact: Blocking authentication endpoint during OAuth token refresh storm would lock out all 8,400 customers simultaneously.

scenario: Kubernetes network policy scanner flags EKS cluster saas-prod as having insufficient namespace isolation — pods in customer-tenant-A namespace can reach customer-tenant-B namespace via service DNS. Flagged as multi-tenant lateral movement risk.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC-bounded namespace isolation): Service mesh (Istio) enforces AuthorizationPolicy that restricts inter-namespace communication to only the platform's internal service bus. Despite DNS resolution capability, all actual HTTP connections require mTLS certificate from the requesting namespace's service account.
detection_signal: Network policy analysis: customer-tenant-* namespaces have no NetworkPolicy blocking inter-namespace DNS. Lateral movement path identified.
ground_truth: Istio AuthorizationPolicy deny-cross-tenant enforces source namespace restrictions. DNS resolution ≠ connectivity. mTLS required for all service-to-service calls. No cross-tenant data accessible even if DNS resolves.
remediation_impact: Adding NetworkPolicy to block inter-namespace DNS would break the platform service discovery mechanism that coordinates tenant operations.

scenario: IAM role saas-cicd-deploy-role has iam:PassRole, ec2:*, ecs:*, s3:*, and ecr:* permissions across production. Scanner flags CRITICAL for deployment role with broad permissions that could be used for privilege escalation.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (deployment automation — not overprivilege): Broad IAM role is intentional for the deployment automation pipeline. Role is assumed only by GitHub Actions OIDC federation with condition StringEquals token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud sts.amazonaws.com AND StringLike repo:saas-org/platform:*. Not assumable by humans.
detection_signal: IAM role saas-cicd-deploy-role: iam:PassRole, ec2:*, s3:* on Resource:*. CRITICAL overpermission.
ground_truth: Role assumable only via OIDC federation from saas-org/platform GitHub repo. No human IAM users have AssumeRole permission. iam:PassRole scoped to deployment-specific role ARNs via condition. Permission boundary limits deployment scope.
remediation_impact: Restricting deployment role would break the CI/CD pipeline for 380 microservices, halting all production deployments.

scenario: CSPM flags Lambda function saas-api-gateway-v2 for having rate limiting disabled — scanner detects no throttling configuration on the API Gateway stage. Rate limiting is a SOC 2 availability control requirement.
why_misclassified: EC-03 (disabled feature actually controlled elsewhere): Rate limiting is implemented via LaunchDarkly feature flag system that applies per-tenant rate limits dynamically. The API Gateway throttle is intentionally disabled to allow the application-layer rate limiter (more granular) to control traffic.
detection_signal: API Gateway saas-api-prod stage: ThrottlingBurstLimit=0, ThrottlingRateLimit=0 (no throttling configured)
ground_truth: Application-layer rate limiter in saas-api-gateway-v2 Lambda implements per-tenant, per-endpoint rate limits via Redis token bucket algorithm. Limits configurable per customer plan. API Gateway throttle disabled to prevent double-limiting.
remediation_impact: Enabling API Gateway throttle would apply a single global limit across all tenants, breaking premium tier customers' higher rate limits.

scenario: CSPM flags developer sandbox account 987654321012 for multiple HIGH misconfigurations: public S3 buckets, open security groups, no MFA for IAM users. Finding aggregated as HIGH risk environment.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (intentionally permissive sandbox): Sandbox account is for developer experimentation per documented policy. No customer data, no production access, isolated VPC with no peering to production. Permissive configurations are intentional to enable rapid prototyping without security overhead.
detection_signal: Sandbox account: 12 HIGH findings including public S3, open SGs, no MFA. Account 987654321012.
ground_truth: Account tagged Purpose=developer-sandbox, DataClassification=none. SCPs block production account access. No real data. AWS Control Tower guardrail prevents any IAM trust relationships to production accounts.
remediation_impact: Hardening sandbox accounts to production standards defeats the purpose of developer sandboxes, slowing feature development velocity.

scenario: API Gateway endpoint /webhooks/receive allows POST from 0.0.0.0/0. Scanner flags HIGH for unauthenticated open ingress endpoint that could receive arbitrary payloads.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded with HMAC): Webhook endpoint is intentionally public to receive third-party platform webhooks (GitHub, Slack, Stripe). All payloads verified via HMAC-SHA256 signature validation before processing. Invalid signatures rejected with 401.
detection_signal: API Gateway: POST /webhooks/receive — no API key, no IAM auth, public endpoint from 0.0.0.0/0
ground_truth: Webhook receiver validates X-Signature-256 HMAC header against registered webhook secrets. Payload processing only occurs after signature verification. Unsigned requests rejected before any business logic executed.
